title: Permission hide rule also hides camera/mic/screen/location sharing indicators and blocked-permission icons
problem: Both configs ship `#identity-permission-box { display: none !important; }` with the comment "Only hides permission items". In Firefox 160 that box holds more than the »permissions granted« icon. It also holds the live sharing indicators (camera, microphone, screen, geolocation, XR, serial), which Firefox paints red, and every blocked-permission icon (pop-ups, autoplay, camera/mic blocked, …). With Cascade, a site that is using your camera, microphone or screen shows nothing in the URL bar. The only remaining sign is the small pulsing overlay on a tab that is not selected. Firefox already hides the box when it has nothing to show (identity-block.css:240-242), so the Cascade rule can only remove information. This is a privacy regression for a daily driver, in Nova and Proton and in both configs.
evidence: browser.xhtml:6498-6546: `<box id="identity-permission-box" …>` contains `<image id="permissions-granted-icon"/>` (6503), `<image class="sharing-icon" id="webrtc-sharing-icon"/>` plus the geo/xr/serial sharing icons (6505-6508) and `<box id="blocked-permissions-container">` (6510). identity-block.css:240-248 `#identity-permission-box { display: none; }` and `#identity-permission-box[open="true"], #identity-permission-box[hasPermissions], #identity-permission-box[hasSharingIcon] { display: flex; }`. identity-block.css:251-282: `#webrtc-sharing-icon[sharing="camera"] {…}` and `#webrtc-sharing-icon[sharing]:not([paused]) { fill: var(--icon-color-critical); }`. browser-sitePermissionPanel.js:198-240 sets `icon.setAttribute("showing", "true")` on blocked permissions and blocked pop-ups and toggles [hasPermissions]; :308-357 toggles [hasSharingIcon]. Harness run on HEAD (dark): after setting hasSharingIcon and webrtc-sharing-icon[sharing=camera], getComputedStyle(#identity-permission-box).display is "none" and no indicator shows (scratchpad/agents/urlbar/run2/sharing-crop.png). With the fix below: display "flex", #permissions-granted-icon "none", red camera icon visible (run3/sharing-crop.png).

title: `#urlbar *` outline:none removes every keyboard focus and selection ring in the URL bar and its results
problem:
`#urlbar, #urlbar * { outline: none !important; box-shadow: none !important; }` is user !important, so it beats every Firefox focus indicator inside #urlbar. In 160 the results view is a light-DOM child of #urlbar, so the rule reaches it too. The effects:
- Tab from the URL bar lands on the bookmark star (the page-actions tab stop) with no visible focus.
- The trust/identity, zoom and revert buttons lose their rings the same way.
- In the results, Tab moves the keyboard selection onto a row's »⋯« result-menu button, onto action buttons (»Clear recent history«, tab-switch actions) and onto tip buttons. Their only selection indicator is an outline, so the user cannot tell whether Enter opens the row or the button.
Only the search-engine switcher keeps a ring, because it lives in moz-button's shadow DOM, and that ring is Firefox blue, not the accent. For a »keyboard centered« theme this is the biggest functional regression in the URL bar. It affects Nova and Proton alike.
evidence: UrlbarInputBase.mjs:171-238: the markup (including `<div class="urlbarView" popover="manual">`) is appended into the moz-urlbar with no shadow root, so `#urlbar *` matches rows and buttons. urlbar.css:981-987 `.urlbar-page-action { … &:focus-visible { outline: var(--focus-outline); outline-offset: var(--focus-outline-inset); } }`. identity-block.css:78-99 `.identity-box-button, #trust-icon-container, #tracking-protection-icon-container { … &:focus-visible { outline: var(--focus-outline); … } }`. view-nova.css:476-487 `.urlbarView-button { &[selected] { outline: var(--focus-outline); outline-color: var(--urlbarview-text-color-selected); … } }`. view-nova.css:1214-1222 `.urlbarView-action-btn … &[selected], &:hover:active { outline: var(--focus-outline); }`; view-proton.css has the same rules. Harness on HEAD: Tab from the URL bar gives activeElement #star-button-box, :focus-visible true, outline "none" (run2/tab-crop.png shows no ring). A result-menu button selected via gURLBar.view.selectBy(1,{userPressedTab:true}) has outlineStyle "none" (run2/menubtn-crop.png). Fixed copy: star outline "solid 2px rgb(120,111,166)", action button "solid 2px rgb(120,111,166)", »⋯« button gets the white selected ring (run3/tab-crop.png, action-crop.png, menubtn-crop.png). The decorations Cascade wanted gone are already invisible because --toolbar-field-border-color and --toolbar-field-border-color-focus are transparent (cascade-colours.css:137-138). The exception is the shadow around the open view (urlbar.css:332 and :613 `box-shadow: var(--urlbar-background-box-shadow-open)`). --focus-outline is a shorthand resolved on :root (tokens-shared.css:368 `--focus-outline: var(--focus-outline-width) solid var(--focus-outline-color);`). Overriding only --focus-outline-color on a descendant therefore does not change `outline: var(--focus-outline)`; Firefox documents the same trap at browser-shared.css:873-875. The same applies to cascade-panels.css:34, so --focus-outline-color on panel/menupopup does not recolour panel focus rings.

title: Result-row highlight rule gives square corners and highlights non-selectable rows on hover
problem: Cascade paints `.urlbarView-row:hover > .urlbarView-row-inner, .urlbarView-row[selected] > .urlbarView-row-inner` in the selection colour. In 160 (Nova and Proton) Firefox paints hover and selection on the row itself, with rounded corners, clipped to the gutter. Cascade's inner box has no radius, so selected and hovered results are hard-edged rectangles, unlike every other box in the theme. The Cascade hover also lacks Firefox's [row-selectable] guard. Hovering the non-selectable »Press tab to select: Clear recent history« actions row (or a tip) therefore highlights it like a selected result: its chip, which has the same colour, disappears into it, and two rows look selected. cascade-colours.css:151-152 already map --urlbarview-background-color-hover/selected to the same colour, so the rule is redundant.
evidence: view-nova.css:154-180: `.urlbarView-row { … padding: var(--urlbarview-row-gutter); border-radius: var(--urlbarview-row-border-radius); background-clip: content-box; … &[menu-trigger], &[row-selectable]:not([selected]):hover { background-color: var(--urlbarview-background-color-hover); … } &[selected] { background-color: var(--urlbarview-background-color-selected); … } }`. view-proton.css:163-180 is the same with a transparent-border gutter. Harness probe on HEAD: selected row bg rgb(30,32,33), radius 8px; its .urlbarView-row-inner bg rgb(30,32,33), radius 0px. Zooms agents/urlbar/sel.png (Nova) and sel-novaoff.png show square corners. Hovering the dynamicType="actions" row gives row-selectable=false, row bg transparent, inner bg rgb(30,32,33) (run6/crop.png). With the rule deleted: rounded selection, and the actions row is not highlighted (run3/open-crop.png, run5/lo.png, run5/no.png).
fix: Delete cascade-nav-bar.css:30-36. The same colour already comes from the tokens at cascade-colours.css:151-152 and Firefox's own row rules.

title: URL bar text-selection colours (--lwt-toolbar-field-highlight*) never apply with the default theme
problem: Cascade sets --lwt-toolbar-field-highlight and --lwt-toolbar-field-highlight-text to give selected URL text the palette colours. Firefox reads them only inside `:root[lwtheme]`. Cascade follows prefers-color-scheme, so its users run the default »System theme — auto«, which has no [lwtheme]. Selecting the URL (Ctrl+L, F6, double-click) therefore shows system Highlight blue with white text, off-palette in both schemes and in every integration. The variables only take effect with a built-in Dark/Light theme or an AMO theme.
evidence: urlbar.css:535-546: `:root[lwtheme] { .urlbar-input::selection, .searchbar-textbox::selection { background-color: var(--lwt-toolbar-field-highlight, Highlight); color: var(--lwt-toolbar-field-highlight-text, HighlightText); } .urlbar-input:not(:focus)::selection, … }`. Harness probe: documentElement lwtheme = null, theme-effective-id = "default-theme@mozilla.org"; shots/before/urlbar-focus.png shows the blue selection. With the fix: inverted background and highlight-coloured text in dark, light and Nova off (agents/urlbar/run3/select-crop.png, run5/ls.png, run5/ns.png).

title: Hiding #pageActionButton makes the bookmark star and extension page actions vanish in windows ≤680px
problem: Firefox already hides the »⋯« page-actions button. It shows it only in windows ≤680px wide, as the overflow target for the bookmark star and extension page-action buttons when more than one page action exists. Any extension with a page_action triggers this, for example Multi-Account Containers' »Always open in…«. In that state Firefox hides the star and the extension buttons, and Cascade hides the button that replaces them. A half-screen window on a 1366px display, or a tiled window, loses the star and every extension page action, with no way to reach them from the URL bar. In every other case the rule does nothing.
evidence: urlbar.css:749-768: `/* The page actions menu is hidden by default, it is only shown in small windows as the overflow target of multiple page action buttons */ #pageActionButton { display: none; } @media (max-width: 680px) { #pageActionSeparator, #pageActionButton[multiple-children] ~ .urlbar-page-action { display: none; } #pageActionButton[multiple-children] { display: revert; } }`. browser-pageActions.js:221-225: `toggleAttribute("multiple-children", PageActions.actions.length > 1)`; the only built-in action is the bookmark (PageActions.sys.mjs:1189-1203). browser.xhtml:6680-6692: #star-button-box follows #pageActionButton. Harness at 660px with [multiple-children] set: HEAD gives pageActionButton "none" and star-button-box "none"; with the rule removed, pageActionButton is "flex" (agents/urlbar/run4/).
fix: Delete `#pageActionButton { display: none !important; }` from both config files. Firefox's own rule already hides the button whenever it is not needed.

title: Nav-bar dimming fades keyboard-focused buttons, their focus ring, badges and attention states
problem:
The rule is `#nav-bar .toolbarbutton-1:not(:hover, [open], [checked], [disabled]) > :is(.toolbarbutton-icon, .toolbarbutton-badge-stack) { opacity: var(--uc-inactive-opacity) }`. It has three problems:
(a) Keyboard focus is not an exception. Firefox draws the toolbar-button focus ring as an outline on that same icon/badge-stack, so a button reached with Tab or the arrow keys keeps a 65%-opacity ring and a dimmed icon, while mouse hover lights it up.
(b) The badge label is a child of .toolbarbutton-badge-stack, so badges are dimmed too: the app-menu »update available / restart« dot, extension unread counts, the account badge.
(c) Attention states are dimmed: the unified-extensions attention dot (a background-image on the icon), and the downloads button's progress ring, success arrow and info/warning/severe badges (for example a blocked dangerous download). Firefox moves the downloads button's children into the badge stack, so they all fade.
evidence: toolbarbuttons.css:218-236: `> .toolbarbutton-icon, > .toolbarbutton-text, > .toolbarbutton-badge-stack { … outline: var(--toolbarbutton-outline); } &:focus-visible { outline: none; > .toolbarbutton-icon, > .toolbarbutton-text, > .toolbarbutton-badge-stack { outline: var(--focus-outline); … } }`. toolbarbutton.js:57-64: the badged fragment is `<stack class="toolbarbutton-badge-stack"><image class="toolbarbutton-icon"/><html:label class="toolbarbutton-badge"/></stack>`; :133-150 move the button's children (downloads indicator, progress and animation boxes) into the stack. unified-extensions.css:100-111: `#unified-extensions-button[attention] > .toolbarbutton-icon { background-image: radial-gradient(…) }`. downloads/indicator.css:14-24, 71-83, 89-113: `#downloads-button[progress] …` and `[attention="success|info|warning|severe"] > .toolbarbutton-badge-stack > …`. panelUI-shared.css:65-110: `#PanelUI-menu-button[badge-status] > .toolbarbutton-badge-stack > .toolbarbutton-badge`. Disabled buttons are already dimmed on the button itself (toolbarbuttons.css:133-134 `&[disabled] { opacity: var(--toolbarbutton-opacity-disabled) }`), so the [disabled] exception is correct. Harness on HEAD: two shift+Tab from the URL bar focus #sidebar-button with :focus-visible, icon outline "solid 2px" and opacity 0.65 (agents/urlbar/run2/st-crop.png). The badge stack with [badge-status=update-available] is at 0.65, and so is the unified-extensions icon with [attention]. Fixed copy: focused icon 1, badge 1, attention icon 1 once the 150ms transition ends.

title: Ayu integration: selected result invisible in dark, URL bar text unreadable in light
problem: The URL bar uses --uc-highlight-colour as its background and --uc-base-colour for the selected and hovered result. Ayu dark sets both to #1f2430, so the selected result row has exactly the view's background, and arrow-key navigation through results is invisible. Ayu light defines a near-black base (#0a0e14), a yellow highlight (#e6b450) and grey text (#b3b1ad). The URL bar text on its background is 1.12:1, which is unreadable: a yellow field with grey text on a black toolbar.
evidence: The mapping in ayu.css:87-110 is identical to cascade-colours.css:133-156: `--toolbar-field-background-color: var(--uc-urlbar-colour)` (the highlight colour, via the :where default at ayu.css:52-55) and `--urlbarview-background-color-selected: var(--uc-urlbar-selection-colour)` (the base colour). Firefox paints the view with urlbar.css:609 `.urlbarView-background { background-color: var(--urlbar-background-color-focus) }`, where urlbar.tokens.css:14 sets `--urlbar-background-color-focus: var(--toolbar-field-background-color-focus)`, and paints the selected row with view-nova.css:177-180. Computed WCAG ratios: Ayu dark, selected vs view 1.00. Ayu light, text on URL bar 1.12, muted on URL bar 3.92.
fix: In the Ayu dark block, give the highlight its own shade, e.g. `--uc-highlight-colour: #2a3040;` (selected vs view 1.18 like the default theme; text 9.2:1; accent 7.5:1). In the light block, use an actual light Ayu palette, e.g. `--uc-base-colour: #fafafa; --uc-highlight-colour: #e7e8e9; --uc-inverted-colour: #5c6166; --uc-muted-colour: #62666b; --uc-identity-colour-purple: #7c4fb0;`. That gives text 5.1:1, muted 4.7:1, and URL text 5.0:1 after the 70% accent mix proposed in the URL-colour finding.

title: Result URLs fail contrast (2.9:1) while badges, links and tip buttons stay Firefox blue: map --link-color instead
problem: `.urlbarView-url { color: var(--uc-accent-colour) !important; }` paints the small (0.85em) result URLs in the raw accent. That is 2.88:1 on the dark results background (#786fa6 on #2e3133) and 4.19:1 in light, below WCAG AA's 4.5:1, for the text that shows which domain a result really goes to. Integrations are similar: nord dark 2.60, nord light 2.10, rose-pine light 3.16, gruvbox ~3.8. Meanwhile everything Firefox colours with --link-color in the view keeps Firefox's system blue: the bookmark/history/tab badges on favicons, tab-to-search icons, explanation text, »Learn more« links. Tip and primary buttons use --color-accent-primary, also blue. And because the rule is !important on the element, the URL keeps the accent even in the selected row, where Firefox switches it to the row's text colour. The same rule is copied in all 8 integration files.
evidence: view-nova.css:831-841: `.urlbarView-url, .urlbarView-explanation { font-size: var(--urlbarview-small-font-size); … .urlbarView-row:not([selected]) & { color: var(--link-color); } }`. view-nova.css:356-361: `.urlbarView-type-icon { … .urlbarView-row:not([selected]) & { fill: var(--link-color); } }`. view-nova.css:339-344: tab-to-search icon `color: var(--link-color)`. view-nova.css:566-580: labelled [selected]/[primary] buttons use `background-color: var(--color-accent-primary)` and `color: var(--button-text-color-primary)`. --link-color is a :root token (tokens-shared.css:428; tokens-platform.css:49 `--link-color: LinkText`). Harness on HEAD: --link-color on .urlbarView is "LinkText", the type-icon fill is rgb(53,132,228) (blue badges in agents/urlbar/badges.png), the URL is rgb(120,111,166). Fixed copy: badges and URLs use the mixed accent (run3/open-crop.png, run5/lo.png). --urlbarview-text-color-secondary also leaks Nova's violet tints `light-dark(#3e315f, #e7e1f8)` (urlbarview.tokens.css:179) into row descriptions and the »Press tab to select:« label.

title: URL bar token mapping is copied into 9 colour files; move it into cascade-nav-bar.css
problem: Every colour integration is a full copy of the colour mapping, including the URL bar section and `.urlbarView-url`. Each URL-bar fix in this audit would have to be repeated in 9 files: cascade-colours.css, ayu, three catppuccin, gruvbox, nord and two rose-pine. Users who copied an integration months ago keep the old mapping indefinitely. Nothing in that section depends on the palette: it only maps --uc-* variables onto Firefox tokens.
evidence: `grep -l urlbarview-background-color-selected` finds 9 files. A diff of cascade-colours.css:95-170 against integrations/ayu/ayu.css:48-125 shows identical URL bar blocks. userChrome.css imports cascade-nav-bar.css after cascade-colours.css (userChrome.css:245-254), so declarations there win over stale copies of the same origin and importance.
fix:
1. Move the `--uc-urlbar-colour` and `--uc-urlbar-selection-colour` defaults (cascade-colours.css:98-101) into the `:where(:root)` block of cascade-nav-bar.css.
2. Move the »URL bar« and »URL bar results« token block (cascade-colours.css:132-156) into a `:root { … }` block in cascade-nav-bar.css, next to the `.urlbar` block from the focus-ring and link-colour findings.
3. Delete those lines and `.urlbarView-url` from cascade-colours.css and every integration, so integrations only carry the palette.
Old integration copies then do no harm, because the include loaded later overrides them.

title: Keyboard-selected result relies on a 1.03–1.34:1 background change; add an accent marker
problem: The selected result is marked only by swapping --uc-urlbar-colour for --uc-urlbar-selection-colour. Measured contrast between the two: default dark 1.25, light 1.34; catppuccin 1.07–1.17; rose-pine 1.07–1.10; gruvbox light 1.03; Ayu dark 1.00. In a keyboard-first theme the selected row is the main navigation cue in the URL bar, and in several palettes it is barely visible (gruvbox light: run7/gh.png). The active tab already has an accent line; results could use the same visual language.
evidence: view-nova.css:154-180: the row background on [selected] is the only selection cue. Harness: agents/urlbar/run7/both.png (gruvbox light; left HEAD, right with the marker) and run7/gf-zoom.png.

title: 1px app-menu button hack leaves an invisible focus target and a floating, dimmed update badge
problem: The keyboard config squeezes #PanelUI-menu-button to a 1px icon with a 9px hit area. The button stays in the toolbar's arrow-key navigation, so keyboard users land on an invisible button. When Firefox badges it (update available or restart needed, add-on alert, sign in to sync again, failed login), the 12px badge floats over the edge of the tab bar with no icon. It is also at 65% opacity because of the nav-bar dimming, so an update that needs a restart is easy to miss.
evidence: browser.xhtml:6798-6803: `<toolbarbutton id="PanelUI-menu-button" class="toolbarbutton-1" … badged="true"`. panelUI-shared.css:65-110: badge styles, including `margin: -5px 0 0 !important; margin-inline-end: -3px !important`. browser-toolbarKeyNav.js:38-50: every toolbarbutton is arrow-navigable. Harness on HEAD: menu button 9×44px, badge 12×12 at x 482-494, stack opacity 0.65 (agents/urlbar/run2/sharing-crop.png). Fixed copy with the update badge: button 40px wide, badge opacity 1 (run3/sharing-crop.png).

title: No hover/pressed feedback on URL bar boxes (engine switcher, site chips, zoom, search-mode close)
problem: --urlbar-box-background-color and its -hover, -active and -focus variants all map to --uc-urlbar-selection-colour. Boxes that already have that background therefore show no change on hover or press: the search engine switcher, the »Firefox«/extension/»Not Secure« chips, the zoom »110%« button, the »Switch to tab:« label and the search-mode close ×.
evidence: urlbar.css:1336-1346: `.searchmode-switcher { --button-background-color-muted: var(--urlbar-box-background-color); --button-background-color-muted-hover: var(--urlbar-box-background-color-hover); --button-background-color-muted-active: var(--urlbar-box-background-color-active); … }`. identity-block.css:123-131: chip hover/active. urlbar.css:1162-1180: zoom button hover/active. urlbar.css:817-842: `.searchmode-switcher-close { … &:hover { background-color: var(--urlbar-box-background-color-hover); … } }`. In both schemes the URL bar colour lies between the selection colour and the text colour, so a small mix toward the text colour lands on the URL bar colour and the box blends in. The step has to overshoot it.

title: Hiding #identity-box.extensionPage removes the chip that names the extension owning the page
problem: On moz-extension:// pages Firefox 160 deliberately keeps the identity chip (extension icon and name), even with the trust panel on. It is the anti-spoofing cue that tells you a page belongs to an add-on, and which one. The Cascade rule also hides that page's permission icons and notification (doorhanger) anchors. With it, only the generic trust shield remains.
evidence: identity-block.css:336-339: `/* Keep displaying the moz-extension or chrome UI chicklet */ #identity-box[pageproxystate="valid"]:not(.chromeUI, .extensionPage) > #identity-icon-box { display: none; }`. identity-block.css:212: `#identity-box[pageproxystate="valid"].extensionPage #identity-icon { … extension.svg }`. browser.xhtml:6481-6546: #identity-box contains #identity-permission-box and #notification-popup-box.
fix:
Make it opt-in, with a comment that says what it costs:
```css
/* Hides the extension name chip on extension pages (and their
   permission icons) */
/* #identity-box.extensionPage { display: none !important; } */
```
Or hide only the text and keep the icon, permissions and anchors: `#identity-box.extensionPage #identity-icon-label { display: none !important; }`.

title: Config comments for the shield/padlock target elements that Firefox 160 no longer shows
problem: The trust panel is on by default in 160, so the shield/padlock is #trust-icon-container. #tracking-protection-icon-container is always display:none, so uncommenting »Disables the Tracking Protection Shield« does nothing. »#identity-box … Hides encryption AND permission items« no longer hides any encryption indicator on normal pages. It hides permission icons and the notification anchors that reopen dismissed camera or password prompts.
evidence: firefox.js:146: `pref("browser.urlbar.trustPanel.featureGate", true);`. identity-block.css:324-339: `@media -moz-pref("browser.urlbar.trustPanel.featureGate") { … #tracking-protection-icon-container { display: none; } … #identity-box[pageproxystate="valid"]:not(.chromeUI, .extensionPage) > #identity-icon-box { display: none; } #trust-icon-container { … } }`. browser.xhtml:6443-6464: #trust-icon-container holds the icon, the »Not Secure« label and the tracker-count wrappers.

title: Mouse config silently hides the container label; both configs hide the Go arrow everywhere
problem: The keyboard config shows the coloured container chip (e.g. »Work«) in the URL bar. The mouse config hides all of #userContext-icons, label and icon, with no knob. Swapping configs therefore removes the only container indicator apart from the 1px tab line. Both configs also hide `.urlbar-go-button` with an unscoped selector. The Go arrow matters most to mouse users, and the rule also removes it from the separate search bar (#searchbar-new uses the same markup and shows its Go arrow while typing).
evidence: browser.xhtml:6624-6628: `<hbox id="userContext-icons" hidden="true" role="button"><label id="userContext-label"/><image id="userContext-indicator"/></hbox>`. urlbar.css:742-746: Firefox already hides #userContext-label below 770px. urlbar.css:177-178: `.urlbar:not([usertyping]) > .urlbar-input-container > .urlbar-go-button, .urlbar:not(#searchbar-new, [focused]) > .urlbar-input-container > .urlbar-go-button { display: none; }`. UrlbarInputBase.mjs:222-225: the go button is part of every moz-urlbar. Harness shots/before/containers.png shows the chip with the keyboard config.
fix:
Make the two configs agree and keep the options commented:
- In cascade-config-mouse.css, keep the icon and drop only the label: `#userContext-label { display: none !important; }`.
- In cascade-config-mouse.css, make the Go-arrow rule optional: `/* #urlbar .urlbar-go-button { display: none !important; } */`.
- In cascade-config.css, scope it to the address bar: `#urlbar .urlbar-go-button { display: none !important; }`.

title: --button-border-radius on #urlbar does not reach the »Switch to Tab« chips its comment names
problem: The comment says the rule gives the engine switcher and »Switch to Tab« the radius of the other boxes. The chips and the action buttons (»Clear recent history«) use --urlbar-border-radius (8px), so they stay rounder than the switcher, the identity chips and the page-action hovers (4px). Only the switcher and the labelled tip buttons follow --button-border-radius.
evidence: view-nova.css:730-733: `/* Chiclet style */ .urlbarView-row:is([type="switchtab"], [type="remotetab"], [type="clipboard"]) & { border: 1px solid currentColor; border-radius: var(--urlbar-border-radius);`. view-nova.css:1199-1203: `.urlbarView-action-btn { … border-radius: var(--urlbar-border-radius);`. view-proton.css:780 is the same. view-nova.css:549-552: labelled buttons use `border-radius: var(--button-border-radius)`. shots/before/urlbar-open.png: chips about 8px against the switcher's 4px.

title: Keyboard focus rings of every button inside the URL bar are removed by `#urlbar *`
problem: chrome/includes/cascade-nav-bar.css:20-24 sets `outline: none !important` on `#urlbar, #urlbar *`. Firefox draws the keyboard focus indicator of everything inside the URL bar as an outline: the site-info/trust button, tracking protection, identity box, page action buttons (star, reader view, translations), zoom, the revert button, plus the selected action buttons and tip links in the results list. If you move into the URL bar with the toolbar keyboard navigation (Shift+Tab, then the arrow keys), focus lands on these buttons with nothing visible on screen. That hits hardest in a theme sold as keyboard centered. The URL bar outline the rule was written for is already invisible, because cascade-colours.css:91-92 sets `--toolbar-field-border-color(-focus): transparent`. Happens in both Nova and Proton.
evidence: Firefox 160: identity-block/identity-block.css:77-99 `.identity-box-button, #trust-icon-container, #tracking-protection-icon-container { ... &:focus-visible { outline: var(--focus-outline); ...} }`; urlbar.css:981-987 `.urlbar-page-action { &:focus-visible { outline: var(--focus-outline);` ; urlbar.css:1190-1193 (zoom) and 1050-1052 (`#urlbar-revert-button:focus-visible`); urlbar/view-nova.css:1219-1221 `&[selected], &:hover:active { outline: var(--focus-outline); }` (result action buttons), view-nova.css:476-477 and 993-996 (`> a[selected] { outline: var(--focus-outline)`). title: The selected tab and tab group labels lose their keyboard focus ring

Harness probe: `ariaFocusedItem = selectedTab` + setFocus(FLAG_BYKEY) → `tablist-has-focus` true, class `tablist-keyboard-focus` true, computed outline-style `none` on the selected tab's .tab-background (probe-selected-tab-focus.png shows no ring). The selected-tab half is real, and worse than described. Plain Left/Right in the tab strip changes the selected tab (advanceSelectedItem), so keyboard focus nearly always sits on the selected tab. The ring is therefore missing in almost every case, and appears only when you use Ctrl+arrow. This is not gated: it hits horizontal and vertical tabs, Nova on and off.

The tab group label half is wrong. In Firefox 160 the label is wrapped as `.tab-group-label-container > .tab-group-label-hover-highlight > .tab-group-label`. Cascade's child-combinator selector `.tab-group-label-container > .tab-group-label` (cascade-tabs.css:120) matches nothing, so `outline: none` never applies and the keyboard-focused group label keeps Firefox's ring. As a side effect, the whole Cascade label rule (radius, width, colours) is dead code in FF160, which is a separate bug for the tabs scope.

The label part keeps the dead `.tab-group-label-container > .tab-group-label` selector, so it does nothing, and nothing needs fixing there today.
refute.better_fix: Apply only the selected-tab change. If the maintainer revives the label rule with a selector that matches FF160, such as `.tab-group-label-container .tab-group-label` or `tab-group > .tab-group-label-container .tab-group-label`, then either drop `outline: none` from it or scope it as `.tab-group-label-container .tab-group-label:not(#tabbrowser-tabs[tablist-has-focus] .tablist-keyboard-focus) { outline: none !important; }`. Without that, the revived rule would start removing the label's focus ring.

Tab group label: not real today. The whole cascade-tabs.css:119-127 rule is dead (border-radius, width and colours too), so Firefox's label ring at tabs.css:2328-2331 is still drawn. title: Focus rings use the system accent (blue) or Firefox violet, never Cascade's accent; `--focus-outline-color` is only set inside panels

The rings clash with every palette (catppuccin, gruvbox, rose pine…), and their contrast against the palette's base/highlight is never controlled. A blue ring on gruvbox light, for example, is unrelated to the palette.

That is an internal inconsistency in a theme that otherwise derives everything from the palette (tab line, toolbar separator, URLs). Setting it once on :root under `not (forced-colors)` reaches every chrome ring, because no closer ancestor redefines it, and it keeps the high-contrast `var(--text-color)` value.

Land it with the palettes-06 dark purple change (#a098cd: 4.91:1 on highlight), or rings on the selected tab fall below 3:1 in the default dark palette. Once this exists, the panel-only `--focus-outline-color` line in cascade-panels.css becomes redundant.

fixreview.reasoning: Real. Setting the property on :root with user !important beats all author values: tokens-shared.css:369, the Proton lwtheme value at browser-colors.css:58, and the forced-colors value at :719, which the guard rightly preserves. Side effects, all consistent: the split-view active pane border (content-area.css:590-596), the splitter hovers (content-area.css:144, sidebar.css:132, tabs.css:2860), the tab drag-over line (tabs.css:74) and the group colour swatches (tabs.css:2476-2484) switch to the accent too.
fixreview.fix_notes: The mechanism is right, but as written it lowers focus-ring contrast below 3:1 on the default dark palette (until palettes-06 lands), on both nord schemes and on the proposed ayu light. Integrations are user-replaceable files, so the ring should not depend on every palette's accent. Clamping the accent's lightness keeps the hue and is palette-independent. If the separate `--uc-accent-text-colour` (oklch clamp for `.urlbarView-url`) fix lands, reuse it: `--focus-outline-color: var(--uc-accent-text-colour) !important;`.

problem: All three files share the Latte light block. Line 37 sets `--uc-identity-colour-pink: #d20f39`, which is Latte *red* (duplicate of line 36), so 'Pink' and 'Red' containers look identical in light mode. refute.reasoning: Every factual claim holds. In all three Catppuccin files the Latte block sets --uc-identity-colour-pink: #d20f39 at line 37, the same value as red at line 36. The official Latte pink is #ea76cb (catppuccin palette.json v1.8.0, in agents/palettes/dl/ctp.json). In cascade-panels.css:30 it maps to --text-color-deemphasized, used for menu accelerators (menu.css:229), panelUI-shared.css descriptions and downloads.inc.css:270. (2) Moving the Latte highlight to surface0 lowers the mauve URL text in unselected dropdown rows from 4.09 to 3.51, because .urlbarView-url uses the accent on the highlight background. Consider blue #1e66f5 for URLs, which the guide maps to 'Links, URLs'.
refute.better_fix: Same as proposed for Mocha, Macchiato and Frappé. For Latte, use --uc-highlight-colour: #ccd0da (surface0), --uc-muted-colour: #6c6f85 (subtext0; 4.37 on base, 1.62 vs text), and --uc-identity-colour-pink: #ea76cb. title: Rosé Pine ports: the 'Blue' container is the text colour and 'Pink' is grey, and highlight/muted use the wrong spec roles
problem: Both files map `--uc-identity-colour-blue` to **text** (#e0def4 at line 9, and Dawn #575279 at line 31, the Dawn text colour) and `--uc-identity-colour-pink` to **subtle** (#908caa at line 15, Dawn #797593 at line 37). Both are neutrals, so 'Blue' (Firefox's default 'Personal' container) renders as the same off-white or ink as the tab labels, and 'Pink' ('Shopping') renders grey. Highlight is `surface` (line 20: #1f1d2e main, #2a273f moon), only 1.07:1 / 1.09:1 from base. Rosé Pine's spec assigns active tabs to `overlay`. Muted is `muted` (line 22 #6e6a86, Dawn #9893a5), which the spec calls 'low contrast foreground, comments'. It scores 3.42/3.03 on base, and Dawn 2.73 on base / 2.48 on highlight. The spec gives exactly Cascade's use case (inactive tabs, non-selected results) to `subtle`.
evidence: Official @rose-pine/palette 4.0.1 dist/css/rose-pine.css: main base #191724 surface #1f1d2e overlay #26233a muted #6e6a86 subtle #908caa text #e0def4 love #eb6f92 gold #f6c177 rose #ebbcba pine #31748f foam #9ccfd8 iris #c4a7e7; moon base #232136 overlay #393552 rose #ea9a97 pine #3e8fb0; dawn base #faf4ed overlay #f2e9e1 muted #9893a5 subtle #797593 text #575279 love #b4637a gold #ea9d34 rose #d7827e pine #286983 foam #56949f iris #907aa9. readme.md Roles: `overlay | Medium contrast background atop surface | text inputs, panels, active tabs`; `subtle | Medium contrast foreground | non-selected results, inactive tabs`; accents `pine | terminal green`, `foam | terminal blue`, `iris | ... links`. contrast.py: `identity colours equal to a text colour: ['blue']` in all four schemes; Dawn muted/base 2.73 FAIL.
fix:
Rosé Pine has six accents for Firefox's eight container colours. This mapping follows the spec's terminal roles and keeps the four default containers (blue, orange, green, pink) distinct.
Main (cascade-rose-pine.css dark):
```css
--uc-identity-colour-blue: #9ccfd8;      /* foam (terminal blue) */
--uc-identity-colour-turquoise: #9ccfd8; /* foam */
--uc-identity-colour-green: #31748f;     /* pine (terminal green) */
--uc-identity-colour-yellow: #f6c177;    /* gold */
--uc-identity-colour-orange: #f6c177;    /* gold */
--uc-identity-colour-red: #eb6f92;       /* love */
--uc-identity-colour-pink: #ebbcba;      /* rose */
--uc-identity-colour-purple: #c4a7e7;    /* iris */
--uc-base-colour: #191724;
--uc-highlight-colour: #26233a;          /* overlay */
--uc-inverted-colour: #e0def4;
--uc-muted-colour: #908caa;              /* subtle */
--uc-accent-colour: var(--uc-identity-colour-pink); /* rose, as before */
```
Moon (cascade-moon.css dark): blue #9ccfd8, turquoise #9ccfd8, green #3e8fb0, yellow #f6c177, orange #f6c177, red #eb6f92, pink #ea9a97, purple #c4a7e7, base #232136, highlight #393552, inverted #e0def4, muted #908caa, accent var(--uc-identity-colour-pink).
Dawn (light block of both files): blue #56949f, turquoise #56949f, green #286983, yellow #ea9d34, orange #ea9d34, red #b4637a, pink #d7827e, purple #907aa9, base #faf4ed, highlight #f2e9e1, inverted #575279, muted #797593, accent var(--uc-identity-colour-purple) (iris, the spec's link colour).
Results: main highlight vs base 1.16, muted 5.48; moon 1.34 / 4.86; Dawn muted 4.02. The accent now points at pink (rose) because orange no longer holds rose.

refute.reasoning: The files do what the finding says. In both Rosé Pine files the dark block maps --uc-identity-colour-blue to text #e0def4 (line 9) and pink to subtle #908caa (line 15). The Dawn block maps blue to #575279 (line 31, Dawn text) and pink to #797593 (line 37, Dawn subtle). The palette (dl/rp/package/dist/css/rose-pine.css) confirms these hexes are the neutrals. These colours matter in FF160. Its default containers are blue 'Personal', orange 'Work', green 'Banking' and pink 'Shopping' (ContextualIdentityService.sys.mjs:179-196). Cascade's `.identity-color-blue { --identity-tab-color/--identity-stroke-color … !important }` (cascade-colours.css:123-128) beats usercontext.css:14-21 (user !important over author normal). So the Personal container's tab line and URL-bar pill render in the label colour, and Shopping renders grey. FF160 also has a separate neutral 'toolbar' container colour, so a hue name rendering as a neutral is misleading. Highlight is surface: main #1f2430 vs base 1.07, moon 1.09. The readme (dl/rp/package/readme.md:150-153) gives overlay to 'active tabs' and subtle to 'non-selected results, inactive tabs'. Muted #6e6a86 is 3.42 main / 3.03 moon. Dawn muted #9893a5 is 2.73 on base and 2.48 on overlay. Cascade uses muted as text (see palettes-07), so it fails AA. Every number in the finding is reproduced. Severity is arguably medium rather than high: the container mapping is cosmetic, while the muted and highlight issues are the a11y part.
refute.fix_notes: Highlight → overlay and muted → subtle are clear improvements and follow the spec. Main highlight is still weak at 1.16, which argues for palettes-11's non-colour selection cue. The container remap has a cost: blue and turquoise become identical (foam), and so do yellow and orange (gold). palettes-07 counts an identical pair as a bug, so the trade-off should be stated. With 6 accents for 8 colours, some duplication is unavoidable. The proposal keeps the four default containers distinct, which is the right priority. Pine #31748f as 'green' is only 3.38 on base and 2.91 on overlay, acceptable for a 1px line. Rose's spec role is 'terminal cyan', but it is visually pink, so pink = rose is fine. Dawn primary buttons stay at 3.47 with iris as accent. That is covered by palettes-12.

fixreview.reasoning: Both files map --uc-identity-colour-blue to the text colour (#e0def4 on line 9, Dawn #575279 on line 31) and pink to subtle (#908caa on line 15, Dawn #797593 on line 37). So the default 'Personal' container line is the same off-white or ink as the labels, and 'Shopping' is grey. The highlight is surface (line 20), 1.07 (main) and 1.09 (moon) from base. Muted is the spec's 'muted' role at 3.42, 3.03 and Dawn 2.73. All proposed hexes match @rose-pine/palette dist/css/rose-pine.css exactly, and the role choices follow readme.md: overlay is listed for 'active tabs', subtle for 'non-selected results, inactive tabs', and foam/pine/gold/love/rose/iris are the accents. Keeping the four default containers (blue, orange, green, pink) distinct is the right priority with six accents for eight slots. The accent stays rose, so the look does not change.
fixreview.fix_notes: The mapping and hexes are correct, but four things should be noted. (1) The fix adds two duplicates, blue = turquoise = foam and yellow = orange = gold. Six accents for eight slots makes that unavoidable, and these are the most natural pairs. Say so in comments (/* foam, shared with blue */) so nobody 'fixes' it back. (2) Main overlay only reaches 1.16 from base. That is the spec colour, but the hover, URL bar and vertical selected tab stay faint. The accent bar from palettes-11 is what actually keeps keyboard selection visible here. highlightMed #403d52 would give 1.69, but subtle on it drops to 3.25, so overlay is the right choice. (3) Dawn: the highlight is already overlay and stays at 1.10, and muted (subtle) at 4.02 still misses 4.5. No Dawn neutral except text does better. (4) The Dawn accent iris #907aa9 is only 3.47 on base and 3.16 on the highlight, which is the URL text in the dropdown and the active-tab line. Pine #286983 is the only Dawn accent above 4.5 (5.59 on base, 5.09 on overlay). If legibility beats the spec's 'links' role, use `--uc-accent-colour: var(--uc-identity-colour-green); /* pine */` in the light block. With palettes-12, the primary buttons are fine either way (black on iris 5.54).

title: Nord port: muted ≈ inverted, the purple accent fails, and the light block reuses dark-ambiance colours
problem: Dark (integrations/nord/nord.css:19-23): inverted nord6 #eceff4 and muted nord4 #d8dee9 are 1.17:1 apart, so de-emphasised text isn't de-emphasised. Highlight nord3 #4c566a is Nord's comment/guide colour. On it the accent nord15 #b48ead is 2.60:1 (URL text, active-tab line) and the blue/red/orange/pink/purple container colours are 1.80-2.72:1. Light (31-45): the identity colours are copied unchanged from the dark ambiance, giving yellow 1.35, green 1.77 and turquoise 1.81 on snow storm. Accent #b48ead on #eceff4 is 2.46:1, and so are the primary buttons (base text on accent): every accent use fails. Pink #d1889f (15, 37) is not a Nord colour.
evidence: Official nordtheme/nord src/nord.css: nord0 #2e3440, nord1 #3b4252, nord2 #434c5e, nord3 #4c566a, nord4 #d8dee9, nord5 #e5e9f0, nord6 #eceff4, nord7 #8fbcbb, nord8 #88c0d0, nord9 #81a1c1, nord10 #5e81ac, nord11 #bf616a, nord12 #d08770, nord13 #ebcb8b, nord14 #a3be8c, nord15 #b48ead. Nord's docs describe nord8 as the primary accent for interactive UI and nord1 as the elevated-UI/panel surface. contrast.py: dark `muted vs inverted 1.17 ROLE?`, `accent/highlight 2.60 FAIL`; light `accent/base 2.46 FAIL`, `base/accent (primary btn) 2.46 FAIL`.
fix:
Dark:
```css
--uc-identity-colour-blue: #81a1c1;      /* nord9 (nord10 is 3.10 on nord0) */
--uc-identity-colour-turquoise: #8fbcbb; /* nord7 */
--uc-identity-colour-green: #a3be8c;     /* nord14 */
--uc-identity-colour-yellow: #ebcb8b;    /* nord13 */
--uc-identity-colour-orange: #d08770;    /* nord12 */
--uc-identity-colour-red: #bf616a;       /* nord11 */
--uc-identity-colour-pink: #d1889f;      /* not Nord; Nord has no pink */
--uc-identity-colour-purple: #b48ead;    /* nord15 */
--uc-base-colour: #2e3440;               /* nord0 */
--uc-highlight-colour: #3b4252;          /* nord1 */
--uc-inverted-colour: #eceff4;           /* nord6 */
--uc-muted-colour: #a4acbb;              /* nord4 65% / nord3 mix: 5.47 on nord0, clearly below nord6 */
--uc-accent-colour: #88c0d0;             /* nord8 */
```
Light: identity blue #5e81ac (nord10), the others as above. base #eceff4, highlight #d8dee9, inverted #2e3440, muted #4c566a, `--uc-accent-colour: #5e81ac` (nord10, 3.50 on base, the best Nord has). Results: dark accent/highlight 5.03, accent/base 6.24, muted 5.47. Light primary buttons should take contrast-color() (separate finding).

Highlight nord3 #4c566a is documented in Nord's own nord.css (dl/nord.css) as 'Used for comments, invisibles, indent- and wrap guide marker … pseudoclass color for disabled elements'. Accent nord15 on it is 2.60. That pair is what Cascade paints for the active-tab line (cascade-tabs.css:98-106) and for URL text in unselected dropdown rows (.urlbarView-url, cascade-colours.css:118-120). Identity colours on the highlight: blue 1.83, red 1.80, orange 2.59, purple 2.60, pink 2.72. The light block (lines 31-38) repeats the dark identity hexes exactly: yellow 1.35, green 1.77, turquoise 1.81 on #eceff4. Accent on light base is 2.46, on the light highlight 2.10, and base text on the accent (primary buttons, cascade-panels.css:81) is 2.46. #d1889f is not one of the 16 Nord colours. One nuance: Nord itself has a single aurora/frost set for both ambiances, so the light identity contrast is inherent to Nord rather than a porting slip.

That weakens the selected tab, URL bar box and selected URL row, which is exactly the regression palettes-11 warns about; Nord is currently one of the few ports where it is fine. Nord's own docs name nord2 #434c5e as the UI 'selection- and highlight color'. nord2 gives 1.45 vs base, nord8 accent 4.31 on it, and inverted 7.49. The muted #a4acbb is off-palette but reasonable (5.47 on base, 1.98 vs inverted). The light fix changes only blue and the accent. Yellow, green and turquoise stay at 1.35-1.81, and the nord10 accent is still 3.50, below AA for URL text. So the light identity and URL-text problems the finding raises are not fixed. That needs darkened off-palette values or an explicit 'Nord has no darker accents' note.

Light: base #eceff4, highlight #d8dee9, inverted #2e3440, muted #4c566a, accent #5e81ac. Either accept 3.5 for URL text or colour .urlbarView-url with inverted. For the light identity colours, use darkened mixes such as color-mix(in srgb, #ebcb8b 55%, #2e3440) for yellow, green and turquoise, if container lines need ≥3:1.

fixreview.reasoning: Every claim reproduces. In dark mode, inverted nord6 and muted nord4 are 1.17:1 apart. The nord15 accent is 2.60 on the nord3 highlight, and the container colours there are 1.80 (red) to 2.72 (pink). refute.reasoning: Every claim checks against morhetz gruvbox.vim (dl/gruvbox.vim:89-132 palette; :170-229 dark/light role mapping: dark uses the bright_* accents, light the faded_*, bg1 = dark1/light1, fg3/fg4 = light3/light4 in dark and dark3/dark4 in light). fixreview.reasoning: Each claim matches morhetz/gruvbox colors/gruvbox.vim. Light base light0 #fbf1c7 and highlight light0_hard #f9f5d7 are 1.03:1 apart, and the highlight is the lighter of the two. #036678 does not exist in gruvbox (faded_blue is #076678). #b57514 is a typo for faded_yellow #b57614. That background only matters for the rare urlbar action text, and fg3 #bdae93 would give 5.32 there but only 1.59 from fg1, so fg4 is the better compromise. In light, faded_aqua (turquoise) and faded_green are both greenish, but that is inherent to gruvbox. Dark neutral_purple at 3.48 is only used for the container line, which is fine for a non-text mark.

title: When highlight ≈ base, the selected tab, hover, URL bar and selected URL-bar result are invisible (keyboard selection lost)
problem: Cascade signals nearly every state with the highlight/base pair alone: the selected tab and hovered tabs (cascade-colours.css:80-81), the URL bar box (`--uc-urlbar-colour` = highlight), toolbar-button hover (74-75), and the keyboard-selected row in the URL-bar results, which is just a `--uc-urlbar-selection-colour` (= base) background on the highlight dropdown (cascade-nav-bar.css:30-36). With result outlines removed, that background is the only indicator of which result Enter will open. Highlight vs base by port: ayu dark 1.00, gruvbox light 1.03, catppuccin 1.07-1.12, rose pine main 1.07 / moon 1.09 / dawn 1.10, gruvbox dark 1.11. The per-port findings carry the palette values. Cascade itself should also stop depending on one weak background difference for keyboard selection.
evidence: contrast.py 'highlight vs base' (agents/palettes/current.txt). Real build with cascade-mocha.css: the selected URL-bar row is #1e1e2e on #181825 (computed), barely visible (agents/palettes/mocha-urlbar-selected.png). With ayu dark both are #1f2430, so the selected row is literally invisible (ayu-dark.png shows no URL bar box). Firefox's own selected-row indicator is the row background (view-nova.css), with no outline on rows.

refute.reasoning: Cascade replaces Firefox's selected-row colour with the base-on-highlight pair. Stock Nova uses color-mix(in srgb, currentColor 32%, transparent) for the browser theme (urlbarview.tokens.css:86-90), roughly 2.7:1 on a dark dropdown. Cascade sets --urlbarview-background-color-selected and -hover to --uc-urlbar-selection-colour (= base) in cascade-colours.css:105-106, puts the same background on .urlbarView-row-inner for both :hover and [selected] (cascade-nav-bar.css:30-36), and paints the dropdown/URL bar with highlight (cascade-colours.css:87-88). I probed the real FF160 build with mocha. The selected .urlbarView-row-inner and its row are rgb(30,30,46), the dropdown is rgb(24,24,37), and the screenshot shows the selected row as a faint band. In ayu dark, highlight and base are both #1f2430 (ayu.css:19-20), so the selected row and the URL bar box are literally invisible. Cascade also kills the outlines that stock Nova draws on Tab-selected result buttons (view-nova.css:476-481, :569-572) via `#urlbar, #urlbar * { outline: none !important }` (cascade-nav-bar.css:20-24). That leaves the background as the only selection cue, and hover and selection look identical. One nuance: in horizontal mode the selected tab keeps the accent line (cascade-tabs.css:98-106), so 'invisible' applies to the selected tab only in vertical tabs. It applies fully to hover, the URL bar box and the URL-bar results.
refute.fix_notes: Part 2 of the proposed CSS does not work, and the stated reason is wrong. `.urlbarView-row[selected] > .urlbarView-row-inner` has specificity (0,3,0). `#urlbar *` has (1,0,0). Both are user !important, so `#urlbar * { box-shadow: none !important }` wins. The row is inside #urlbar: moz-urlbar is light DOM, and the probe returned innerInUrlbar: true. With the proposed rule appended to cascade-nav-bar.css, the real build returned innerBoxShadow "none". When I prefixed the selector with #urlbar, giving (1,3,0), it returned "rgb(203, 166, 247) 2px 0px 0px 0px inset" and a clearly visible accent bar (agents/verify-palettes2/probe-fix2-crop.png). Part 1 (per-port highlight corrections) is fine. The accent bar also separates keyboard selection from mouse hover, which currently look identical.

fixreview.reasoning: The problem is real. Cascade removes all outlines inside #urlbar (cascade-nav-bar.css:20-24). Firefox Nova marks the selected row only with a background (view-nova.css:176-179), and Cascade maps that background to base on a highlight dropdown (cascade-colours.css:105-106, cascade-nav-bar.css:30-36). Whenever highlight ≈ base, which ranges from 1.00 in ayu dark to 1.12 in the ports, the result Enter will open is hard to see. Nova off is no better, because Cascade overrides Proton's blue selected row the same way. One overstatement: in horizontal tabs the selected tab keeps the accent line (cascade-tabs.css:98-106), so 'selected tab invisible' holds only for vertical tabs, plus hovered tabs and the URL bar box. The proposed CSS does NOT work, and I verified this. `#urlbar *` has specificity (1,0,0), and `.urlbarView-row[selected] > .urlbarView-row-inner` has (0,3,0). Both are user !important, so the ID rule wins whatever the order, which is the opposite of the note in the proposal. The view is inside #urlbar (row.closest('#urlbar') is true; browser.xhtml:6430 `<html:moz-urlbar id="urlbar"`), and in Firefox 160 the computed box-shadow of the selected row-inner was 'none'. Adding `#urlbar` to the selector, (1,3,0), makes it apply. I verified that with Nova on and off and in an RTL pseudo-locale.
fixreview.fix_notes: Part 1, the per-port highlights, is covered by palettes-07/08/09/10 and the ayu finding. Part 2 needs `#urlbar` in the selector, otherwise `#urlbar * { box-shadow: none !important }` wins on specificity (verified: computed 'none'). :dir(rtl) is the standard form; nesting is already used in Cascade (cascade-tabs.css:74, cascade-panels.css:109). The bar also shows on the first result while typing, because Firefox selects it automatically. That is a feature: it shows what Enter will do.

title: Primary buttons use base-on-accent text, which fails 4.5:1 in five palettes; use contrast-color()
problem: cascade-panels.css:81-83 sets `--button-text-color-primary(-hover/-active): var(--uc-base-colour)` on the accent background (Translate, Install, Allow… buttons in panels and doorhangers). Base-on-accent is 3.60 in default dark, 3.48/3.73 in gruvbox, 2.46 in nord light, 3.47 in rose pine dawn, and 2.04 with the ayu light accent. The hover state mixes 15% inverted into the accent (cascade-panels.css:66-77), which changes contrast again. Each palette would need a hand-tuned text colour.
evidence: contrast.py `base/accent (primary btn)` rows. Firefox 160 supports `contrast-color()` in chrome: harness `CSS.supports('color','contrast-color(red)')` → true. contrast-color() picks black or white, whichever contrasts more: #786fa6→black 4.62, #b16286→black 4.96, #b48ead→black 7.41, #907aa9→black 5.54, #ff9940→black 9.88, #822fee→white 5.85, #8839ef→white 5.41.

refute.reasoning: cascade-panels.css:81-83 sets --button-text-color-primary(-hover/-active) to --uc-base-colour on `menupopup, panel`, with the background set to the accent at :74. FF160 defines these tokens only on `:root, :host(.anonymous-content-host)` (tokens-shared.css:10-11), so Cascade's panel-level values inherit to the primary buttons inside panels. global-shared.css:345-358 paints `button[default], button.primary` with them. I confirmed this in the real build: a probe element inside #appMenu-mainView resolved var(--button-background-color-primary) to Cascade's accent. Base-on-accent ratios across the shipped palettes: default dark 3.60, gruvbox 3.48 / 3.73, nord light 2.46, rose pine Dawn 3.47 (both files), and nord dark 4.41, which the finding omits. That is at least five schemes below 4.5. One inaccuracy: '2.04 with the ayu light accent' is not the shipped ayu.css, which has 9.08 because its light block wrongly uses a dark base. It must come from a proposed ayu palette. contrast-color() is supported in FF160 chrome. With the proposed change in place, the panel's primary text computed to rgb(0,0,0) on rgb(203,166,247). contrast-color(#786fa6) gave black, contrast-color(#822fee) gave white, and contrast-color(#b16286) gave black, matching the finding.
refute.fix_notes: The three-line change works in FF160 and needs no per-palette tuning. contrast-color() only returns pure black or white. That clashes slightly with palettes like Catppuccin whose guide wants 'On Accent: Base', but there base-on-accent already passes and black/white is visually close. If the maintainer wants palette control, an optional knob such as `--uc-accent-text-colour` defaulting to `contrast-color(var(--uc-accent-colour))` (declared in both config files plus a :where(:root) default) keeps the Cascade convention, but it is not required.

fixreview.reasoning: cascade-panels.css:81-83 puts base-coloured text on the accent. That scores 3.60 in default dark, 3.48 / 3.73 in gruvbox, 2.46 in nord light and 3.47 in Dawn. The ayu 2.04 figure uses the accent proposed in another finding (#ff9940), not the current #cb9ff8. contrast-color() works in Firefox 160 chrome and resolves through the custom properties. I tested a real `.footer-button.primary` (global-shared.css:344-358) added to the app menu. With the proposed Mocha palette it computed to rgb(0,0,0) on rgb(203,166,247), and with Latte to rgb(255,255,255) on rgb(136,57,239). The hover token resolved too. Firefox picks whichever of black/white has the higher WCAG contrast: #786fa6 → black (a near tie, 4.62 vs 4.54), #57759c → white. So the proposal works. Two weaknesses remain. (1) Evaluating each state on its own background flips the label colour on hover when the accent is mid-luminance. Nord light's proposed nord10 #5e81ac gives black (5.21), but its hover #57759c gives white (4.74). (2) The primary-disabled tokens are still resolved on :root by Firefox (tokens-shared.css:72 `--button-background-color-primary-disabled: var(--button-background-color-primary)`, :168 `--button-text-color-primary-disabled: var(--button-text-color-primary)`). Inside Cascade panels the probe returned `--button-text-color-primary-disabled: AccentColorText`, so disabled primary buttons still show Firefox's own accent.
fixreview.fix_notes: The proposal works as written in Firefox 160. I recommend two refinements. Use one text colour for every state so the label does not flip black→white on hover with mid-luminance accents (nord light). Hover then stays ≥5.05 everywhere except nord light at 4.43, and only during hover. Also set the disabled primary tokens, which otherwise keep Firefox's AccentColor/AccentColorText from :root. Defining the derived value as a --uc-panel-* helper in the same `menupopup, panel` rule matches the file's existing --uc-panel-button-hover-colour / --uc-panel-primary-hover-colour pattern. It is not a user knob, so it does not need entries in the config files.

title: Accent and container colours are used as text with no contrast guarantee (URLs in results, container name in the URL bar)
problem: `.urlbarView-url { color: var(--uc-accent-colour) !important; }` (cascade-colours.css:118-120) paints every URL in the results with the raw accent on the highlight dropdown: 2.88 default dark, 2.60 nord dark, 2.10 nord light, 3.16 rose pine dawn, 4.09 catppuccin latte, 1.12 ayu light. The identity classes (123-170) set `--identity-fill-color` to the raw container colour, and Nova uses it as the text colour of the container name in the URL bar, where light palettes reach only 1.5-2.5:1. An accent picked for its look has to double as a text colour in both schemes.
evidence: Firefox 160 usercontext.css:183-191 `#userContext-label { ... @media -moz-pref("browser.nova.enabled") { color: var(--identity-fill-color);` . Relative colour syntax is supported in Fx160 chrome (`CSS.supports('color','oklch(from red calc(l * 0.8) c h)')` → true). Patched-copy probe: `.urlbarView-url` computes to `oklch(0.78 0.084 291)` with the rule below (agents/palettes/fix-urlbar-open.png is clearly more legible than before/urlbar-open.png).
