title: --uc-inactive-opacity pushes tab labels below AA in light palettes, and to ~2:1 in inactive windows
problem: cascade-tabs.css:115-117 sets the whole `.tab-content` of unselected tabs to `opacity: 0.65` (knob in cascade-config.css:21). That blends the label into the base colour. Palettes that pass become failing: catppuccin latte 7.06→3.10, rose pine dawn 6.66→3.00, gruvbox light 10.22→3.82, nord light 4.01, frappé 4.38, ayu dark 5.42. In an inactive (background) window Firefox switches the toolbox text to `--toolbox-text-color-inactive`, which Cascade maps to muted (cascade-colours.css:66). The label is then muted *and* at 65% opacity: latte 1.67, dawn 1.84, gruvbox light 2.02, mocha 2.17, ayu mirage 2.31, default dark 3.80. With `--uc-inactive-opacity` the contrast depends on opacity instead of on the palette.
evidence: Harness: inactive tab label color rgb(250,250,252) (inverted) with `.tab-content` opacity 0.65. Firefox 160 browser-shared.css:318-332 `body { ... color: var(--toolbox-text-color); &:-moz-window-inactive { ... color: var(--toolbox-text-color-inactive); }`. contrast.py `dimmed text/base (opacity 0.65)` rows. muted@0.65 computed separately.

title: No prefers-contrast / forced-colors handling: Cascade's !important tokens override Firefox's high-contrast layers
problem: Cascade has no `@media (prefers-contrast)` or `(forced-colors)` rule anywhere. Firefox ships its high-contrast adaptations as author tokens in `@layer tokens-prefers-contrast` / `tokens-forced-colors` (e.g. tab background SelectedItem, text SelectedItemText, borders CanvasText). Cascade redefines the same properties on :root with user-origin !important (cascade-colours.css:61-115) and paints backgrounds directly (cascade-tabs.css:95-106), so those layers never apply. With the OS 'increase contrast' setting (prefers-contrast), stock Firefox adds a 1px outline to the selected tab and URL bar and shows tabs at full opacity. Cascade keeps tabs at 0.65 opacity and shows the selected tab only as a 1.34:1 grey plus a thin line. Under Windows High Contrast (forced-colors), the system colours never reach the toolbars or tabs because of the same override. I could not trigger forced-colors in the Linux harness, so that part rests on the source analysis.
evidence: Firefox 160 tokens-shared.css:573-574 `@layer tokens-prefers-contrast { @media (prefers-contrast) {` and 642-643 `@layer tokens-forced-colors { @media (forced-colors) {`; tab.tokens.css:97-106 `--tab-background-color-selected: SelectedItem; ... --tab-text-color-selected: SelectedItemText;` (overridden by cascade-colours.css:81-82). Harness with `ui.useAccessibilityTheme=1` (prefers-contrast true): stock → tabs opacity 1, selected tab and URL bar outlined (agents/palettes/hc-stock-top.png). Cascade → tabs opacity 0.65, no outlines (hc-cascade-top.png).

title: Vertical tabs: a hovered tab looks exactly like the selected tab
problem: Hover and selected share one colour (`--tab-background-color-hover` and `-selected` = highlight, cascade-colours.css:80-81). The accent line that marks the active tab is only drawn when `#tabbrowser-tabs[orient="horizontal"]` (cascade-tabs.css:98-106), and hover also lifts the dimming. So in vertical tabs a hovered tab is pixel-identical to the active one, and you can't tell which tab is current while the mouse is over the list. In horizontal tabs the 2px line is the only difference.
evidence: Harness (sidebar.verticalTabs=true, sidebar.revamp=true, dark), hovering tabs[3]: selected .tab-background `rgb(46,49,51)`, backgroundImage none, content opacity 1. Hovered: `rgb(46,49,51)`, none, opacity 1 (agents/palettes/vertical-hover.png: 'Firefox 160 release notes' and 'Rust documentation' look the same). Firefox 160 tabs.css:1083 `background-color: var(--tab-background-color-hover);`.

title: Light mode: the floating page has no visible edge (base #fafafc vs white page 1.04:1)
problem: The floating page (gap plus rounded corners, cascade-layout.css:94-114) only reads as a shape when the frame differs from the page. In light mode the default base #fafafc against a white page is 1.04:1, and ayu light #fafafa is 1.04, so the gap and rounded corners disappear and the page merges with the toolbar. Light palettes also put the highlight (selected tab, URL bar) *darker* than the frame. That is the reverse of the usual light-UI structure (stock Firefox light: grey frame, white selected tab and field), and it is why accent/identity text on the #dadadc URL bar falls to 3.35-4.19.
evidence: before/light.png: no page edge is visible between the toolbar and the white page, while before/dark.png shows it clearly. contrast: #fafafc vs #ffffff 1.04, #ebebed vs #ffffff 1.19. With base #ebebed / highlight #fafafc (rest of the corrected light palette): inverted 13.74/15.69, muted 6.08/6.95, accent 4.91/5.61, identity on the URL bar 4.49-5.61, inactive-tab label at 0.65 opacity 4.76.
fix: Default light block: `--uc-base-colour: #ebebed; --uc-highlight-colour: #fafafc;` (keep inverted #1e2021, muted #55575b and the darkened identity list from the default-palette finding). This yields a visible page edge and white tab/URL bar on a grey frame, and every text pair passes AA.

title: prefers-reduced-motion: the Tab Center Reborn integration animates sidebar width and slides labels without a guard
problem: The core theme gates its only motion (the URL bar growing) behind `prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference` (cascade-responsive.css:56-61, cascade-responsive-windows-fix.css:35-37). The 150ms opacity fades in cascade-nav-bar.css:40 and cascade-tabs.css:113 are not motion. The TCR integration animates the sidebar sliding from 50px to 250px wide (`transition: all 0.2s ease`, cascade-tcr.css:32) and slides tab titles in with `transform: translateX(-10px)` (`transition: all 200ms ease`, tabcenter-reborn.css:36-49), and neither honours the setting.
evidence: grep: cascade-tcr.css:32 `transition: all 0.2s ease;`; tabcenter-reborn.css:38 `transform: translateX(-10px);`, :40 `transition: all 200ms ease;`. No prefers-reduced-motion in either file.

title: The app menu button is shrunk to a 1×44px target but stays keyboard-focusable
problem: cascade-config.css:40-48 sets the `#PanelUI-menu-button` icon to `width: 1px` with zero padding, which leaves a 1px-wide button. It is still in the toolbar's keyboard navigation and still the only mouse entry to the app menu. Keyboard users arrowing along the toolbar land on an invisible control (its focus ring is drawn around a 1px icon), and as a pointer target it is far below WCAG 2.5.8's 24×24.
evidence: Harness getBoundingClientRect: `#PanelUI-menu-button` width 1, height 44, display flex. Firefox 160 toolbarbuttons.css:227-236 draws the focus ring on the (1px) `.toolbarbutton-icon`.

title: Eight full copies of cascade-colours.css make palette and accessibility fixes land unevenly
problem: Lines 47-170 of every integration are byte-identical to cascade-colours.css (`diff` of lines 47+ shows no difference for all 8 files). Only the two palette blocks differ. Any fix to the mapping, such as the accent-text clamp, the identity fill colours, a forced-colors block or a new token, has to be repeated in nine files, and users who installed an integration keep the old mapping. The wrong roles above (muted = overlay/muted, highlight = mantle/surface) suggest ports are made by search-and-replace of hex values with no check of roles or contrast.
evidence: `for f in integrations/*/*.css; do diff <(sed -n '47,$p' chrome/includes/cascade-colours.css) <(sed -n '47,$p' $f); done` → SAME for all eight.
fix: Split each colour file into a palette part and a mapping part: `chrome/includes/cascade-palette.css` holds only the two `@media (prefers-color-scheme)` blocks, and cascade-colours.css keeps the mapping and imports nothing. In userChrome.css, `@import "includes/cascade-palette.css";` goes before `cascade-colours.css`. Integrations then ship only palette files (~45 lines), and users swap in a palette file. Add the contrast script (agents/palettes/contrast.py in the scratchpad) to the repo as a check that every palette keeps inverted ≥4.5, muted ≥4.5 on base, accent text ≥4.5 and highlight ≠ base.

title: Window resizes animate the nav-bar width, so Firefox measures a stale width and leaves toolbar buttons drawn over the tabs or stuck in the » menu
problem: chrome/includes/cascade-responsive.css:17 sets `width: var(--uc-urlbar-min-width)`, which is 35vw by default (cascade-config.css:87-88, cascade-config-mouse.css:83-84). Lines 56-60 also put `transition: width 200ms` on #nav-bar in every state. A vw width resolves to a new px value whenever the window is resized, so every resize (maximize/restore, snapping, tiling, dragging the edge) starts a 200ms width animation. Firefox's OverflowableToolbar decides which buttons go into the » menu right after the resize event, so it measures the nav-bar partway through that animation, at roughly its old width. After shrinking a window, the last buttons stay in the bar and are drawn past its end, over the tab strip. After growing it, buttons stay in the » menu even though there is room for them. Nothing corrects this until the next resize. Anyone whose nav-bar needs the overflow menu is affected, which is common at 1000-1300px with a few extension buttons. The windows fix has the same problem with `transition: margin` and vw margins (cascade-responsive-windows-fix.css:10-11, 33-38).
evidence:
Firefox 160 re-checks overflow only on window resize, widget DOM changes and customization: CustomizableUI.sys.mjs:7701 `window.addEventListener("resize", this);`, :8397-8403 `#onResize(aEvent) {... this.#checkOverflow(); }`. #getOverflowInfo (:8039-8099) measures `getBoundingClientRect().width` of the toolbar inside `await win.promiseDocumentFlushed(...)` (:8068), which runs on the first flush after the resize.
Harness test (current HEAD, 6 extra buttons, 1400px): 60ms after `window.resizeTo(1100,800)`, `#nav-bar.getAnimations().length == 1` and the nav-bar is 430px wide, partway between 490 and 385.
Once settled: nav-bar ends at x=386 but history-panelmenu is at 355-391; the customization target has scrollWidth 390 against clientWidth 348, so the button spills over the tabs.
After resizing back to 1400: library-button and history-panelmenu are now also in the » menu, although the URL bar is 257px wide (185px before). The bar never returns to its original state.
The same steps with the fix below: no animation on resize (anims [], width immediately 385); at 1100 scrollWidth 348 = clientWidth 348 with the right items overflowed; back at 1400 the original state is restored exactly.
A registered custom property works from userChrome in FF160: computed `--uc-urlbar-grow` was 0.93 at 80ms after the popover opened, and 0.28 at 80ms after it closed.
Tested files: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-cascade/48698eae-20a7-558b-9a00-57da38f74033/scratchpad/agents/oneline/chrome-final/includes/cascade-responsive.css

refute.reasoning: A vw width turns into a new px value on every resize, so `transition: width` (cascade-responsive.css:56-60) starts a 200ms animation each time. Firefox 160's OverflowableToolbar re-checks only on window resize, on widget DOM changes and around customization: CustomizableUI.sys.mjs:7701 adds the resize listener, :8397-8403 `#onResize` calls `#checkOverflow`, and the handleEvent switch at :8532-8575 has no overflow/underflow event. The check measures `getBoundingClientRect().width` inside `promiseDocumentFlushed` (:8068). That flush comes at the start of the transition, so the bar is measured at roughly its old width. I reproduced this myself, with a control run where only the transition is removed, and the bug goes away in that run. The proposed @property fix works on the same steps.
refute.fix_notes: Verified: with a registered `<number>` animated instead of `width`, the width follows the vw value instantly on resize, and the grow animation still runs. It works for old configs that still use vw. The weaker `%` alternative is also correct, because a percentage stays a percentage in the computed value. The windows-fix `transition: margin` with vw margins has the same mechanism (not separately tested). Keep the urlbar-container shrink rule and its comment when rewriting the file: the tested chrome-final copy accidentally dropped that comment.

fixreview.reasoning: Real. A vw width computes to px, so every window resize changes the computed `width` of #nav-bar and starts the 200ms `transition: width` (cascade-responsive.css:56-60). OverflowableToolbar never uses ResizeObserver or overflow events. It re-checks only on window resize, widget DOM changes and customization, and it measures in the first flush after the resize, which is the start of the animation. I reproduced this on HEAD and the proposed @property fix removes it. The fix is correct in Firefox 160: @property from a user sheet registers (computed value is "0", not ""), the transition interpolates, the width follows resizes instantly, and the fix does not depend on Nova, density or orientation. Old configs are not at risk: --uc-urlbar-min-width and --uc-urlbar-max-width have been in every config since the first commit (88b8b7d), so the calc never goes invalid.
fixreview.fix_notes: Works as proposed. Ship it together with oneline-03 ([open]), -04 and -06; the combined file is the agents/oneline/chrome-final version. --uc-urlbar-grow is internal, so a short comment saying it is not a user knob avoids confusion with the --uc-* knobs. No config change is needed. The 'weaker alternative' (35%/45% defaults) works for default configs only: a percentage stays a percentage in the computed value, but configs that keep vw would still animate on resize. The @property version is preferable. Replacing the windows fix with a forward (oneline-05) also removes its `transition: margin` copy of this bug.

title: Windows fix: focusing the URL bar with vertical tabs (or in a popup) moves the whole nav-bar off-screen
problem: In cascade-responsive-windows-fix.css, the 'no tab bar' reset (lines 28-31, `margin: 0 !important`) loses to the focus rule (lines 17-20, also `!important`) because the focus rule's selector is more specific. With native vertical tabs, or in a popup, mini window or taskbar-tab window ([tabs-hidden]), Ctrl+L or a click into the URL bar applies the negative top margin and the 100vw-based end margin. The nav-bar moves above the window, so the URL bar you are typing into disappears and the toolbox collapses to 0px.
evidence:
Specificity: `#navigator-toolbox:has(#urlbar:is(:focus-within, [open])) #nav-bar` is (3,1,0), because :has() takes `#urlbar:is(...)` = (1,1,0). `#navigator-toolbox[tabs-hidden] #nav-bar` is (2,1,0). Both are user !important, so the higher specificity wins.
Harness, windows-fix + `sidebar.verticalTabs=true` + `gURLBar.focus()`: `#nav-bar` rect [0,-40,630,40], margin `-40px 770px 0px 0px`, navigator-toolbox height 0. The screenshot /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-cascade/48698eae-20a7-558b-9a00-57da38f74033/scratchpad/agents/oneline/wf-vert-focus.png shows no URL bar at all.
Before focusing, the same window is correct: nav-bar [0,0,1400,40], margin 0px.
Firefox 160 sets tabs-hidden for vertical tabs and single-tab popups, mini windows and taskbar tabs (tab-bar-visibility.js:9-25, 36). cascade-responsive.css avoids the problem only because its focus width (line 37) is not !important.

refute.reasoning: In the windows fix, both rules are user `!important`, so specificity decides. `#navigator-toolbox:has(#urlbar:is(:focus-within,[open])) #nav-bar` is (3,1,0), because :has() takes its most specific argument, (1,1,0). `#navigator-toolbox[tabs-hidden] #nav-bar` is (2,1,0) and `#nav-bar.browser-titlebar` is (1,1,0). So the focus margin beats the `margin: 0 !important` reset. Firefox sets tabs-hidden for native vertical tabs and for single-tab popups, taskbar tabs and mini windows (tab-bar-visibility.js:9-25, 36). `.browser-titlebar` goes on nav-bar only when the tabs are hidden (:40-48). cascade-responsive.css escapes this only because its focus width (line 37) is not !important.
refute.fix_notes: The preferred fix is fine (forwarding @import, see oneline-05). The scoped alternative is also correct: `:not([tabs-hidden])` scoping, logical margins (which also fix RTL), and grow on [open]. It still leaves the 40px vs 44px height mismatch from oneline-05(a): in normal density `--urlbar-container-padding-block` is still 4px, so the nav-bar stays 4px short and its URL bar about 2px below centre. It also lacks the urlbar-container shrink rule from oneline-05(d).

fixreview.reasoning: Real, and the specificity analysis is right. :has() takes the specificity of its most specific argument, `#urlbar:is(...)` = (1,1,0), so the focus rule is (3,1,0) and beats the (2,1,0) `[tabs-hidden]` reset. Both are user !important. TabBarVisibility sets tabs-hidden for vertical tabs, popups, mini windows and taskbar tabs, so any focus there pulls the nav-bar off-screen. The preferred fix (replace the file with an @import of cascade-responsive.css) works. The scoped margin fallback is syntactically fine, but it keeps the 4px/touch offset from oneline-05 and drops the animation, so the forward is clearly better.
fixreview.fix_notes: Use the forward from oneline-05. I verified that it resolves (the relative URL resolves against includes/) and gives the exact same layout as cascade-responsive.css. If the margin variant is kept anyway, also copy the `#nav-bar #urlbar-container` shrink rule, and compute the height from --urlbar-container-padding-block (or simply drop the file). The fallback as written does not do either.

title: A new window opens with the URL bar focused and grown, so the overflow menu is filled for the wide bar and buttons spill over the first tab after the first click
problem:
The bar grows on `#urlbar:is(:focus-within, [open])` (cascade-responsive.css:35-43). Firefox focuses the URL bar in every new window (Ctrl+N, about:blank, home page), and OverflowableToolbar runs its first check after first paint, while the bar is at --uc-urlbar-max-width. It therefore keeps more buttons in the bar than fit at the minimum width. When the user clicks into the page, the bar shrinks back and the extra buttons are drawn past its end, over the » button and the first tab. They stay there until the window is resized. The same happens when the window is resized while the URL bar is focused.
A smaller side effect of growing on focus: UrlbarView decides whether result rows wrap onto two lines once, when the popover opens, from the input's width at that moment. Clicking into the bar and typing after Ctrl+L can therefore give different row layouts at the same window size (for example at 1920px: about 490px vs 680px around the 650px threshold).
evidence:
Harness (HEAD, 12 extra nav-bar buttons, OpenBrowserWindow()): in the new window gURLBar.focused=true, #nav-bar is 630px (45vw), and the overflow menu holds 6 items.
After `gBrowser.selectedBrowser.focus()`: nav-bar ends at x=491 while bookmarks-menu/print/find sit at 428-536; target scrollWidth 535 against clientWidth 453.
Resizing while focused gives the same picture: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-cascade/48698eae-20a7-558b-9a00-57da38f74033/scratchpad/agents/oneline/overflow-stuck-crop.png shows print/find/new-window over the » button and the 'Cascade' tab.
Firefox only re-checks on resize or widget changes (CustomizableUI.sys.mjs:7701, 8397-8403, 8433-8500).
Row wrap: UrlbarView.mjs:4106-4110 `let wrap = getBoundsWithoutFlushing(this.input).width < 650;` runs when the view opens (:1335) and on window resize only (:1344, :4826-4828).
With `#urlbar[open]` instead: the new window initialises at 490px (focused, not open), the overflow menu holds 9 items, and after blur scrollWidth 453 = clientWidth 453. The bar still grows to 630px once results open (verified with gURLBar.search('c')). The popover follows the growth because it is CSS-anchor positioned (urlbar.css:581-596 `position-anchor: --urlbar-anchor; position-area: block-end center`).

refute.reasoning: `_setInitialFocus` (browser-init.js:775-782) calls `gURLBar.select()` when the initial page is a blank page. `isBlankPageURL` (utilityOverlay.js:84-90) covers about:blank, about:home and the new-tab URL, and about:privatebrowsing is also included. OverflowableToolbar.init() runs only on browser-delayed-startup-finished (CustomizableUI.sys.mjs:7685-7689, :8514-8522), so its first check (:7721) measures the grown bar. After blur there is no resize, so nothing re-checks. One correction: this does not happen for every home page. A custom website home page sends focus to the content, not the URL bar. Ctrl+N with the default home or new tab page, and a first window on about:home, are affected. The UrlbarView row-wrap side effect is plausible: `#enableOrDisableRowWrap` uses `getBoundsWithoutFlushing(this.input).width < 650` (UrlbarView.mjs:4106-4110) when the view opens (:1335) and on resize. I did not test it separately.
refute.fix_notes: Growing only on `#urlbar[open]` is verified and is a reasonable trade-off: Ctrl+L alone no longer widens the bar, but it widens at the first keystroke or when a click opens the view. `overflow-x: clip` on #nav-bar-customization-target is valid. Firefox sets only `min-width: 0` on it (browser-shared.css:614-618), and clip combined with visible is allowed. It is only a safety net, though: spilled buttons become invisible and unreachable instead of overlapping. If the URL bar is the last item in the target, the clip also cuts the open background's 8px overhang (urlbar.css:28) and its 14px shadow (urlbar.css:131), which keyboard users who remove all buttons will hit. As the first item it is partly covered by the first-child padding (browser-shared.css:620-623). overflow-clip-margin would need about 22px, not 8px.

fixreview.reasoning: Real. A new window focuses the URL bar before OverflowableToolbar's first check. With focus-based growth that check measures the 45vw bar, and after blur the extra buttons spill. Firefox does not re-check on focus or blur. Growing only on `#urlbar[open]` fixes it and keeps growth working: the popover is anchor-positioned to the input container, so it follows the growth. Row wrap is decided in #openPanel() before `open` is set, so it is now always computed at the minimum width (consistent). The cost is that Ctrl+L alone no longer widens the bar until typing opens results, which matters for a keyboard-centred theme; I see no CSS-only way to tell the startup focus apart from a user focus, so the trade-off is acceptable. The unconditional `overflow-x: clip` safety net has a real visual regression, though. The URL bar's open background reaches 8px past the input in Nova (plus a 14px shadow). With the URL bar as the first or last item of the target (plausible in minimal setups), its top half is cut flat at the target edge while the popover half below is not. That leaves a visible notch at the corner. Clipping only while the results are closed avoids this: while open the bar is at its widest, so nothing can spill then.
fixreview.fix_notes: The [open] part is correct and verified; keep it. Replace the unconditional clip with one scoped to closed results. That way the open background and its shadow are never cut, and you do not need overflow-clip-margin (which would also let stale buttons paint over the tabs). In customize mode Firefox's own author `overflow: clip` (customizeMode.css:24-26) still applies, because author normal beats user normal.

title: Customize mode: a 100px empty gap left of the nav-bar, and the 35vw nav-bar clips the buttons Firefox moves back into it
problem:
In the 'customize' screenshot the nav-bar starts about 100px from the left edge, over empty space. The hidden menu bar is itself a `.customization-target`, and customize mode gives every target `min-width: 100px`. Cascade's `width: 0px` (cascade-layout.css:36-42) is not !important and is also skipped while [customizing], so in the one-line row this zero-height menu bar takes 100px.
When customizing starts, OverflowableToolbar moves every overflowed button back into the nav-bar. The nav-bar stays 35vw wide and Firefox clips its target with `overflow: clip`. Users with many buttons cannot see or drag the clipped ones, and the flexible spaces are squeezed into 12px 'brackets' around a tiny URL bar.
evidence:
Probe in customize mode (HEAD): #toolbar-menubar has attributes `autohide,inactive`, computed min-width 100px, rect [0,0,100,0]; #nav-bar rect [100,0,490,44].
Sources: customizeMode.css:17-19 `:root[customizing] .customization-target:not(#widget-overflow-fixed-list) { min-width: var(--size-layout-xsmall); }`; customizeMode.css:24-26 `toolbar[overflowable][customizing] > .customization-target { overflow: clip; }`; CustomizableUI.sys.mjs:8556-8558 `case "customizationstarting": this.#disable();` → :8269-8275 `#moveItemsBackToTheirOrigin(true)`.
Screenshots: harness/shots/before/customize.png (gap, squeezed springs). With the fix, /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-cascade/48698eae-20a7-558b-9a00-57da38f74033/scratchpad/agents/oneline/fix-customize.png shows the nav-bar as a full 1400px row (springs 112px, URL bar 955px) and the tabs as a second row.
This fix must ship together with the @property finding. With a width transition, leaving customize mode animates 100% → 35vw, and the check Firefox runs after customization (aftercustomization → #enable → #checkOverflow) measures the wide bar. Verified: all 3 overflowed buttons stayed in the bar and spilled (scrollWidth 547 vs 489). With the @property version the original overflow state comes back.

refute.reasoning: The menu bar toolbar is its own customization target: class `customization-target` is confirmed by a probe. customizeMode.css:17-19 gives every target `min-width: var(--size-layout-xsmall)` (100px, tokens-shared.css:486), and min-width beats Cascade's width: 0. customizeMode.css:24-26 clips overflowable targets while customizing. The customizationstarting handler (CustomizableUI.sys.mjs:8556) calls `#disable()` → `#moveItemsBackToTheirOrigin(true)` (:8269-8275), so every overflowed button returns into the 35vw bar and gets clipped. One small inaccuracy: the `:not([customizing])` exclusion in cascade-layout.css:38 is irrelevant here. The menu bar never gets [customizing], because CustomizeMode.sys.mjs:533-538 only marks `toolbar[customizable=true]:not([autohide], [collapsed])`; min-width alone causes the 100px. #nav-bar does get [customizing], so `#nav-bar[customizing]` is a valid selector. The claim that the two fixes must ship together is also confirmed.
refute.fix_notes: Both rules are verified. `#toolbar-menubar[autohide][inactive]{min-width:0 !important;width:0 !important}` also removes the 1px offset from oneline-06. Cosmetic note: in customize mode the nav-bar row is 40px tall instead of 44px, which does not matter. The fix has to ship with the `--uc-urlbar-grow` change, as the finding says.

fixreview.reasoning: Real. In customize mode the hidden menu bar takes 100px of the row, and the 35vw nav-bar clips the buttons that Firefox moves back into it. One detail of the stated cause is wrong: Cascade's rule is not 'skipped while [customizing]'. CustomizeMode only sets [customizing] on `toolbar[customizable=true]:not([autohide], [collapsed])`, so the autohide menu bar never gets it and `:not([customizing])` was always true. The 100px comes from customizeMode.css's min-width, which beats any width; outside customize mode, toolbar.css's 1px min-width (author) beats Cascade's non-!important rule. The proposed `min-width: 0 !important; width: 0 !important` on `#toolbar-menubar[autohide][inactive]` is correct. It does not touch a menu bar shown with Alt (inactive removed) or one shown permanently (autohide removed). `#nav-bar[customizing] { width: 100% !important }` works, and the TabsToolbar (flex 1 1 0%) wraps to its own row. It must indeed ship with the @property change. The cited screenshot fix-customize.png came from an intermediate variant that still had a width transition: there the customize panel's arrow sits under 'Hacker News' instead of the » button, because #updateOverflowPanelArrowOffset measured the » button mid-transition. With the @property version the arrow is correct (final-customize.png and my run).
fixreview.fix_notes: Correct as proposed when combined with oneline-01 (no width transition). The old selector `#nav-bar.browser-titlebar`, which the proposal silently drops, is redundant: tab-bar-visibility.js:40-48 only adds browser-titlebar to #nav-bar when hideTabsToolbar is true, which also sets [tabs-hidden] (:36). Dropping it is safe. Fix the rationale comment, since there is no [customizing] skip involved.

title: cascade-responsive-windows-fix.css is obsolete in FF160 (written for the removed #titlebar) and has further bugs: RTL overlap, off-centre in touch density, buttons over the tabs at narrow widths, ignores --uc-urlbar-position
problem:
The windows fix pulls the nav-bar up into the tab row with negative and 100vw-based margins. It was written for the old #titlebar wrapper; commit f67aa11 only renamed `#titlebar` to `#TabsToolbar`. In FF160 #TabsToolbar is a direct child of #navigator-toolbox on every platform, so the flex-wrap layout in cascade-responsive.css applies on Windows too, and the margin hack only adds bugs:
(a) Height formula: the variables still exist, but `--urlbar-height + 2 * --urlbar-padding-block` = 40px while the tab row is 44px, so the nav-bar sits 4px low. In touch density the urlbar container uses its own 5px padding, so the nav-bar is 6.5px off-centre and the toolbox is 2px taller than the tab row.
(b) The physical `margin: top right bottom left` is not mirrored in RTL: the nav-bar covers the leftmost 490px of the tab strip and the right 490px of the row stay empty.
(c) `--uc-urlbar-position: 3` is ignored.
(d) It lacks the URL-bar shrink rule from cascade-responsive.css:24-28, so near 1000px the 311px-minimum URL bar cannot shrink and the » and extensions buttons are drawn over the first tab.
(e) The vertical-tabs focus bug and the resize-animation bug from the other findings.
evidence:
browser.xhtml has no id="titlebar" (grep count 0); #TabsToolbar is at browser.xhtml:6267, a direct child of `<toolbox id="navigator-toolbox">` (5825). `git show f67aa11` replaced `#titlebar` with `#TabsToolbar` in this file.
(a) variables.css:14 `--urlbar-height: max(32px, 1.4em)`; urlbar.tokens.css:26 `--urlbar-padding-block: 4px`; urlbar.css:47 and :59-61 `&[uidensity="touch"] { --urlbar-container-padding-block: 5px; }`. Probe (normal): TabsToolbar [490,0,910,44], nav-bar [0,4,490,40]. Probe (touch): TabsToolbar height 53, nav-bar [0,11,490,44], margin -42px, toolbox 55px, URL bar centre y=33 vs tab centre 26.5.
(b) Probe with intl.l10n.pseudo=bidi: TabsToolbar [0,0,910,44], nav-bar [0,4,490,40], so they overlap on the left. Screenshot /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-cascade/48698eae-20a7-558b-9a00-57da38f74033/scratchpad/agents/oneline/wf-rtl-crop.png shows the 'Wikipedia'/'Rust' tabs under the URL bar. cascade-responsive.css in RTL is correct: nav-bar [909..1399], tabs [0..909].
(d) urlbar.css:14 `--urlbar-container-min-width: 310px`, :672-692 width calc, :717-720 `flex: 400 0 auto`. Probe at 1010px: nav-bar ends at 354, URL bar 311px, unified-extensions at 390-422, scrollWidth 422 vs 321. Screenshot wf-1000-crop.png shows » and the extensions icon over the 'Cascade' tab.

refute.reasoning:
I checked the obsolescence argument against the Firefox 160 markup:
- browser.xhtml has no id="titlebar" (count 0), and #TabsToolbar (6267) sits inside `<toolbox id="navigator-toolbox">` (5825).
- `git show f67aa11` only renamed #titlebar to #TabsToolbar in this file.
- The original reason, 'flexbox is broken on Windows' (old README removed in 8239e30), dates from XUL box layout. No `display: -moz-box` remains anywhere in the FF160 chrome or UA CSS, and xul.css:302-304 styles toolbox as plain flex.

I could not test on Windows. The concrete defects of the file all reproduce in the harness, and none of them depend on the platform.
refute.fix_notes: A file that only contains `@import url("cascade-responsive.css");` is valid: the @import comes first, and nested imports work. It is the cleanest fix, but have one Windows user test it before announcing that the file is retired, because the harness only runs Linux. The current README has no 'use the Windows fix' instruction (the docs moved to the external vitepress site in 8239e30), so the docs change belongs on that site.

fixreview.reasoning: Real. In Firefox 160 #TabsToolbar is a direct child of #navigator-toolbox (no #titlebar), and commit f67aa11 only renamed the selectors. The margin hack then adds bugs that the flex layout does not have. I confirmed (b) RTL overlap and (d) buttons over the first tab near 1000px in the provided screenshots, and (e) by my own vertical-tabs run. The forward is the right fix and I verified that it works: every one of my runs used a userChrome.css importing cascade-responsive-windows-fix.css reduced to the @import, and gave the exact same layout as cascade-responsive.css. A forward is kinder than deleting the file: a missing @import is silently ignored and users would lose the one-line layout. Caveat: the extracted build is Linux, so Windows' own platform browser.css cannot be checked here. The markup is platform-independent, and the shared CSS has no Windows-only toolbox layout (browser-shared.css Windows blocks at :180, :197 and :438 only set tokens and hide a titlebar spacer). The historic reason ('flexbox broken on Windows', README at 88b8b7d) was about the removed #titlebar wrapper. Smoke-test on Windows before announcing.
fixreview.fix_notes: Ship the two-line forward. The 'swap in the Windows fix' instruction lives in the external vitepress docs (README.md no longer has it since 8239e30), so the change belongs there. If a margin variant were kept, the oneline-02 fallback alone is not enough: it still needs --urlbar-container-padding-block (and still sits low, because the tab row is taller than the URL bar) plus the shrink rule.
