title: #TabsToolbar width rules and transition do nothing (UA `flex: 1 !important`); the '- 1px' only compensates a 1px menu-bar strip
problem:
cascade-responsive.css:30-32 and :40-42 size #TabsToolbar with `calc(100vw - ... - 1px)`, and lines 57-59 transition it 'so that their widths always add up to one row'. #TabsToolbar has flex="1", which xul.css (a UA sheet) maps to `flex: 1 !important`. UA !important beats any userChrome declaration, so the toolbar's flex-basis is 0% and its `width` is never used. It always takes whatever the nav-bar leaves, frame by frame.
The '- 1px' exists only because the hidden menu bar is 1px wide: Cascade's `width: 0px` (cascade-layout.css:39) loses to toolbar.css `min-width: 1px`. That pushes the whole row 1px to the right and leaves a 1px strip at the window edge. The TabsToolbar transition still runs useless style animations on every focus and resize.
For reference, the #navigator-toolbox children in FF160 are script, #toolbar-menubar, #TabsToolbar, #nav-bar, #PersonalToolbar, #notifications-toolbar and template#BrowserToolbarPalette. No toolbar is new compared with 159.
evidence:
xul.css:683-685 `[flex="1"] { flex: 1 !important; }`; browser.xhtml:6267-6275 `<toolbar id="TabsToolbar" ... flex="1">`; toolbar.css:11-12 `toolbar { min-width: 1px;`.
Probe (HEAD): TabsToolbar computed flex `1 1 0%`; #toolbar-menubar computed min-width 1px, rect [0,0,1,0]; #nav-bar rect [1,0,490,44]; TabsToolbar [491,0,909,44].
With the TabsToolbar widths and transition removed and the menu bar at min-width 0: nav-bar [0,0,490,44], TabsToolbar [490,0,910,44]. 90ms into the grow animation: nav-bar width 590, TabsToolbar x=590 w=810, adjacent without a gap or overlap.
fix:
Delete cascade-responsive.css:30-32 and :40-42, remove `#TabsToolbar` from the transition selector (57-58), and change the comment at 53-55. Add a short note above the #nav-bar rule:

```css
/* #TabsToolbar has flex="1", which xul.css turns into `flex: 1 !important`
   (UA !important, userChrome cannot override it): it always takes what the
   Navigation Bar leaves of the row, only the Navigation Bar needs a width. */
```

Apply the menu-bar `min-width: 0 !important; width: 0 !important` rule from the customize finding, which removes the 1px strip.

refute.reasoning: #TabsToolbar has `flex="1"` (browser.xhtml:6275). xul.css:683-685 `[flex="1"] { flex: 1 !important; }` is UA !important, which beats userChrome, so the flex-basis is 0% and the `width` rules at cascade-responsive.css:30-32 and :40-42 never affect layout. The toolbar always takes what the nav-bar leaves. The transition still creates style animations, because transitions act on computed values. The 1px offset comes from toolbar.css:11-12 `min-width: 1px` beating Cascade's `width: 0px` on the hidden menu bar. The 1px strip exists in layout but cannot be seen: pixels at x=0, 1 and 3 have the same colour in shots/before/dark.png (30,32,33) and light.png (250,250,252). So the value of this fix is removing dead code and a misleading comment, not a visual change.
refute.fix_notes: Deleting the #TabsToolbar widths and its transition is safe. With flex-basis 0 the toolbar also wraps to its own line in customize mode (verified: tabs [0,40,1400]). The menu-bar `min-width:0 !important; width:0 !important` rule removes the offset (nav at x=0). The proposed explanatory comment is accurate.

fixreview.reasoning: Real. xul.css is a UA sheet, and `[flex="1"] { flex: 1 !important; }` is UA !important, which no userChrome declaration can beat. #TabsToolbar has flex="1", so its flex-basis is 0% and its `width` is never used. The width rules and the TabsToolbar transition are dead layout-wise, yet they still create a style transition on every resize and focus. The '- 1px' only exists because the menu bar is 1px wide: toolbar.css `min-width: 1px` (author) beats Cascade's non-!important `width: 0px`. Removing the rules and making the menu bar `min-width: 0 !important` closes the 1px strip, and the two toolbars stay adjacent during the grow animation.
fixreview.fix_notes: Correct, and the proposed comment is accurate. With oneline-01 applied the TabsToolbar transition disappears anyway, because only --uc-urlbar-grow is transitioned on #nav-bar. The menu-bar rule is the same one as in oneline-04; apply it once.

title: Menu bar shown (Alt or always): labels stick to the top of the 44px row, and every Alt press shifts the URL bar and tabs about 350px
problem: In the one-line row a shown menu bar is laid out inline before the nav-bar. It is stretched to the row height, but its items stay at its top, so File/Edit/View sit about 10px above the centre line of the toolbar buttons (see the 'menubar' screenshot). Pressing Alt temporarily inserts the 349px menu bar, so the URL bar and every tab jump right, then jump back when the menu closes.
evidence:
Probe with the menu bar shown: #toolbar-menubar [0,0,349,44] with align-items `normal`; #menubar-items [0,1,349,42]; #main-menubar [0,1,349,23]; File label at y=4-20, while the urlbar-container centre is at y=22. With Alt (inactive removed): nav-bar moves from x=0 to x=349 and the TabsToolbar shrinks from 910 to 561px.
With `#toolbar-menubar { align-items: center }` the labels line up with the buttons: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-cascade/48698eae-20a7-558b-9a00-57da38f74033/scratchpad/agents/oneline/final-menubar-crop.png. Firefox sets no align-items on #toolbar-menubar (browser-shared.css:542-569 only sets overflow and heights), so a normal declaration is enough.

refute.reasoning: Both parts of the claim hold. Firefox puts the menu bar at the top of its box on purpose: browser.css:20-23 `#menubar-items { flex-direction: column; justify-content: normal; /* align the menubar to the top also in customize mode */ }`. The `align="center"` on #menubar-items (browser.xhtml:5835, which becomes `align-items:center !important` via xul.css:657) only centres it horizontally because of the column direction. Stock Firefox gives the menu bar a row of its own, so this does not show there. In Cascade's one-line flex row, #toolbar-menubar is stretched to the 44px line height (its align-items is the initial `normal`), so the menus sit at the top while the nav-bar buttons are centred. I checked who sets align-items on #toolbar-menubar: browser-shared.css:542-569 sets only overflow, min-height and height; .browser-toolbar (browser-shared.css:375-385), toolbar.css:11-33 and xul.css have no align-items for toolbar; and #toolbar-menubar has no [align] attribute. So a user-origin normal `align-items: center` applies. The Alt shift happens because #toolbar-menubar (order 0) goes from the 1px stub to its content width while #TabsToolbar (flex 1 1 0%) absorbs the loss. The 1px stub comes from `min-width: 1px` at toolbar.css:12 beating Cascade's normal `width: 0px`.
refute.fix_notes: `align-items: center` is all that is needed and is verified above. In the inactive state the 23px menubar-items box ends up at y=-12 inside the 0px-tall toolbar, but the `overflow: hidden` that browser-shared.css:544 sets on [autohide] hides it, so nothing shows. The `min-width: 0 !important` in the fix removes the measured 1px stub (nav-bar at x=1) that toolbar.css:12 causes, which is a small gain. Dropping `:not([customizing])` is harmless: CustomizeMode.sys.mjs:533-538 only adds [customizing] to `toolbar[customizable=true]:not([autohide], [collapsed])`, so an [autohide] menu bar never has it. The optional `#toolbar-menubar[autohide]:not([inactive]) { width: 100% }` puts the temporary menu bar on its own row (order 0, it wraps first). That swaps the 348px sideways jump for a downward shift of the toolbox and page, which is what stock Firefox does. It is a taste call and still a layout shift, so it should stay optional.

fixreview.reasoning:
Both parts of the problem are real.

1. Labels sit too high. In the one-line row #toolbar-menubar stretches to 44px, which also stretches #menubar-items. Firefox deliberately pins #main-menubar to the top of #menubar-items: browser.css:20-23 `#menubar-items { flex-direction: column; justify-content: normal; /* align the menubar to the top also in customize mode */ }`.

2. Alt shifts the row sideways. The 349px menu bar is a flex item on the same wrapping line as the nav-bar. #TabsToolbar has flex="1", which xul.css:683-685 turns into `flex: 1 !important` (basis 0, UA !important). So the tab bar shrinks while the nav-bar slides right, instead of anything wrapping.

The core fix is right and the cascade holds:
- Firefox sets no align-items on #toolbar-menubar. Checked browser-shared.css:542-569 (overflow and heights only), .browser-toolbar at :375-386, .browser-titlebar at :390 and browser.css:119-124, toolbar.css:11-35, and xul.css toolbar rules. So a normal user declaration applies.
- `min-width: 0 !important` is needed: toolkit toolbar.css:11-12 `toolbar { min-width: 1px; }` is author-origin. That 1px is why the inactive menu bar measured [0,0,1,0] and the nav-bar started at x=1.
- It also beats customizeMode.css:17-19 `:root[customizing] .customization-target:not(#widget-overflow-fixed-list) { min-width: var(--size-layout-xsmall) }` (100px, tokens-shared.css:486). The toolbar is its own customization target (CustomizableUI.sys.mjs:2042), so HEAD leaves a 100px gap at the start of the row in customize mode.
- Dropping `:not([customizing])` changes nothing. CustomizeMode.sys.mjs:533-537 only sets [customizing] on `toolbar[customizable=true]:not([autohide], [collapsed])`, so an autohide menu bar never gets it.
- `align-items: center` applies outside the @media too. Below 1000px, and in the windows fix, the toolbox is a column and the menu bar is its own row. There the labels are centred rather than top-aligned in that row (content height, or --tabstrip-min-height with the custom titlebar), which is harmless.
- It does not depend on Nova, density or lightweight themes. Touch and compact were re-measured.
- Vertical tabs: the nav-bar is `width: 100% !important`, so the menu bar already wraps onto its own row in HEAD. Popup, mini and taskbar windows hide the menu bar (browser-shared.css:505-508). Fullscreen collapses it (no fullscreentoolbar attribute).

The optional part also works as described. It turns the 349px sideways jump into a vertical one: the content area shrinks by the menu bar row on every Alt press. That row is 25px without the custom titlebar, and --tabstrip-min-height (about the tab row height) with it, per browser-shared.css:550-554. Stock Firefox behaves the same way, and so does Cascade today with vertical tabs. It belongs inside the existing `@media (min-width: 1000px)` block of cascade-responsive.css, not as a new @media in cascade-layout.css. cascade-responsive-windows-fix.css does not need it: its toolbox stays a column, so the menu bar already gets its own row there.
fixreview.fix_notes:
The core fix is correct, minimal and verified. Comments to add:
- Explain the 1px min-width.
- Explain the 100px customize-mode min-width.
- Explain that Firefox top-aligns #main-menubar (browser.css:20-23).

The optional part works and is consistent with Cascade's vertical-tabs behaviour. Keep it optional: the page reflows on each Alt press, which some keyboard users may like less than the toolbar sliding. If adopted, put it in cascade-responsive.css inside the existing @media block; it is not needed in the windows fix.

Side note: once the inactive menu bar has 0 width, the `- 1px` in `#TabsToolbar { width: calc(100vw - var(--uc-urlbar-min-width) - 1px) }` has no purpose. In fact every #TabsToolbar width in cascade-responsive.css is ignored, because xul.css forces `flex: 1 !important` on it. That belongs to a separate cleanup.

title: `#nav-bar.browser-titlebar` is redundant and the 'popup windows' comment is wrong (popups match only [tabs-hidden])
problem: Both responsive files match `#navigator-toolbox[tabs-hidden] #nav-bar, #nav-bar.browser-titlebar` and label `.browser-titlebar` as the popup case (cascade-responsive.css:45-51, windows-fix:25-31). In FF160 that class is added only when the custom titlebar is on and the tab bar is hidden, so it never occurs without [tabs-hidden]. Popups disable the custom titlebar and are matched by [tabs-hidden] alone. The extra selector adds nothing and the comment misleads maintainers. (The [tabs-hidden] selector itself is correct for FF160 and also covers the new mini windows and taskbar tabs.)
evidence:
tab-bar-visibility.js:9-25 computes `hideTabsToolbar = (isSingleTabWindow && hasSingleTab) || hasVerticalTabs`, with isSingleTabWindow = popup, taskbar tab or mini window. Line 30 `CustomTitlebar.allowedBy("non-popup", !(isPopup && hasSingleTab))`, line 36 `gNavToolbox.toggleAttribute("tabs-hidden", hideTabsToolbar)`, lines 41-48 `let isTitlebar = CustomTitlebar.enabled && hideTabsToolbar; ... classList.toggle("browser-titlebar", isTitlebar)`. With Nova this also applies to #PersonalToolbar.
Harness: a 1200x500 popup (openDialog without toolbar) has tabs-hidden=true, nav-bar [0,0,1200,40], URL bar 1189px, both unfocused and focused.

refute.reasoning: The redundancy is real, but this is a maintainability nit, not a bug. In tab-bar-visibility.js, line 36 `gNavToolbox.toggleAttribute("tabs-hidden", hideTabsToolbar)` and lines 40-48 `let isTitlebar = CustomTitlebar.enabled && hideTabsToolbar; ... classList.toggle("browser-titlebar", isTitlebar)` run in the same update() call. Nothing else sets either one: rg over fxsrc finds no other `browser-titlebar` toggle and no other `tabs-hidden` setter. So `#nav-bar.browser-titlebar` implies `#navigator-toolbox[tabs-hidden]`, and the second selector never matches anything the first one misses. Single-tab popups also turn the custom titlebar off (line 30, `CustomTitlebar.allowedBy("non-popup", !(isPopup && hasSingleTab))`), so they are matched only through [tabs-hidden]. Removing the selector changes no rendering, which is why 'bug' overstates it. The comment ('native vertical tabs and popup windows') describes the whole rule, and popups are covered, so it is incomplete rather than wrong: it leaves out mini windows and taskbar tabs (line 12: `isSingleTabWindow = isPopup || isTaskbarTab || isMiniWindow`), which [tabs-hidden] also covers. The same applies to cascade-responsive-windows-fix.css:28-31.
refute.fix_notes: Dropping `#nav-bar.browser-titlebar` and updating the comment to list vertical tabs, popups, mini windows and taskbar tabs is safe and changes nothing visually. The proposed block also adds `#nav-bar[customizing] { width: 100% !important }`. That line is not explained by this finding and changes customize mode: the nav-bar takes the full row and the tab strip wraps to a second row. The selector itself exists (CustomizeMode.sys.mjs:533-538 sets [customizing] on the nav-bar). Leave that line out of this change or justify it in a separate finding.

fixreview.reasoning:
The redundancy is real. tab-bar-visibility.js is the only code that touches either `tabs-hidden` or the nav-bar's `browser-titlebar` class (checked with rg on .js, .mjs and .xhtml).
- Line 36 toggles `tabs-hidden` to hideTabsToolbar.
- Lines 41-48, in the same update() call, set `browser-titlebar` on #nav-bar to `CustomTitlebar.enabled && hideTabsToolbar`.
- So `#nav-bar.browser-titlebar` can never match without `#navigator-toolbox[tabs-hidden]`.
- Popups turn the custom titlebar off (line 30), so they are matched only by [tabs-hidden]. The comment is wrong.
- The static `browser-titlebar` class on #toolbar-menubar and #TabsToolbar (browser.xhtml:5830, :6268) does not matter, because the selector names #nav-bar.

Removing the selector and fixing the comment is correct in both files and changes no behaviour.

The proposal also slips in `#nav-bar[customizing]`. That is a customize-mode layout change from a different oneline finding and is not motivated here. The instruction "Do the same in the windows fix" is wrong for that part. In cascade-responsive-windows-fix.css, `#nav-bar[customizing] { margin: 0 !important }` moves the nav-bar to its own row below the tabs. But #TabsToolbar keeps `margin-inline-start: var(--uc-urlbar-min-width) !important` (windows-fix:13-15), which leaves an empty 35vw gap at the left of the tab row in customize mode.
fixreview.fix_notes: For this finding, only remove `#nav-bar.browser-titlebar` and correct the comment, in both files. Drop `#nav-bar[customizing]` from this fix. It belongs to the customize-mode finding and should be judged there. If that change is adopted, the windows fix also needs `#TabsToolbar[customizing] { margin-inline-start: 0 !important; }`. Without it the tab row keeps a 35vw empty gap (verified).

title: Little window-drag space on Windows/Linux CSD: every .titlebar-spacer is hidden, so with many tabs only the 28px tab-strip spring is left
problem: With the custom titlebar (the default on Windows, and on Linux with CSD), the one-line row is the window's titlebar. cascade-layout.css:64-66 hides every `.titlebar-spacer` with `display: none !important`, including the 40px pre-tabs drag spacer in #TabsToolbar. The default config also hides the caption buttons (cascade-config.css:32-34). Once the tabs fill the strip, the only places left to drag the window are the default spring at the end of the tab strip (28px) and the nav-bar springs beside the URL bar, which shrink to 1-10px. A user who removes that spring in customize mode has almost nothing to grab.
evidence:
Markup: browser.xhtml:6277 `<hbox class="titlebar-spacer" type="pre-tabs"/>` in #TabsToolbar; #vertical-spacer also carries the class (:6421).
Firefox already hides these spacers when they are not needed: browser-shared.css:428-460 hides them without customtitlebar, in fullscreen, when maximized on Windows/Linux, and with vertical tabs.
Drag rules: xul.css:278-280 `toolbar:not([nowindowdrag], [customizing]) { -moz-window-dragging: drag; }`; toolbarspring is not in the no-drag list at xul.css:283-294. Default TabsToolbar placements include "spring" (CustomizableUI.sys.mjs:414-417), with min-width 28px (toolbarbuttons.css:670-676). Nav-bar springs `min-width: 1px` (:684-687); measured 10px each at 1400px.
The many-tabs screenshot leaves about 30px after the '+' button.

refute.reasoning:
Most of the factual premise is right. cascade-layout.css:64-66 hides every .titlebar-spacer, #TabsToolbar holds only a `pre-tabs` spacer (browser.xhtml:6277), and the TabsToolbar spring has `min-width: 28px; max-width: 112px` (toolbarbuttons.css:666-676). Nav-bar springs can shrink to 1px (toolbarbuttons.css:684-687), and toolbarspring is not in the no-drag list (xul.css:283-294). But the problem is narrow, and the proposed knob adds nothing Firefox does not already offer.
(1) Firefox itself hides the pre-tabs spacer whenever the window is maximized on Windows, and when maximized or tiled on Linux (browser-shared.css:437-449). So stock Firefox maximized has the same 'spring plus nothing' drag area with many tabs. The difference only exists in restored, custom-titlebar windows whose tabs overflow. With few tabs, the empty part of the tab strip stays draggable: no no-drag rule covers #tabbrowser-tabs, and the only no-drag rules in tabs.css are for split-view wrappers (:1540) and group labels (:2263).
(2) Users who want more drag space can already drop a Flexible Space wherever they like in Customize mode. Cascade never touches toolbarspring, and each spring in the tab strip gets at least 28px (up to 112px). That is the native, placeable equivalent of a 40px spacer. A config knob that defaults to 0px and only affects restored CSD windows is extra surface for a niche that is already solved. Also, with the default `--uc-urlbar-position: 1`, the pre-tabs spacer would land between the URL bar and the tabs, an odd spot that a Flexible Space lets the user choose better.
This is a nice-to-have, not a genuine improvement for a minimal theme, so it does not meet the bar.
refute.fix_notes: The CSS would work: a user `!important` width beats the author `width: 40px`, and Firefox's own display rules still hide the spacer when maximized, in fullscreen and without CSD. But it adds a knob, in both config files plus a :where default, for something Customize → Flexible Space already provides, with no change for anyone who leaves it at 0px. If anything, add a one-line README tip: on Windows/CSD with the window buttons hidden, drag a Flexible Space into the tab strip to get more window-drag area.
refute.better_fix: No CSS change. Optionally add a note to the README or config comment next to the `.titlebar-buttonbox-container` rule: 'Window buttons are hidden; with many tabs open, add a Flexible Space to the tab bar (Customize Toolbar) if you need more room to drag the window.'

fixreview.reasoning:
The problem is real but narrow:
- It needs the custom titlebar (Windows by default, Linux with CSD, macOS) and a non-maximized window. Firefox itself hides the pre-tabs spacer when maximized or tiled on Windows/Linux (browser-shared.css:437-448), in fullscreen and without customtitlebar (:433-436), and with vertical tabs (:463-467).
- A maximized stock window also has only the tab-strip spring to grab.
- In FF160 #TabsToolbar has only the pre-tabs spacer (browser.xhtml:6277). The post-tabs spacer (:6805), the nav-bar pre-tabs spacer (:6389) and #vertical-spacer (:6421) are all in #nav-bar.

The proposed knob works:
- `width: ... !important` is needed to beat `.titlebar-spacer { width: 40px }` (browser-shared.css:428-431, author).
- It sets only width, so Firefox's own display:none rules keep working.
- At 0px the spacer is displayed at 0 width: no layout change and no gap, because #TabsToolbar has no flex gap.
- The spacer drags the window like any non-interactive child of the toolbar (xul.css:278-280, browser-shared.css:390-391).
- The `:where(:root)` default keeps older configs working.

Refinements:
- The config comment "between the URL Bar and the tabs" is only true for `--uc-urlbar-position: 1`. With 3 (tabs on the left) the spacer sits at the window's left edge. Say "in front of the tabs".
- `#nav-bar .titlebar-spacer` covers the nav-bar's pre-tabs, post-tabs and #vertical-spacer in one selector (#vertical-spacer is a descendant, not a child), keeping today's behaviour there.
- The mouse-friendly config could reasonably default to Firefox's 40px, since dragging the window is a mouse action. That is the maintainer's call; 0px keeps the current look.
fixreview.fix_notes: The fix works as proposed (verified). Apart from the refinements above, both config files need the knob declared next to the other tab bar knobs, with the same comment.

title: Status panel label sits flush against the page edge when it flips to the right (mirror state, and always in RTL locales)
problem: Cascade gives the label a left margin only: `margin: 0 0 var(--uc-status-panel-spacing) var(--uc-status-panel-spacing) !important`. Firefox moves #statuspanel to `right: 0` whenever the mouse touches the panel (the mirror state) and permanently in RTL locales. In that position the label has 12px of space below it and 0px to its right, so it touches the right edge of the rounded page. Hovering a link near the bottom-left corner flips the panel, so this happens often. The `--uc-status-panel-spacing` knob only works on one side.
evidence: Firefox 160 tabbrowser/content-area.css:691-695 `&:not([mirror]):-moz-locale-dir(rtl), &[mirror]:-moz-locale-dir(ltr) { left: auto; right: 0; }`. status-panel.js:132-153: onMouseEnter/onMouseLeave call _mirror(), which toggles `mirror` and sets `sizelimit`. Firefox's own spacing is per side (content-area.css:763-791: `margin-right: 1em` when the label is on the left, `margin-left: 1em` when it is on the right). Cascade's user-origin !important `margin` replaces both of them. The panel sits inside .browserStack: Tabbrowser.sys.mjs:1337-1342 `browser.insertAdjacentElement("afterend", StatusPanel.panel)`, and xul.css:467-470 gives `stack { position: relative }`, so `right: 0` is the page's right edge. getComputedStyle probe after StatusPanel._mirror(): label rect [1162.1, 762, 231.9, 20]. Its right edge is 1394, exactly the .browserStack right edge (6+1388). margin-left 12px, margin-right 0px. Screenshot: agents/content/shots/p6-mirror-head.png (crop agents/content/mcmp.png, top). The status-panel rules are also split across two files: the border and radius are in cascade-layout.css:89-92, the margin is in cascade-floating-panel.css.

refute.reasoning: Firefox moves #statuspanel to the right edge in the mirror state, and always in RTL. The relevant rule is tabbrowser/content-area.css:691-695 `&:not([mirror]):-moz-locale-dir(rtl), &[mirror]:-moz-locale-dir(ltr) { left: auto; right: 0; }`. status-panel.js:132-153 toggles `mirror` from onMouseEnter/onMouseLeave (MousePosTracker), so a real mouse over the label flips it. Firefox's own spacing is per side (content-area.css:763-791: margin-right:1em on the left, margin-left:1em on the right). Cascade's user-origin `!important` shorthand at cascade-floating-panel.css:2 replaces both with `0 0 12px 12px`, which leaves 0px on the right. The panel sits in .browserStack (Tabbrowser.sys.mjs:1337-1342; my probe gives parent `browserStack`), so `right:0` is the page edge. I reproduced it with a real xdotool mouse move rather than by calling _mirror().
refute.fix_notes: The symmetric `margin: 0 var(--uc-status-panel-spacing) var(--uc-status-panel-spacing) !important` works: verified at 12px in the mirror state, and the non-mirrored state is unchanged at x=18. #statuspanel has max-width calc(100% - 5px), or 50% with [sizelimit], so both margins fit. Moving the border/radius rule from cascade-layout.css:89-92 into cascade-floating-panel.css is a good small cleanup.

title: Split view shrinks the floating-page gap to 2px on ordinary tabs while any split view exists
problem: The reduced split-view padding is keyed on the `[splitview]` attribute. Firefox keeps that attribute on #tabbrowser-tabpanels as long as a split view exists anywhere in the window, even when a normal tab is selected. On such a tab the dormant split panels are hidden and the page gets no 4px panel margin. The page therefore sits 2px from the window edges instead of 6px, and the gap changes as you move between tabs.
evidence: content-area.css:46-52 (Nova comment): "the suspended state — where #tabbrowser-tabpanels still has [splitview] (because suspended split-view panels remain in the tabbox) but the currently-selected tab is a non-split-view one". content-area.css:457-468: `.split-view-panel:not(.split-view-panel-active) { display: none; }` and `.split-view-panel.split-view-panel-active { margin: var(--space-xsmall); }`, so only active split panels bring the 4px. Cascade: `#tabbrowser-tabbox:has(> #tabbrowser-tabpanels[splitview]) { padding-inline: max(0px, calc(var(--uc-content-margin) - 4px)) !important; padding-block-end: … }`. Probe in Firefox 160: split tabs 2 and 3, then select tab 5. Result: `splitview=""`, panel classes `browserSidebarContainer split-view-panel` (no -active), tabbox padding 2px, page rect [2, 44, 1396, 754] instead of [6, 44, 1388, 750]. Screenshot agents/content/shots/p5-suspended-head.png. Side-by-side crop agents/content/susp-vs-normal.png: left is suspended (2px), right is normal (6px). Separately, active split panels also start about 3px lower than a normal page (rect y=47.3 vs 44) because the 4px margin also applies at the top.

refute.reasoning: content-area.css:457-468 hides dormant split panels (`.split-view-panel:not(.split-view-panel-active) { display:none }`) and gives the 4px margin only to `.split-view-panel.split-view-panel-active`. The Nova comment at content-area.css:46-52 says explicitly that #tabbrowser-tabpanels keeps [splitview] while a non-split tab is selected. Cascade's reduced padding at cascade-layout.css:102 is keyed on the attribute alone, so a normal tab in that state gets 2px and no 4px margin.
refute.fix_notes: Verified in Firefox 160. The optional `margin-block-start: 0 !important` on active split panels is reasonable to remove the ~3px vertical jump (the panel margin is 3.33px, not 4px, because --space-xsmall is 0.25rem).

title: Tab-modal dialog backdrop keeps square corners and darkens the gap around the rounded page
problem: When a tab-modal prompt is open (alert/confirm, "leave page?", HTTP auth, some print and permission dialogs), its semi-transparent backdrop is not clipped by the page's rounded corners. The square backdrop corners darken the floating gap, which leaves a black wedge at each corner of the page. Cascade only clips `.browserContainer`, but the dialog stack is not inside it.
evidence: browser.js:4471-4475 `static _containerFor(browser) { return browser.closest(".browserSidebarContainer, .webextension-popup-stack, .sidebar-browser-stack"); }`, and browser.js:4481-4485 appends the .dialogStack there. It is a sibling of .browserContainer, so Cascade's `#tabbrowser-tabpanels .browserContainer { border-radius…; overflow: clip !important }` (cascade-layout.css:110-113) does not clip it. The stack is anchored to the <browser> (content-area.css:876-893, 406-409). Nova sets `#tabbrowser-tabpanels > :not(.split-view-panel) .dialogOverlay[topmost="true"] { border-radius: 0; }` (content-area.css:1062-1065) and rounds only the start corners when a sidebar is shown (1067-1080). Firefox's own comment at 1045 reads "Radius the backdrop so it doesnt occlude the radiused .browserContainer below it". The backdrop is `background-color: var(--background-color-overlay)` (1057-1060), computed oklch(0 0 0 / 0.5). Probe with Services.prompt.asyncAlert(..., MODAL_TYPE_TAB, ...): stack parent is `browserSidebarContainer deck-selected`, overlay border-top-left-radius 0px. Crop agents/content/d9.png, left half: square black wedge at the page's top-left corner. Full shot: agents/content/shots/p9-dialog-head.png.

refute.reasoning: The .dialogStack is appended to the .browserSidebarContainer, not to .browserContainer, so Cascade's `overflow: clip` + radius on .browserContainer (cascade-layout.css:110-113) does not clip it. The backdrop `.dialogOverlay[topmost="true"] { background-color: var(--background-color-overlay) }` (content-area.css:1057-1060) is anchored to the <browser> rect (content-area.css:876-893) and Nova forces `border-radius: 0` on it for non-split panels (content-area.css:1062-1065). Its square corners therefore darken the frame-coloured wedges outside the rounded page corners.
refute.fix_notes: Placing the rule inside the non-fullscreen floating-page block is correct, and Firefox's own fullscreen `border-radius: 0` still applies there. Clipping .browserSidebarContainer would cut off the dialog's -5px top overlap, so the overlay-radius approach is the right one. There is one cosmetic detail without content-06's border removal: the overlay starts 1px below the container (y=45 vs 44), so its 8px radius is a hair rounder than the 8x7 padding-box curve. That difference is negligible.

title: macOS: overlay scrollbars run into the rounded page corners
problem: On macOS, Firefox moves the content scrollbars away from any corner it rounds by setting inset custom properties, which the <browser> forwards into the page. Cascade rounds all four corners of every page but never sets these insets. On macOS the vertical scrollbar's ends get cut by the top-right and bottom-right curves, and the horizontal scrollbar's ends by the bottom corners. Firefox's own rounding (start corner with a sidebar, split panels) does set them.
evidence: content-area.css:213-223: "This container rounds and clips the content area, but the scrollbar being clipped belongs to the content document inside <browser>. Every rule below that sets a border-radius here must set the matching inset, which browser[type=\"content\"] forwards into the content document" (defaults are `--content-scrollbar-inset-*: 0` on macOS). content-area.css:435-440 `@media (-moz-platform: macos) { browser[type="content"] { -moz-scrollbar-inset-block: var(--content-scrollbar-inset-block); -moz-scrollbar-inset-inline: var(--content-scrollbar-inset-inline-start) var(--content-scrollbar-inset-inline-end); } }`. Firefox sets the insets only for corners it rounds (53-66, 85-124) and for split panels on all sides (504-516, 580-584). Cascade sets border-radius on every .browserContainer and never touches these properties. Source analysis only: the harness is Linux and cannot show macOS overlay scrollbars.

refute.reasoning: The mechanism is real. .browserContainer insets default to 0 on macOS (content-area.css:219-223), browser[type=content] forwards them (435-440), and Cascade rounds every corner without touching the insets. But the finding misdescribes the default Nova case. Content-area.css:56-60 (inside the Nova block, for every non-split .browserContainer, with no sidebar needed) already sets `--content-scrollbar-inset-block: 0 var(--border-radius-medium); --content-scrollbar-inset-inline-start/end: var(--border-radius-medium)`. So with Nova on and no sidebar, the bottom end of the vertical scrollbar and both ends of the horizontal scrollbar are already inset by at least 8px. Only the top end of the vertical scrollbar (block-start 0) runs into Cascade's top-right curve. The fuller exposure the finding describes happens in narrower cases. With a sidebar open, Firefox zeroes the inset on the sidebar side: lines 91-92 set inline-start 0, and lines 108-111 set inline-end 0 and block-end 0, while Cascade still rounds those corners. With Nova off, every inset is 0. I could not test on macOS here.
refute.fix_notes: The proposed overrides are harmless and do cover the real gaps: the top end in default Nova, the sidebar-side corners, and Nova off. User !important beats Firefox's author custom-property declarations on .browserContainer, and the rule is correctly gated to the non-fullscreen block. I verified that `@media (-moz-platform: …)` works in userChrome: a linux probe matched and a macos probe did not. The finding's description of the scope should be corrected to say that by default only the vertical scrollbar's top end is affected.

title: Window controls hidden unconditionally (both configs, in fullscreen too, with overlap on macOS); make it a knob
problem:
`.titlebar-buttonbox-container { display: none !important; }` is active in both configs. What users lose:
- On Windows (Firefox draws its own title bar by default) and on Linux when Firefox draws its own title bar (GNOME/Wayland, or "Title Bar" unchecked in Customize): no minimise, maximise or close buttons at all. Also no restore/close in the fullscreen toolbox, since Firefox shows the controls there too. Only keyboard shortcuts or the WM menu remain.
- The mouse config hides them as well, which contradicts its purpose.
- On macOS the box is only the placeholder that reserves room for the native traffic lights, which macOS keeps drawing. Hiding it lets the first toolbar items (the sidebar and reload buttons in the oneline layout) slide underneath them.
- Together with `.titlebar-spacer { display: none }` (cascade-layout.css:64-66), the window can only be dragged by the small empty gaps in the toolbars. With many tabs the tab strip has no free space (harness shots/strip-many-tabs.png).
The only workaround today is to edit the config or turn the system title bar on.
evidence: browser-shared.css:404-427: `.titlebar-buttonbox-container { order: 1000; @media (-moz-platform: macos) and (not (-moz-mac-rtl)) { &:-moz-locale-dir(ltr) { order: -1; } } … :root:not([customtitlebar], [inFullscreen]) & { display: none; } }`. browser-shared.css:491-497 `.titlebar-buttonbox { … :root:not([customtitlebar], [sizemode="fullscreen"]) & { display: none; } }`. browser-shared.css:482-484 shows them only in the first visible toolbar. So with a system title bar the rule changes nothing; it only removes controls when Firefox draws its own. Probe (customtitlebar/inFullscreen attributes simulated, because Xvfb has no window manager): stock Firefox 160 gives `TabsToolbar:flex [1285.5,0,114.5,44]`, with min/max/close visible (agents/content/ctb-stock-z.png), and with inFullscreen+sizemode=fullscreen still `TabsToolbar:flex`. Cascade gives `TabsToolbar:none` in both cases. The macOS overlap follows from the native buttons being placed from this box; it cannot be reproduced on this Linux build, so that part has medium confidence.

refute.reasoning: The facts check out. browser-shared.css:404-427 shows .titlebar-buttonbox-container only when `[customtitlebar]` or `[inFullscreen]` (`:root:not([customtitlebar], [inFullscreen]) & { display: none }`). Cascade's unconditional `display:none !important` (cascade-config.css:31-34, cascade-config-mouse.css:37-40) therefore only ever removes controls Firefox would draw. That covers Windows by default, Linux CSD, and the fullscreen toolbox, and the mouse config does it too. Hiding them in the keyboard config is Cascade's deliberate minimalist choice (commented 'remove window control buttons'), and users can delete the rule, so that part is taste. The real improvements are narrower. The mouse config arguably should keep them. On macOS, hiding the -moz-window-button-box placeholder plausibly lets the native traffic lights overlap the first nav-bar items, but I cannot verify that on this Linux build, and neither could the finding. The proposed macOS exception has an unverified side effect: in the oneline layout the box lives at the start of #TabsToolbar (order:-1 on macOS), so the native buttons may end up mid-toolbar rather than at the window edge.
refute.fix_notes: The knob + `@container style(--uc-window-controls: none)` + `@media not (-moz-platform: macos)` works on Linux as described (verified both values). It is heavier than Cascade's usual convention for optional hide rules, which is a plain or commented rule in the config file. The macOS behaviour of the exception is unverified.
refute.better_fix: Keep Cascade's config convention. In both config files wrap the existing rule as `@media not (-moz-platform: macos) { .titlebar-buttonbox-container { display: none !important; } }` (fixes the macOS overlap). In cascade-config-mouse.css comment it out, like back/forward are there, so mouse users keep the controls. No new knob or container query is needed.

title: Floating page is practically invisible in light mode, with vertical tabs and on dark websites: add an outline knob
problem:
The floating page relies only on the colour difference between page and frame:
- Light palette: frame #fafafc against the usual white page, a contrast of about 1.04. The gap and the rounded corners do not show at all (before/light.png). With vertical tabs the page merges into the sidebar (before/vertical-light.png).
- Dark palette: dark websites (#0f0f0f to #1e1e1e) blend into the #1e2021 frame.
- Nova vs Nova-off: Nova removes Firefox's card shadow and outline from the page, while Nova-off (sidebar.revamp) keeps a box-shadow, so the two look different.
- Nova's 1px top/inline separator borders are made transparent by Cascade but still take space. The page content starts 1px below its rounded box (browser y=45, container y=44), which shows as a 1px frame-coloured line at the top once any edge is drawn.
evidence: content-area.css:53-70 (Nova): `#tabbrowser-tabpanels > :not(.split-view-panel) .browserContainer { … outline: none; box-shadow: none; border-block-start: var(--border-width) solid var(--chrome-content-separator-color); }`, and 85-105 add border-inline-start/end with a sidebar. Nova-off with revamp: content-area.css:366-369 `outline: 0.01px solid var(--chrome-content-separator-color); box-shadow: var(--content-area-shadow);`. Cascade sets `--chrome-content-separator-color: transparent !important` (cascade-layout.css:27), so every separator is invisible. Probe: bc box-shadow `none`, outline-style `none`, border-top-width 1px transparent, browser rect y=45 vs bc y=44. Crops: agents/content/lcmp.png left (light, edge invisible) and agents/content/dcmp.png left (page #101010 on frame #1e2021).

refute.reasoning: The floating page that was just added is effectively invisible in the default light palette. The frame --uc-base-colour #fafafc against a white page gives a contrast of about 1.04, and the gap/corners do not read. Cascade also makes every Nova separator transparent (cascade-layout.css:27 `--chrome-content-separator-color: transparent !important`), and Nova removes the card outline and shadow for non-split pages (content-area.css:53-70 `outline: none; box-shadow: none; border-block-start: var(--border-width) solid var(--chrome-content-separator-color)`). So nothing delimits the page. The 1px transparent top border still takes space (browser y=45 vs container y=44). Nova-off with sidebar.revamp (default true, firefox.js:869) keeps `box-shadow: var(--content-area-shadow)` (content-area.css:366-369), so the two modes do differ. A palette-derived hairline knob that can be set to transparent is a small change in line with Cascade's style that makes the feature work in light mode. Leaving it on by default in dark mode is a taste call, but the knob covers that.
refute.fix_notes: Verified in Firefox 160. User !important beats Nova's author outline:none and the border declarations, and the rule targets only `> :not(.split-view-panel) > .browserContainer`, so the selected split pane keeps its focus ring. It sits inside the non-fullscreen block. Add the `:where(:root)` default as proposed. With --uc-content-margin: 0 the outline would draw outside the tabbox, so the comment telling users to set it transparent then is needed.

title: Status panel label and split-view footer use system dialog colours, not the palette; the borderless label disappears on matching pages
problem:
Cascade only removes the label's border and rounds it. Its colours stay Firefox's:
- On Linux they are GTK `-moz-dialog`/`-moz-dialogText`.
- On Windows and macOS they are a fixed light-dark grey that follows the content colour scheme, not the chrome.
So the label does not match the default palette, and colour integrations (catppuccin, nord, gruvbox, …) never reach it. Without a border, a dark label over a dark site (or a light label over a light site) has no edge. The address footer of an inactive split pane uses the same Firefox rule and shows a third grey.
evidence: content-area.css:738-751: `#statuspanel-label, split-view-footer { color-scheme: env(-moz-content-preferred-color-scheme); background-color: -moz-dialog; border-color: ThreeDShadow; color: -moz-dialogText; @media (not (prefers-contrast)) and (not (-moz-platform: linux)) { background-color: light-dark(#f9f9fa, hsl(240, 1%, 20%)); … } }`. Probes on Linux: dark gives label background rgb(54,54,58) and colour #fff, against palette #1e2021/#fafafc. Light gives rgb(246,245,244)/rgb(46,52,54), against #fafafc/#1e2021. Cascade has `border: none !important`. Crops: agents/content/dcmp.png left (label on a #101010 page) and agents/content/split-footer.png (footer grey vs frame).

title: Split view decoration ignores Cascade: blue active-pane ring and 12px clip on the inactive pane
problem:
Two parts of the split view do not follow Cascade.
- The active pane gets Firefox's 2px focus ring in the system accent blue (rgb(53,132,228) under GTK), which clashes with Cascade's palette. The same blue appears on the find bar field and the sidebar search box focus rings, and on the hovered splitter.
- Nova clips the inactive pane with its own 12px radius while Cascade rounds the page box to 8px. The two panes have different corners, and setting `--uc-content-border-radius: 0px` still leaves the inactive pane rounded.
evidence: Ring: content-area.css:524-527 `&.deck-selected > .browserContainer { z-index: 1; outline: var(--focus-outline); }` and 592-598 (Nova) `border-color: var(--focus-outline-color); outline-width: calc(var(--focus-outline-width) - var(--border-width));`. Splitter hover at 143-145 is `background-color: var(--focus-outline-color)`. tokens-shared.css:368-369 composes `--focus-outline: var(--focus-outline-width) solid var(--focus-outline-color); --focus-outline-color: var(--color-accent-primary);` on :root, and tokens-platform.css:34 sets `--color-accent-primary: AccentColor`. Cascade sets --focus-outline-color only inside menupopup/panel (cascade-panels.css:34). Clip: content-area.css:471-480 `:root:not([inDOMFullscreen]) & > .split-view-panel:not(.deck-selected) { overflow: clip; @media -moz-pref("browser.nova.enabled") { border-radius: var(--border-radius-medium); } }`, and Nova sets --border-radius-medium to 12px (tokens-shared.css:765/782). Probe: active ring rgb(53,132,228). Inactive panel `12px:clip` while its .browserContainer is 8px. Screenshot before/split.png. Nova answer: Nova rounds the page itself only at the start corner when a sidebar or AI window is shown (content-area.css:85-114, 12px), which Cascade's all-corner !important radius overrides cleanly. The leftovers that still double up are this split-panel clip, the dialog backdrop and the separator borders (separate findings).

title: Find bar: the olive field is Firefox's first-use flash, but the bar stays off-palette and the page loses its bottom corners
problem:
The olive/yellow find field in shots/before/findbar.png is not a Cascade colour bug. It is Firefox's one-time "flash" when the find bar is first used in a profile: three yellow pulses over 3s, caught mid-pulse at 1.5s. What does persist:
- The "not found" state is a fixed pink tint.
- The focus ring is the system blue (covered by the split-view finding).
- The find bar is a row inside the rounded page box with the frame colour. While it is open, the page's bottom corners are square and the rounded corners belong to the find bar.
evidence: findbar.css:125-133: `&[status="notfound"] { background-color: rgba(226, 40, 80, 0.3); }` and `&[flash="true"] { background-color: rgba(255, 233, 0, 0.3); }`. findbar.js:1149-1154 starts `setInterval(() => this._flash(), 500)` and decrements `accessibility.typeaheadfind.flashBar`. firefox.js:491 sets `pref("accessibility.typeaheadfind.flashBar", 1)`. findbar.js:1047-1062 alternates flash true/false for 6 ticks, then removes the attribute. Probe: `flash` was set at about 1.5s and gone (null) at 5s. Field background is rgb(46,49,51), i.e. --uc-urlbar-colour, under the yellow. The find bar sits in the grid row of .browserContainer (content-area.css:244-251, 308-310), and browser-shared.css:810-813 gives it `background-color: var(--toolbar-background-color)`. Probe: find bar rect [6, 749, 1388, 45] inside the page box [6, 44, 1388, 750]. before/findbar.png shows square page corners at y=749.

title: Selected tab never shows a keyboard focus ring (and the ring is Firefox blue, focused inactive tabs stay dimmed)
problem: When you Tab into the tab strip, keyboard focus lands on the active tab first. Cascade's `.tabbrowser-tab[selected]:not([multiselected]) .tab-background { outline: none !important }` deletes Firefox's focus outline on exactly that tab, so you can't see where focus is. This is a real problem for a theme sold as 'keyboard centered'. Once you arrow away to another tab the ring does appear, but it is Firefox's/the system's blue, not the accent colour. That tab also stays dimmed at --uc-inactive-opacity, so the item that has focus looks less important than the tabs around it. Happens horizontal and vertical, Nova on and off.
evidence: FF160 tabs.css:1199-1202 `#tabbrowser-tabs[tablist-has-focus] .tabbrowser-tab.tablist-keyboard-focus > .tab-stack > .tab-background { outline: var(--focus-outline); outline-offset: var(--focus-outline-inset); }` is author-normal, so the user `!important` `outline: none` at cascade-tabs.css:107-109 wins. tabs.mjs:668-677 on_focusin: when the selectedItem gets focus it sets `tablistHasFocus = true` and `ariaFocusedItem = this.selectedItem`, so the first focus target is always the selected tab. Harness probe (focus on gBrowser.selectedTab with FLAG_BYKEY): tablist-has-focus=true, .tablist-keyboard-focus=true, computed `outline-style: none`. Screenshot agents/tabs/probe/h-kbfocus-selected.png shows no ring. After moving ariaFocusedItem to tabs[5]: outline solid rgb(53,132,228) (system blue, from tokens-shared.css:369 `--focus-outline-color: var(--color-accent-primary)`) and `.tab-content` opacity 0.65. Also see shots/before/tab-focus-ring.png (blue ring). Setting `--focus-outline-color` on #tabbrowser-tabs does NOT help: `--focus-outline` (tokens-shared.css:368) is already resolved on :root with the root colour, which I confirmed in a probe.

refute.reasoning: I reproduced this with real key presses. Starting in the URL bar, three shift+Tab presses (searchmode switcher, then sidebar-button) land on gBrowser.selectedTab. At that point #tabbrowser-tabs has [tablist-has-focus] and the tab has .tablist-keyboard-focus, but the computed outline-style of its .tab-background is none. The cause is Cascade's user !important `outline: none` at cascade-tabs.css:107-109, which beats FF160's author-normal focus rule. The problem is worse than described: plain arrow keys go through tabbox.js on_keydown and advanceSelectedTab, so they select the next tab, and the focused item is always the selected tab. Only Ctrl+Arrow (tabs.mjs #advanceFocus) moves focus to a tab that is not selected. When I moved with ctrl+Right, the focused background tab got outline solid 2px rgb(53,132,228) (system accent) and its .tab-content kept opacity 0.65. The same happened with Nova off. A group label focused with ctrl+Right also showed the blue ring. The point about --focus-outline is also right: tokens-shared.css:368 declares `--focus-outline` on :root, so it is substituted there, and overriding --focus-outline-color lower in the tree has no effect. I also checked the side effect of the fix: a mouse click on the selected tab does not focus it (tablist-has-focus false), so mouse users see no new ring.
refute.fix_notes: I applied the fix and checked it. `:root{--tab-border-color-selected:transparent !important}` keeps the selected tab without a ring when it is not focused (outline-color rgba(0,0,0,0)), and the user !important also beats `&[lwtheme]` at tabs.css:71. After the fix, the keyboard-focused selected tab shows outline solid 2px rgb(120,111,166) (the accent), the ctrl+Right focused tab shows the accent with opacity 1, and the group label shows the accent ring. One thing to watch: the opacity reset as proposed targets `:is(.tab-label-container, .tab-icon-image)`, which only works together with the agent's dimming rewrite. Against the current file, which dims `.tab-content`, the reset has to be `#tabbrowser-tabs[tablist-has-focus] .tabbrowser-tab.tablist-keyboard-focus .tab-content { opacity: 1 !important }`. That is the variant I tested.

fixreview.reasoning:
The problem is real. Firefox draws the tab keyboard focus ring with author-normal `outline: var(--focus-outline)` (tabs.css:1199-1202). Cascade's user `!important` `outline: none` on `.tabbrowser-tab[selected]:not([multiselected]) .tab-background` (cascade-tabs.css:107-109) beats it. on_focusin (tabs.mjs:668-677) makes the selected tab the first keyboard-focus target, so the first thing you reach with Tab shows no ring. Other focused tabs get the system-blue `--focus-outline` (tokens-shared.css:368-369, already resolved on :root) and stay at 0.65 opacity.

The proposed fix works. I re-ran it in FF160 with Nova on (dark), Nova off (dark and light) and compact vertical. Overriding `--tab-border-color-selected` on :root is safe: Firefox only defines it on :root (tab.tokens.css:21, `:root[lwtheme]` at tabs.css:71), so the user `!important` reaches every tab, lwtheme included.

Two weaknesses:
- The undim rule targets `.tab-label-container, .tab-icon-image` and only works together with the separate dimming rewrite. On the current file, which dims `.tab-content`, `opacity: 1` on a child does nothing because opacity multiplies down from the parent.
- The :root token also applies in every chrome document userChrome styles: the sidebar current-row outline (sidebar-tab-row.css:132, sidebar-opentabs.css:15) and the Firefox View [open] outline (tabs.css:3103). That is harmless but broader than needed.

A version that changes the outline colour only on the tab itself, with the keyboard-focus exclusion folded into the dimming selector, does the same job with no dependency and no global token. I tested it: the class `tablist-keyboard-focus` persists after blur (tabbox.js:861, tabs.mjs:693-698), but tablist-has-focus is removed, so the tab dims again correctly.
fixreview.fix_notes:
The outline part is correct and was verified in every mode tested.

The opacity part needs the dimming rewrite. If tabs-01 lands alone, the focused tab stays dimmed.

The `:root` token is broader than necessary: it also drops the current-tab outline in the sidebar documents and the Firefox View [open] outline. It works, but the scoped version below is the same size and self-contained.

title: Vertical tabs: margin-inline:0 sticks tabs to the window edge and puts the collapsed-sidebar highlight off-centre
problem: With native vertical tabs, every tab background, selected or hovered, touches the window's left edge (x=0) while its right end is inset. In the collapsed sidebar the 32px highlight square sits at x=0..32 while the favicon is at x=17..33, so the active and hover highlights are visibly 9px off-centre. In the expanded pinned grid the tiles also run into each other with no gap. Horizontal tabs gain nothing from the rule, because Firefox sets no inline margin on a horizontal .tab-background.
