In the collapsed state Firefox sizes the background `width: var(--tab-collapsed-background-width)` (tabs.css:2953-2954) and centres the icon with `--tab-padding-inline: calc((var(--tab-collapsed-width) - var(--icon-size)) / 2)` (tabs.css:2879) = 17px. That centring depends on the 9px margin. Probe (sidebar.verticalTabs): expanded selBg [0,145,242,32], bgMargin 0px. Collapsed selBg [0,186,32,32] vs icon [17,194,16,16]. Pinned tiles [4..121] adjacent. Screenshots: shots/before/vertical.png, vertical-collapsed.png, agents/tabs/probe/z-v-collapsed.png. Firefox's only horizontal inline margin on .tab-background is the split-view `margin-inline: 0` (tabs.css:1593-1595).
fix: Remove `margin-inline: 0px !important;` from cascade-tabs.css:84 (keep margin-block). Checked: expanded bg at x=9 (width 224), collapsed bg [9,186,32,32] centred on icon [17,194], pinned grid gaps restored (probe-fix/z-vexp.png, z-vcol.png).

refute.reasoning: Cascade's user !important `margin-inline: 0px` at cascade-tabs.css:84 beats FF160's author rules `#tabbrowser-tabs[orient=vertical] .tab-background { margin-inline: var(--tab-margin-inline-inner) }` (9px under Nova) and the pinned-expanded `margin-inline: var(--tab-margin-inline-pinned-expanded)`. In the collapsed state Firefox centres the icon with `--tab-padding-inline: calc((--tab-collapsed-width - --icon-size)/2)`, where --tab-collapsed-width includes 2x the inner margin, so taking the margin away moves the 32px highlight off-centre. Horizontal tabs have no inline margin on .tab-background, apart from split-view, which is already 0 in Firefox (tabs.css:1593-1595). The rule therefore only does harm.
refute.fix_notes: Deleting the one line works as shown above. Horizontal is unaffected, because Firefox sets no horizontal inline margin on .tab-background and keeps 0 inside split view by its own rule.

fixreview.reasoning:
The problem is real. cascade-tabs.css:84 sets `margin-inline: 0px !important` (user `!important`), which beats `#tabbrowser-tabs[orient="vertical"] .tab-background { margin-inline: var(--tab-margin-inline-inner) }` (tabs.css:2936-2937) and the pinned-expanded margin (tabs.css:2818-2819). The collapsed sidebar centres the icon through `--tab-padding-inline: calc((var(--tab-collapsed-width) - var(--icon-size)) / 2)` (tabs.css:2879), with `--tab-collapsed-width` = background + 2 × inner margin (tabs.css:59). That centring assumes the margin.

The only horizontal inline margin Firefox sets on `.tab-background` is the split-view `margin-inline: 0` (tabs.css:1593-1595). Removing the declaration therefore changes nothing for horizontal tabs, Nova on or off.

The fix works, and I checked it in normal and compact density. Touch density and Nova off just go back to stock Firefox values (`--tab-margin-inline-inner`: tab.tokens.css:79, tabs.css:160/170/175). It follows the convention of deferring to Firefox, and nothing else in Cascade relies on the zero margin.
fixreview.fix_notes: Correct and minimal. Delete only line 84 and keep margin-block and border-radius. There is no horizontal regression, because Firefox sets no inline margin there apart from the split-view 0.

title: Adaptive tab widths also apply to vertical tabs: inactive tabs are cut off at 200px in a wider sidebar
problem: The --uc-active-tab-width / --uc-inactive-tab-width max-widths are meant for the horizontal tab bar, but they also hit vertical tabs. In an expanded sidebar wider than about 200px, inactive tabs stop at 200px while the active tab fills the sidebar. Titles get cut off early and the hover background is visibly shorter than the selected one. The cap moves with window width (20vw), so the sidebar layout changes when you resize the window.
evidence: cascade-tabs.css:36-41 `.tabbrowser-tab[fadein]:not([selected]):not([pinned])... { max-width: var(--uc-inactive-tab-width) !important; }` has no orientation scope, and user !important beats FF160 tabs.css:3051-3055 `#tabbrowser-tabs[orient="vertical"][expanded] .tabbrowser-tab { max-width: none; }`. Probe: sidebar 242px wide, inactive tab rect width 200 (maxWidth 200px), selected 242 (maxWidth 300px). Screenshots shots/before/vertical.png ('Wikipedia, the free en' cut at x≈180 vs stock/vertical.png 'encyclop…' to x≈222) and agents/tabs/probe/z-v-expanded-hover.png (hover bg 200px vs selected 242px).

refute.reasoning: The max-width rules at cascade-tabs.css:36-41 have no orientation scope. As user !important they beat FF160's author `#tabbrowser-tabs[orient=vertical][expanded] .tabbrowser-tab { max-width: none }`. In the expanded sidebar, inactive tabs are capped at clamp(100px,20vw,200px), which is 200px at 1400px wide, while the sidebar is 242px. Titles are cut off early and the hover background is shorter than the selected one. Because the cap is in vw, it changes with window width. The scoped fix also corrects the collapsed-group exclusion. FF160 hides collapsed-group tabs with `max-width: 0 !important` (author important), which a user !important would beat, so the exclusion is needed. Today, however, it is broader than Firefox's hiding rule.
refute.fix_notes: I tested the scoped rules. Vertical maxWidth becomes none. In horizontal, the nested `#tabbrowser-tabs[orient="horizontal"] .tabbrowser-tab` still matches (tab widths unchanged in the screenshots), and Firefox itself relies on the orient attribute (tabs.css:1046). The narrower exclusions match FF160 tabs.css:2002-2005. As a side effect, the visible active tab of a collapsed group now gets Cascade's active width instead of Firefox's 225px, which is consistent with the knob.

fixreview.reasoning:
The problem is real. Cascade's max-width rules (cascade-tabs.css:36-41) have no orientation scope, and as user `!important` they beat `#tabbrowser-tabs[orient="vertical"] ... &[expanded] .tabbrowser-tab { max-width: none }` (tabs.css:3051-3055). Firefox itself only caps horizontal tabs (tabs.css:298-300: `#tabbrowser-tabs[orient="horizontal"] &:not([pinned]) { max-width: var(--tab-max-width) }`), so scoping to `[orient="horizontal"]` mirrors Firefox. The attribute is always present: browser.xhtml:6287, browser-sidebar.js:2397/2402.

The tighter collapsed-group exclusions copy tabs.css:2002-2005 correctly. Firefox's collapsed-tab hiding uses author `max-width: 0 !important`, which user `!important` would beat, so the exclusions have to match exactly, and they do: hidden tabs are `:not([visuallyselected],[multiselected])`, plus the selected tab only while `[movingtabgroup]`.

The nesting syntax is already used in Cascade. There is one tiny edge: Cascade keys on `[selected]` while Firefox hides on `[visuallyselected]`, which differ for a frame during async tab switching. This is negligible.
fixreview.fix_notes: Correct as written. Optionally, in both cascade-config.css:148-152 and cascade-config-mouse.css:153-157, change the comment to say these widths apply to the horizontal tab bar only, because vertical tabs fill the sidebar.

title: Tab group label rule matches nothing in FF160, and fixing only the selector would break contrast and focus
problem: Nothing in the 'tab group labels' block applies: no --uc-border-radius on labels, and nothing stops the label changing colour when the group collapses. With Nova off (Proton), a collapsed group still flips to the inverted colour plus outline. The declarations themselves are also wrong for FF160, so making the selector match would cause harm. `outline: none !important` would remove the keyboard focus ring on group labels (arrow-key navigation) and the Nova drag-over outline. `--tab-group-color-pale` doesn't exist under Nova, so in light mode `color` becomes invalid. In dark mode the background would switch to the dark `-invert` shade under near-black --tab-group-label-text-dark text, which is unreadable. The `!important` background also removes the Nova hover feedback.
evidence: FF160 tabgroup.mjs:87-92 markup: `<vbox class="tab-group-label-container"><vbox class="tab-group-label-hover-highlight"><label class="tab-group-label"/>`. The label is a grandchild, so `.tab-group-label-container > .tab-group-label` never matches. Probe: `labelParent: tab-group-label-hover-highlight`, `matches(cascade selector) = false`, computed border-radius `16px 16px 16px 4px` (Nova pill, tabs.css:2289-2290), not 8px. Nova off: collapsed 'Fun' label color oklch(0.97 0.05 50) on oklch(0.48 0.2 50), outline solid (tabs.css:2309-2312 `tab-group[collapsed] > .tab-group-label-container & { background-color: var(--tab-group-color-invert); ... outline: 1px solid ... }`). `--tab-group-*-pale` is defined only inside tabs.css:120-147 `@media not -moz-pref("browser.nova.enabled")`, while tabgroup.mjs:323 sets `--tab-group-color-pale: var(--tab-group-${code}-pale)`. Focus ring: tabs.css:2328-2331 `#tabbrowser-tabs[tablist-has-focus] &.tablist-keyboard-focus { outline: var(--focus-outline) }`. Nova hover: tabs.css:2292-2294. --tab-group-label-text-dark = gray-100 #15141a (tabs.css:150).

refute.reasoning: The main claim holds. In FF160 the label is a grandchild of the container (container > .tab-group-label-hover-highlight > label), so `.tab-group-label-container > .tab-group-label` never matches and the whole block is dead. Under Nova the label keeps Firefox's pill radius of 16px 16px 16px 4px. With Nova off, the collapsed 'Fun' label still switches to the inverted colours with a 1px outline. The hypothetical harms of fixing only the selector are mostly right, but one detail is wrong. `outline: none !important` would remove the keyboard focus ring and the Nova drag-over outline, and the !important background would remove the Nova :hover feedback. --tab-group-*-pale exists only under `@media not -moz-pref(browser.nova.enabled)`, so the `color` declaration is invalid at computed-value time in BOTH schemes, not only in light mode. I tested a naive selector fix in dark Nova: the text becomes the inherited rgb(250,250,252) on the -invert blue rgb(69,95,231), which is readable. It is not near-black text as the finding says. In light mode the inherited dark text on a dark --tab-group-color would have poor contrast. None of this changes the bug or the fix.
refute.fix_notes: I applied the fix. Nova: radius 8px, the focus ring is kept (and gets the accent with the tabs-01 rule), and the colours are untouched. Nova off: the collapsed Fun label becomes rgb(21,20,26) on oklch(0.86 0.14 50) with outline none, the same as the expanded Work label. One small cosmetic leftover: in vertical Nova, .tab-group-label-hover-highlight keeps its pill radius (tabs.css:2218-2224) around an 8px label, so the hover halo will not match exactly.

fixreview.reasoning:
The problem is real. The markup is `.tab-group-label-container > .tab-group-label-hover-highlight > .tab-group-label` (tabgroup.mjs:87-92), so the child combinator never matches. The probe shows labelParent=tab-group-label-hover-highlight, the cascade selector matching false, and the Nova pill radius `16px 16px 16px 4px`.

The analysis of the original declarations is right:
- `--tab-group-*-pale` only exists under `@media not -moz-pref("browser.nova.enabled")` (tabs.css:120-147).
- `outline: none !important` would kill the label focus ring (tabs.css:2328-2331).
- The `-invert` background would be unreadable in dark mode.

The proposed fix works. With Nova on, every label gets radius 8px and the focus ring is kept, in the accent colour once tabs-01 lands. With Nova off, the collapsed label gets the same colours as an expanded one in dark and in light, outline none. `-moz-pref()` media queries do evaluate in userChrome (verified).

One small flaw: `:not(.tablist-keyboard-focus)` keys on a class that persists after focus leaves the tab strip (tabbox.js:861; tabs.mjs:693-698 only clears tablist-has-focus). With Nova off, the collapsed label you last arrowed to gets Firefox's 1px collapsed outline back. That outline is `light-dark(var(--tab-group-color), var(--tab-group-color-pale))`, drawn inset over Cascade's `var(--tab-group-color)` background. It is invisible in light mode and only a faint pale ring in dark mode, so the impact is cosmetic.

The `[dragover-groupTarget]` exclusion is unnecessary under Proton, where drag feedback is the box-shadow (tabs.css:2301-2303), but it is harmless.

Optional cosmetic: with Nova on, in an expanded vertical sidebar, the hover highlight around a collapsed group keeps its pill radius (tabs.css:2219-2225) around the now 8px label.
fixreview.fix_notes: Works in Nova on and off, light and dark. For exactness, change `&:not(.tablist-keyboard-focus, [dragover-groupTarget])` to `&:not(#tabbrowser-tabs[tablist-has-focus] .tablist-keyboard-focus)` so the outline does not come back on the last keyboard-focused collapsed label after focus leaves. The visible effect is tiny either way. Dropping `width: 100%` is right.

title: Close-button knobs: 'always show' + 'hover off' hides the button on the hovered tab; 'hover' bypasses Firefox's narrow-tab protection
problem: The two knobs are separate display values, and the hover rule always wins on the hovered tab. Results for the four combinations: none/none means never shown, which is fine. none/flex (mouse config) shows it on hover only. flex/flex always shows it. flex/none ('always show the close button') shows it on every tab except the one under the mouse, exactly when you want to click it. Also, with hover=flex (the mouse config), the button appears on background tabs even when Firefox has set closebuttons="activetab" because tabs are narrow or overflowing. Firefox does that on purpose so a click meant to select a narrow tab doesn't close it. In expanded vertical tabs, 'always' still hides it on inactive tabs, because Firefox uses visibility:collapse, which display doesn't override.
evidence: cascade-tabs.css:28-33: `.tabbrowser-tab:not([pinned]) .tab-close-button { display: var(--show-tab-close-button) !important; }` and `.tabbrowser-tab:not([pinned]):hover .tab-close-button { display: var(--show-tab-close-button-hover) !important; }` (the second is more specific). Harness probe, mouse on tabs[2], knobs set inline: none/flex → hovered flex, others none. flex/none → hovered none, others and selected flex (agents/tabs/probe/h-close-flex-none.png). flex/flex → all flex. Firefox protection: tabs.css:1046-1048 `#tabbrowser-tabs[closebuttons="activetab"][orient="horizontal"] &:not([selected]) { display: none; }`, set by tabs.mjs:1338-1380 `_updateCloseButtons` ('so that people don't accidentally close tabs by selecting them'). Vertical: tabs.css:3074-3075 `&:not(:hover) .tab-close-button:not([selected]) { visibility: collapse; }`. FF160 supports custom-property style queries, used in its own chrome at moz-page-nav.css:67 `@container style(--page-nav-collapsed: collapsed)`.

refute.reasoning: Both declarations are user !important. The hover rule has specificity (0,4,0) against (0,3,0), so it always wins on the hovered tab. If you set 'always show' (flex) and leave hover at its default of none, the button disappears on exactly the tab under the mouse. With hover set to flex (mouse config), the user !important rule also beats Firefox's author `#tabbrowser-tabs[closebuttons=activetab][orient=horizontal] .tab-close-button:not([selected]) { display: none }`. Firefox sets that attribute on purpose when tabs are narrow or overflowing, so that clicking to select a tab does not close it. The vertical expanded point is also correct: Firefox hides the button with visibility: collapse, which display does not affect.
refute.fix_notes: @container style() on a custom property is supported in FF160 chrome (used at moz-page-nav-button.css:6 and moz-widget-header.css:38). I tested the proposed rule. flex/none: hovered flex. none/flex: hovered flex, others none. flex/flex and none/none unchanged. With activetab: a hovered background tab gets none and the hovered selected tab gets flex. One edge case: a config that does not define --show-tab-close-button never matches the style query, so the hover knob does nothing there. Both shipped configs define it.

fixreview.reasoning:
The problem is real:
- With flex/none, the hovered tab loses its button, because the `:hover` rule is more specific.
- With hover=flex, user `!important` beats Firefox's narrow-tab protection, `#tabbrowser-tabs[closebuttons="activetab"][orient="horizontal"] &:not([selected]) { display: none }` (tabs.css:1046-1048, set by `_updateCloseButtons` in tabs.mjs:1338-1380).
- In expanded vertical tabs, inactive buttons keep `visibility: collapse` (tabs.css:3074-3076).

The proposal works. `@container style(--x: none)` evaluates in FF160 userChrome against the inherited knob, and Firefox uses the same construct itself (moz-page-nav.css:67, moz-widget-header.css:38).

The proposal is more complex than needed, though, and only half-applies its own rationale. With 'always' (flex), the base rule still forces `display: flex !important` on narrow or overflowing background tabs. A simpler layout covers every combination: the hover rule inside the style query, then one higher-specificity rule that hides the button on non-selected tabs when `closebuttons="activetab"` in horizontal tabs. That restores Firefox's protection in every mode, with no compound `:not()`. I tested all 4 knob combinations with and without activetab.

Also worth knowing, though neither version handles it: with `sidebar.visibility=expand-on-hover`, Firefox hides the collapsed-sidebar close button with author `display: none` (tabs.css:3034-3046). Cascade's hover rule (user `!important`) overrides that in both versions. It is an edge case, so the fix is optional.
fixreview.fix_notes:
It fixes both stated bugs, verified. The better_fix below is simpler: a plain hover selector inside the style query, plus one protection rule that also applies to 'always', which is exactly Firefox's default behaviour. Whichever you use, update the comments in both config files (cascade-config.css:173-185, cascade-config-mouse.css:178-190):
- 'show: flex' always shows the button and covers hover too.
- The hover knob only matters when the first knob is none.
- Firefox keeps buttons off narrow background tabs.
- In expanded vertical tabs, Firefox shows the button only on the hovered and active tab.

title: Pinned-tab sound/mute indicator vanishes on hover (dark icon on dark background)
problem: Hovering the speaker badge on a pinned tab (or on any tab in the collapsed vertical sidebar) is meant to invert it. Instead the icon turns the base colour on a still-dark circle and disappears, right when you are about to click it to mute or unmute. In the normal state Cascade's background-color is never seen either.
evidence: FF160 tabs.css:725-733 paints the badge with opaque image layers: `--audio-overlay-extra-background: transparent; background-color: var(--lwt-accent-color); ... background-image: image(var(--audio-overlay-extra-background)), image(var(--toolbox-background-color));` and on hover tabs.css:749-750 `--audio-overlay-extra-background: var(--button-background-color-ghost-hover)`. Cascade (cascade-tabs.css:62-79) only changes `background-color`, which is painted underneath those layers, and sets `color: var(--toolbox-background-color)` on hover. Probe while hovering the overlay: color rgb(30,32,33), fill rgb(30,32,33), background-image `image(color(srgb 0.1176 0.1254 0.1294 / 0.17)), image(rgb(30,32,33))`, so the icon is the same colour as the background. Screenshot agents/tabs/probe/z-h-overlay-hover.png. The `stroke:` declarations do nothing: the element only exposes `-moz-context-properties: fill` (tabs.css:727).

refute.reasoning: FF160 paints the pinned or collapsed audio badge with opaque background-image layers on top of background-color. Cascade's `background-color` changes are therefore never visible. On hover Cascade sets `color: var(--toolbox-background-color)`, the dark base colour, while the layers underneath are still a 17% hover tint over the opaque toolbox colour. The speaker icon ends up the same colour as its badge and disappears at the moment you would click it to mute. On a selected pinned tab the stack also includes --tab-background-color-selected, so the badge is low-contrast rather than invisible. The `stroke` declarations do nothing, because only `-moz-context-properties: fill` is exposed.
refute.fix_notes: I tested it. With `--audio-overlay-extra-background: var(--toolbar-text-color) !important` on :hover, the hover background-image is `image(rgb(250,250,252)), image(rgb(30,32,33))` and the speaker is rgb(30,32,33), so you get a light badge with a dark speaker (ovcmp.png, bottom). A user !important custom property on the element itself beats Firefox's author hover value. Small trade-off: Firefox's :hover:active pressed tint is also overridden, so there is no pressed feedback unless a `&:hover:active` value is added.

fixreview.reasoning:
The problem is real. Firefox paints the badge with opaque image layers over background-color: `background-image: image(var(--audio-overlay-extra-background)), image(var(--toolbox-background-color))`, plus a `[selected]` variant with `--tab-background-color-selected` (tabs.css:725-746, and the expand-on-hover copy at tabs.css:818-841). Cascade's `background-color` is therefore never visible, and on hover its `color: var(--toolbox-background-color)` matches the opaque `image(toolbox-bg)` layer, so the speaker disappears. Only `-moz-context-properties: fill` is exposed (tabs.css:727), so the `stroke` lines are dead.

The fix is correct. User `!important` `--audio-overlay-extra-background` on `:hover` beats Firefox's own hover value on the same element (tabs.css:750). It covers `:hover:active` and the window-inactive and `[selected]` stacks, and works in both the pinned and expand-on-hover vertical blocks, because the selector does not depend on context. Removing the `color` line leaves the normal state on `--toolbox-text-color` / `--tab-text-color-selected`, which Cascade already maps (cascade-colours.css:65, 82), so the normal look is unchanged.

The only loose end is the ambiguous `border-radius: var(--uc-border-radius) /* or keep the round badge */`. Firefox already rounds the badge with `--border-radius-circle` (tabs.css:729), so drop the line rather than make a design decision in a bug fix.
fixreview.fix_notes: Correct. Apply it without the border-radius line (or keep the existing 10px, which is equivalent on a 16px badge). Firefox's badge is already a circle, so the `/* or keep the round badge */` choice is unnecessary.

title: Accent line on a selected pinned tab shrinks to a 2px dot that looks like Firefox's attention dot
problem: The line width is `100% - 2 * --uc-tab-padding`, but pinned tabs don't use --uc-tab-padding. A selected pinned tab is only 32px wide, so the line is 2px. It sits bottom-centre like Firefox's blue 'title changed / needs attention' dot on pinned tabs, so the active pinned tab looks like it has a notification. Split-view tabs are similar: Firefox pads their content with --space-medium, so the line no longer lines up with the title.
evidence: cascade-tabs.css:101-105 `center bottom / calc(100% - 2 * var(--uc-tab-padding)) var(--uc-active-tab-line)`. FF160 tabs.css:382-384 pinned tabs get `padding: 0 calc((var(--tab-min-height) - var(--icon-size)) / 2)` = 8px instead of --tab-padding-inline. Nova .tab-background has `border: 1px solid transparent` (tabs.css:1094), so the padding box is 30px. Probe: selected pinned .tab-background 32x32, `background-size: calc(100% - 28px) 2px`, i.e. 2px. Attention dot: tabs.css:1255-1261 `background-image: radial-gradient(circle, var(--tab-attention-dot-color) ... 2px ...); background-position: center bottom 6.5px; background-size: 4px 4px`. Screenshot agents/tabs/probe/z-h-pinned.png: the selected pinned tab's purple dot next to the pinned tab's blue attention dot.

refute.reasoning: The maths and the render both hold for the default setup (Nova on, normal density). Pinned tabs don't use --tab-padding-inline: under :root:not([uidensity=compact],[sidebar-expand-on-hover]) Firefox gives .tab-content[pinned] a padding of (32-16)/2 = 8px, so the pinned .tab-background is 32px wide. Nova adds a 1px transparent border, so the padding box (the background positioning area, since Cascade's `background` shorthand resets the origin to padding-box) is 30px, and calc(100% - 28px) gives a 2px line. The line sits at y≈35-37 (bottom of the bg padding box). Firefox's attention dot on pinned tabs sits at `center bottom 6.5px` of the 44px .tab-content, so y≈33.5-37.5. That is nearly the same spot, under the same icon, and the screenshot shows a purple dot next to a blue dot. The attention dot is never drawn on the selected tab (:not([selected])), so the two never meet on one tab. The problem is purely that they look alike, plus the active marker being a 2px speck. The setup matters: compact gives a ~14px line (pinned uses Cascade's 14px padding there), touch ~11px, Nova off ~8px. The split-view sub-point is real but only a nit: content padding is 10px (--space-medium) and the line inset is about 17px, a ~5px offset.
refute.fix_notes: Verified in FF160: the computed background-size becomes `max(16px, 100% - 28px) 2px` and renders as a 16px line, so the active marker no longer looks like a dot. Regular tabs are unchanged. --icon-size resolves to 16px on .tab-background (tokens-shared.css:399). It doesn't address the small split-view misalignment, which is acceptable.

title: Split view squeezes two tabs into Firefox's 225px, so the first title is cut off and the width knobs are ignored
problem: A split view's wrapper keeps Firefox's 225px --tab-max-width, so each of its two tabs gets about 113px, while a normal active tab can grow to --uc-active-tab-width (300px). In the 'split' screenshot the active 'Firefox 160 re…' title is cut off. The adaptive width knobs have no effect on split views. Also, with the 'square tabs' setting (--uc-tab-margin: 0px) the wrapper keeps Firefox's 6px block margin and still floats.
evidence: FF160 tabs.css:1427-1438 `#tabbrowser-tabs[orient="horizontal"] tab-split-view-wrapper { margin-block: var(--tab-margin-block); ... max-width: var(--tab-max-width); }`, and tabs.css:1534-1535 `display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr`. Probe: wrapper [599,6,225,32], max-width 225px; tabs 113px each. Screenshot shots/before/split.png, agents/tabs/split-zoom.png. Collapsed groups hide wrappers with author `!important` (tabs.css:1475-1477 `tab-group[collapsed] &:not([hasactivetab]) { min-width: 0 !important; max-width: 0 !important; ...}`), which a user !important would override, so those wrappers must be excluded.

refute.reasoning: Firefox caps the horizontal split-view wrapper at --tab-max-width (225px), and it lays out its two tabs on a 1fr 1fr grid. Cascade only raises max-width on .tabbrowser-tab, and that has no effect inside the grid, so each split tab gets about 113px while a normal inactive tab is 200px and the active one can reach 300px. The width knobs really don't reach split views. Stock Firefox has the same 225px pill, so this is a gap in Cascade's width feature rather than a regression, but with Cascade's wider tabs the pill looks cramped and titles get cut. The square-tabs sub-point is also right: Cascade never touches the wrapper's own margin-block (tabs.css:1432), so with --uc-tab-margin: 0px the pill still floats. The point about the collapsed-group author !important is correct too: a user !important max-width would un-hide collapsed wrappers, so excluding them is needed.
refute.fix_notes: Verified (out-fix.txt step 23): wrapper max-width 400px, width 400, tabs 200px each, no textoverflow. The :not() complex selector works in FF160. I didn't render a collapsed group, but the exclusion logic is sound. A descendant combinator (`tab-group[collapsed] tab-split-view-wrapper`) would be slightly more robust than `>`. Like the tab rule, it only helps when the strip has spare room.

title: Dimming inactive tabs also fades indicators (attention dot, sound, camera/mic sharing, loading) and drops below AA in inactive windows
problem: The opacity is set on the whole .tab-content. That fades everything inside the tab, not just title and favicon: the blue attention/'title changed' dot on pinned and vertical tabs, the sound/mute badge and audio button, the red camera/microphone/screen-sharing indicator (privacy-relevant), the loading throbber, the crashed icon and the tab-note icon. Firefox already fades explicitly unloaded tabs' favicons to 0.5 with grayscale, so they drop to about 0.33. The partner tab of an active split view, which is on screen, is dimmed too. There is no reduced-motion or high-contrast guard. In dark mode in an unfocused window (--toolbox-text-color-inactive = --uc-muted-colour) the dimmed titles reach only about 3.8:1 contrast.
evidence: cascade-tabs.css:115-117 `.tabbrowser-tab:not([selected], [multiselected], :hover) .tab-content { opacity: var(--uc-inactive-opacity) !important; }`. tab.mjs:14-38: .tab-content holds .tab-icon-stack (throbber, icon, `.tab-sharing-icon-overlay`, `.tab-icon-overlay`), `.tab-audio-button`, label, `.tab-note-icon`, `.tab-close-button`. The attention dot is a background-image on .tab-content itself (tabs.css:1255-1261). Sharing indicator: tabs.css:654-675 (`fill: rgb(224, 41, 29); animation: var(--tab-sharing-icon-animation)`). Unloaded fade: tabs.css:611-619 `&[pending][discarded] { filter: grayscale(100%); opacity: 0.5; }`, with firefox.js:1117 `pref("browser.tabs.fadeOutExplicitlyUnloadedTabs", true)`. Probe: soundplaying pinned tab content opacity 0.65, titlechanged pinned tab opacity 0.65, split partner opacity 0.65. Screenshot agents/tabs/probe/z-h-pinned.png. Contrast (computed): #aaaaac at 0.65 over #1e2021 = #797a7b, 3.8:1.

refute.reasoning: The core claim is right. The opacity sits on the whole .tab-content, so it fades the attention dot (a background-image on .tab-content itself), the audio button, the sharing overlay, the throbber and the other overlays. The sharing overlay is only ever shown on unselected tabs (`&[sharing]:not([selected])`), which are exactly the dimmed ones, so the camera/mic/screen privacy indicator is always faded. Against #1e2021, the blue attention dot drops from about 4.3:1 to 2.6:1 and the red camera icon from about 3.5:1 to 2.1:1 at peak, both below the 3:1 non-text contrast guideline. So dimming only the label and favicon is a real improvement. The inactive-window contrast claim is wrong for the default, though. In Nova, tokens-shared.css:1060 sets `--toolbox-text-color-current: var(--toolbox-text-color)` (a plain colour, resolved at :root), so tab text stays #fafafc in a background window. Dimmed, that is about 7.3:1, not 3.8:1. The 3.8:1 figure only applies with Nova off, where the token is currentColor and inherits #aaaaac. The split-partner and double-fade (unloaded tab) points are true but minor and partly a matter of taste.
refute.fix_notes: The direction is right, and the guards are good: `@media not ((prefers-contrast: more) or (forced-colors))` parses in FF160 and labels still dim to 0.65. But `.tab-icon-image:not([pending])` breaks the sharing-indicator pulse, as shown above. Use `.tab-icon-image:not([pending], [sharing])` (both attributes are inherited onto .tab-icon-image, tab.mjs:131-132). Drop the inactive-window contrast note, or limit it to Nova off.

title: 'Adaptive' width does nothing once the tab bar is full: the active tab is as narrow as the rest
problem: The config says tabs 'have dynamic widths', with the active tab up to 300px. In practice the larger max-width only matters when there is spare room. With 5 tabs in a 1400px window every tab, the active one included, is 176px and the active title is cut off. With many tabs (overflow), every tab drops to the 76px minimum, and the 2x14px padding leaves about 5 characters (many-tabs.png), the active tab included.
evidence: FF160 tabs.css:299-300 `flex: 100 100; max-width: var(--tab-max-width)`. `flex: 100 100` means a 0 basis, so space is split evenly and Cascade's different max-widths (cascade-tabs.css:36-41) only kick in if tabs could grow past 200px. Probe (5 tabs, strip 881px): widths [176,176,176,176,176]; the selected tab has maxWidth 300px but its label has `textoverflow`. Screenshot shots/before/dark.png ('Firefox 160 release not'), many-tabs.png.

refute.reasoning: `flex: 100 100` has a 0% basis, so every tab gets an equal share. Cascade's bigger max-width for the active tab (300px versus 200px) only matters once that equal share is over 200px. In the oneline layout at 1400px the strip is 881px, so from 5 tabs onward the active tab is exactly as narrow as the others and its title is cut off. That is a very normal tab count, so in daily use the 'dynamic widths' knob barely does anything. When the strip overflows, every tab, the active one included, sits at the 76px minimum (many-tabs.png shows about 5 characters per tab). Raising the active tab's flex-grow makes the feature behave as the config describes. That fits the theme and adds one small rule.
refute.fix_notes: Verified. Caveats for the config comment: Firefox's --tab-width-transition only animates min-width and max-width, so the flex-grow jump on tab switch isn't animated. The rule doesn't help in overflow, and the min-width idea for that case is untested. The selector also matches the visible active tab of a collapsed group (Cascade's max-width rule excludes it). That is harmless, but `:not(tab-group[collapsed] .tabbrowser-tab)` would keep the two rules consistent.

title: New-tab buttons hidden in the include, not the config: mouse config can't get them back, and vertical tabs have none at all
problem: The hide rule is in cascade-tabs.css, so users of the mouse-friendly config lose the new-tab button too. The comment ('there is also one for overflow') is wrong for vertical tabs: #vertical-tabs-newtab-button is the overflow button. With both hidden, the vertical sidebar never has a '+ New Tab' row, overflowing or not (stock shows one). Horizontal tabs get no + until the strip overflows, because Firefox also hides the toolbar #new-tab-button while the in-strip button is 'adjacent'.
evidence: cascade-tabs.css:129-132 `#vertical-tabs-newtab-button, #tabs-newtab-button { display: none !important; }`. FF160 tabs.css:3159-3165: `#tabbrowser-tabs[hasadjacentnewtabbutton]:not([overflow]) ~ #new-tab-button` and `#tabbrowser-tabs[orient="vertical"]:not([overflow]) > #vertical-tabs-newtab-button` are display:none. So in vertical, #tabs-newtab-button is the inline button and #vertical-tabs-newtab-button the overflow one, and Cascade hides both. browser.xhtml:6297-6311 shows both live inside #tabbrowser-tabs. Screenshots: shots/before/vertical.png (no New Tab row) vs stock/vertical.png ('+ New Tab'). shots/before/many-tabs.png shows + only on overflow.
fix:
Follow the convention that hide rules belong in the config: move the rule into cascade-config.css's TAB-BAR section, e.g.
```css
/* Hide the New Tab buttons in the tab bar (Ctrl+T, or double-click the empty tab bar) */
#tabs-newtab-button,
#vertical-tabs-newtab-button { display: none !important; }
```
and leave it out of (or commented in) cascade-config-mouse.css. Don't use a display-valued knob: `display: flex !important` would override Firefox's own hiding in tabs.css:3159-3165 and show two buttons.

refute.reasoning: The configurability point holds. The hide rule lives in cascade-tabs.css, so cascade-config-mouse.css users, whose config otherwise keeps mouse affordances (back/forward, close-on-hover, all-tabs button), can't get a + button. Hide rules elsewhere live in the config, so moving it there follows the project's own convention. The horizontal behaviour is also correct: Firefox hides the toolbar #new-tab-button while the in-strip button is adjacent, so with Cascade the + appears only once the strip overflows. However, the claim that the comment is 'wrong' and that vertical tabs have no New Tab row at all describes intended behaviour, not a bug. Commits 815ff88/8700d77 ('hide vertical tabs new tab button', issue #142) deliberately hide both vertical buttons. The comment means 'there is also one for overflow (hide it too)'.
refute.fix_notes: Moving the rule into cascade-config.css and leaving it out of the mouse config is right. The warning against a display-valued knob is also correct: `display: flex !important` from user origin would override Firefox's author display:none and show two buttons. Note the compatibility cost: users who update the includes but keep an old config file will get the + buttons back. Mention it in the changelog.

title: box-shadow:none removes the stacked look of several tabs being dragged together
problem: When you drag several selected tabs, Firefox draws a stack ('small-stack'/'big-stack') with box-shadows on .tab-background. Cascade's blanket box-shadow:none removes it, so you can't tell several tabs are being moved.
evidence: cascade-tabs.css:18-20 `.tabbrowser-tab > .tab-stack > .tab-background { box-shadow: none !important; }`. FF160 tabs.css:1117-1160 `.tabbrowser-tab[small-stack] > .tab-stack > & { box-shadow: 5px 0 0 -3px var(--tab-background-color-selected), 3px 0 var(--tab-dragover-outline-color); }` (+ big-stack, vertical, RTL). Attributes set in drag-and-drop.js:1572-1574. I reasoned this from the CSS; I didn't take a drag screenshot because Marionette can't easily drive real drag and drop.

refute.reasoning: When two or more tabs are dragged together, Firefox puts small-stack or big-stack on the dragged element and draws the stack with box-shadows on its .tab-background. Cascade's blanket `box-shadow: none !important` is user-origin !important, so it beats those author declarations whatever their specificity, and the stack never appears. Setting the attributes in a probe shows it directly. Low severity is right: it is only a visual cue during a multi-tab drag.
refute.fix_notes: Verified. `:not([small-stack], [big-stack])` brings the stack back during a drag and still removes the selected-tab shadow everywhere else, which was the rule's intent.

title: --uc-tab-border-radius only rounds .tab-background; split pill, close/audio buttons and scroll arrows ignore it
problem: The 'square and full height (classic Cascade)' setting (--uc-tab-border-radius: 0px) makes tab backgrounds square, but the split-view wrapper, the close button, the audio button, the tab-strip scroll buttons and the vertical new-tab button keep rounded corners. Firefox derives all of those from --tab-border-radius, which cascade-layout.css ties to the global --uc-border-radius.
evidence: cascade-layout.css:11 `--tab-border-radius: var(--uc-border-radius) !important;` vs cascade-tabs.css:85 `border-radius: var(--uc-tab-border-radius) !important;`. FF160 users of --tab-border-radius: tabs.css:1075 (.tab-background), 1538 (split wrapper), 1032 (close button `calc(var(--tab-border-radius) - 3px)`), 958 (audio button), 2619 (scroll buttons), 2687 (vertical new-tab button), 2204 (group label highlight). No closer redefinition than :root (only tab.tokens.css:22).
fix:
Set the token once in cascade-tabs.css and drop the per-element radius and the layout line:
```css
:root { --tab-border-radius: var(--uc-tab-border-radius) !important; }
```
(remove cascade-tabs.css:85 and cascade-layout.css:11). Checked: tab backgrounds and the split wrapper stay rounded with the default setting (probe-fix screenshots).

title: Vertical tabs: no active-tab marker, and a hovered tab looks the same as the active tab
problem: In the horizontal strip the accent line marks the active tab. In vertical tabs Cascade leaves only the highlight background, and the hover background is the same colour, and hover also undims. Moving the pointer over the sidebar makes a second tab look exactly like the active one. That matters more in the collapsed sidebar, where there is no title to tell them apart.
evidence: cascade-colours.css:80-81 `--tab-background-color-hover: var(--uc-highlight-colour)` and `--tab-background-color-selected: var(--uc-highlight-colour)`. cascade-tabs.css:98-106 adds the line only under `#tabbrowser-tabs[orient="horizontal"]`. Screenshot agents/tabs/probe/z-v-expanded-hover.png: hovered 'Wikipedia' and active 'Rust documentation' look identical.

title: Compact density: --uc-tab-padding makes pinned tabs wider than normal density; the knob does nothing for vertical tabs
problem: Firefox centres pinned favicons with its own padding in normal and touch density, but in compact it falls back to --tab-padding-inline, which Cascade forces to 14px. Compact pinned tabs come out 48px wide (Firefox: 32px), wider than in normal density. Separately, the 'space between the edge of a tab and its icon / label / close button' setting has no effect in vertical tabs, because Firefox sets --tab-padding-inline on #tabbrowser-tabs[orient=vertical], which is closer than Cascade's :root override. Firefox does that on purpose so icons don't jump when the sidebar expands, so the config should say so.
evidence: FF160 tabs.css:382-384 `:root:not([uidensity="compact"], [sidebar-expand-on-hover]) &[pinned] { padding: 0 calc((var(--tab-min-height) - var(--icon-size)) / 2); }`. tabs.css:15-17 compact `--tab-padding-inline: 6px` is overridden by cascade-tabs.css:44-46. Probe (browser.uidensity=1): pinned tab width 48px, padding 14px. Vertical: tabs.css:2877-2879 `#tabbrowser-tabs[orient="vertical"] { --tab-padding-inline: calc((var(--tab-collapsed-width) - var(--icon-size)) / 2); }`. Probe: root --tab-padding-inline 14px, tab content padding 17px.

title: Container line: different inset from the accent line, horizontal only, and the glow knob is ignored in vertical
problem: On a selected container tab, the container line (top) is inset 10px and the accent line (bottom) 14px, so the two lines have different widths (containers.png). The rules are scoped with `#TabsToolbar`, so native vertical tabs, which live in the sidebar, get Firefox's Nova line, and --container-tabs-indicator-margin / --uc-identity-glow do nothing there.
evidence: cascade-tabs.css:49-59 `#TabsToolbar .tab-context-line { margin: 2px var(--container-tabs-indicator-margin) 0 ... }`. Config default 10px (cascade-config.css:198) vs --uc-tab-padding 14px used by the accent gradient (cascade-tabs.css:103). FF160 Nova line: tabs.css:1222-1231 (`margin-block-start: var(--tab-context-line-block-offset); width: calc(100% - 2 * var(--tab-context-line-inline-offset))`). Vertical tabs are in #vertical-tabs, not #TabsToolbar. Screenshot agents/tabs/containers-zoom.png.
fix: Default the knob to the tab padding in both configs and the include defaults: `--container-tabs-indicator-margin: var(--uc-tab-padding);` and add it to the `:where(:root)` block. Scope by orientation instead of toolbar: `#tabbrowser-tabs[orient="horizontal"] .tabbrowser-tab[usercontextid] > .tab-stack > .tab-background > .tab-context-line { ... }`. If vertical should match, add an expanded-only variant: `#tabbrowser-tabs[orient="vertical"][expanded] ...`.

title: Missing old-config defaults and inconsistent knob names; a missing knob silently sets max-width/display to their initial values
problem: The include's `:where(:root)` block covers only 5 of the 12 tab knobs. If an older or hand-edited config lacks --uc-active-tab-width or --uc-inactive-tab-width, the `max-width: var(...) !important` declaration is invalid at computed-value time and behaves as `unset`. It still wins the cascade, so tabs lose Firefox's 225px cap and stretch across the whole bar. A missing --uc-show-all-tabs-button made the all-tabs button reappear as `display: inline` (the commit 7407005 situation). --show-tab-close-button, --show-tab-close-button-hover and --container-tabs-indicator-margin break the --uc-* naming convention. Rules key off `.tabbrowser-tab[selected]`, while Firefox styles visuals by `visuallyselected` (forwarded as `selected` on .tab-background, tab.mjs:120-121), so the highlight can jump ahead of the page during an async tab switch.
evidence: cascade-tabs.css:4-10 defines only --uc-tab-padding, --uc-tab-border-radius, --uc-tab-margin, --uc-active-tab-line, --uc-inactive-opacity. Used without defaults: cascade-tabs.css:14, 29, 32, 37, 40, 50, 58. FF160 tabs.css:300 `max-width: var(--tab-max-width)` is the value lost when the knob is missing. git show 7407005: 'the button only showed because the declaration reading it was invalid'.

title: Tab tokens left unthemed or mapped through unrelated variables in cascade-colours.css
problem: Multiselect borrows --toolbarseparator-color, which cascade-colours.css sets to the accent. That also turns every real toolbarseparator/menuseparator the accent colour, and ties the tab outline to an unrelated token. The attention dot, the loading throbber and the keyboard focus ring keep Firefox's or the system's blue (#3584e4 here), so they ignore the palette and the integration themes. --tab-border-color-selected-leading/-trailing: transparent are redundant: the selected background shorthand already replaces Nova's gradient border. --tab-border-color-selected, the token that actually matters (see the focus finding), is not mapped.
evidence: cascade-colours.css:73 `--toolbarseparator-color: var(--uc-accent-colour) !important;`. cascade-tabs.css:23-25 `outline-color: var(--toolbarseparator-color)`. FF160 tab.tokens.css:13 `--tab-attention-dot-color: var(--color-accent-attention)`, :74/:144 `--tab-icon-fill-loading`. Probe: attention dot `radial-gradient(circle, rgb(53, 132, 228) ...)`, focus outline rgb(53,132,228). Nova gradient border: tabs.css:1100-1104 (overridden by cascade-tabs.css:101). tab.tokens.css:115-117 leading/trailing feed only that gradient.
fix: In cascade-tabs.css use `outline-color: var(--uc-accent-colour) !important` for multiselect. In cascade-colours.css's tab section (and the 8 integration copies, which duplicate this file) add `--tab-border-color-selected: transparent !important; --tab-icon-fill-loading: var(--uc-accent-colour) !important;`. Optionally add `--tab-attention-dot-color: var(--uc-accent-colour) !important;`, which only works well once the pinned accent line is wider than the dot (pinned finding). Then the leading/trailing lines can go. Consider moving --toolbarseparator-color back to a neutral colour (panels/toolbar owners).

title: Hiding the all-tabs button by default also removes the 'Tab group saved' hint and the quickest way to saved groups
problem: In the default (keyboard) config #alltabs-button is display:none. In FF160 it is also the anchor for the 'Tab group saved' confirmation and the place that lists saved/closed tab groups, unless browser.tabs.groups.alternateMenu is on. It also carries the badge for sound playing in a hidden tab. Users who save and close groups get no confirmation, with no explanation.
evidence: FF160 tabgroup.mjs:33-47 getSaveHintAnchor: `let widgetId = alternateMenu ? "tab-groups-button" : "alltabs-button"; ... return isVisible(anchor) ? anchor : null;`. tabs.css:3170-3176 `#tabbrowser-tabs[hiddensoundplaying] ~ & > .toolbarbutton-badge-stack > .toolbarbutton-badge`. cascade-tabs.css:13-15 `display: var(--uc-show-all-tabs-button) !important`.
fix: Extend the knob comment in both configs: '…also lists saved tab groups and anchors the "group saved" hint; set flex if you use tab groups (or enable browser.tabs.groups.alternateMenu)'. Fix the comment typo 'Hide the all Tabs button' → 'Show or hide the List All Tabs button'.

title: Tab hover preview keeps Nova's 16px radius instead of --uc-border-radius
problem: The tab hover preview panel ignores Cascade's global radius, because Firefox redefines --panel-border-radius on the panel element itself, so the :root override never reaches it. With Nova on it uses 16px corners next to 8px tabs and menus.
evidence: FF160 tab-hover-preview.css:5-11 `#tab-preview-panel { ... @media -moz-pref("browser.nova.enabled") { --panel-padding: ...; --panel-border-radius: var(--border-radius-large); } }` (tokens-shared.css:33 `--border-radius-large: 16px`). Cascade only sets it on :root (cascade-layout.css:20 `--panel-border-radius: var(--uc-border-radius) !important;`). A custom property declared on the element itself wins over the inherited one.
fix: Add to cascade-tabs.css (or cascade-panels.css): `#tab-preview-panel { --panel-border-radius: var(--uc-border-radius) !important; }`

title: Accent, focus and link tokens are only mapped inside panels: focus rings, split view, links, primary buttons, checkboxes and loading/attention icons stay Firefox blue/violet
problem: Cascade sets --color-accent-primary, --focus-outline-color and --link-color only on `menupopup, panel` (cascade-panels.css:27-35). Everything outside panels still uses Firefox's accent: the system AccentColor on Linux with the system theme (GNOME blue rgb(53,132,228)) and Nova violet light-dark(#764edd,#b89cff) on Windows or with the built-in Light/Dark themes. This covers the keyboard focus ring on tabs and toolbar buttons, the URL-bar search-mode switcher ring, the findbar field ring and checkboxes, the sidebar search ring, the split-view active pane outline and splitter hover, sidebar splitter hover, the customize-mode Done button and footer links, the bookmarks-toolbar placeholder link, the bookmark/switch-to-tab badges on URL-bar results, the tab loading throbber, the download progress bar and the download/star 'attention' icons. Inside panels it is also only half fixed. Firefox resolves the shorthand `--focus-outline` on :root, so every `outline: var(--focus-outline)` inside a panel is still Firefox blue. In the same tab-group editor the name field gets a blue ring while the colour swatch gets a purple one.
evidence: FF160 resolves the derived tokens on :root: tokens-shared.css:368 `--focus-outline: var(--focus-outline-width) solid var(--focus-outline-color);`, :369 `--focus-outline-color: var(--color-accent-primary);`, :428 `--link-color: var(--color-accent-primary);`, :69/:805 `--button-background-color-primary: var(--color-accent-primary);`, :1040 (Nova) `--toolbarbutton-icon-fill-attention: var(--color-accent-primary);`, tab.tokens.css:144 `--tab-icon-fill-loading: var(--color-accent-primary);`. Nova :858 `--color-accent-primary: light-dark(var(--color-violet-50), var(--color-violet-30))`. The Linux system theme (-moz-native-theme) gives tokens-platform.css:34 `--color-accent-primary: AccentColor;` and :49 `--link-color: LinkText;` (LinkText is not derived from the accent). With Nova off the values are literals: tab.tokens.css:74 `--tab-icon-fill-loading: var(--color-blue-50)`, tokens-shared.css:543 `--toolbarbutton-icon-fill-attention: light-dark(var(--color-blue-60), var(--color-cyan-30))`, and browser-colors.css:58 `--focus-outline-color: light-dark(#0061e0, #00ddff)` under [lwtheme]. Consumers: tabs.css:1198-1200 `.tabbrowser-tab.tablist-keyboard-focus > .tab-stack > .tab-background { outline: var(--focus-outline) }`; content-area.css:526 `&.deck-selected > .browserContainer { outline: var(--focus-outline) }`, :596 `border-color: var(--focus-outline-color)`, :144 splitter `:hover { background-color: var(--focus-outline-color) }`; sidebar.css:132 and sidebar-main.css:70 (splitters); findbar.css:112 `outline: var(--focus-outline)` and :193 `accent-color: var(--color-accent-primary)`; global-shared.css:345-348 `&[default], &.primary { background-color: var(--button-background-color-primary) }`, which is the Done button (browser.xhtml:7152 `<button id="customization-done-button" default="true">`); view-nova.css:839 `.urlbarView-row:not([selected]) & { color: var(--link-color) }` and :360 type-icon `fill: var(--link-color)`; progressmeter.css:8 `--download-progress-fill-color: var(--toolbarbutton-icon-fill-attention)`. Probes (dark, Linux): :root `--focus-outline-color: AccentColor`, `--link-color: LinkText`, `--button-background-color-primary: AccentColor`; Done button bg rgb(53,132,228); findbar ring and checkbox accent rgb(53,132,228); split pane outline and border rgb(53,132,228). In the tab-group editor panel `--focus-outline-color: #786fa6` but `--focus-outline: 2px solid AccentColor`, and the #tab-group-name outline is rgb(53,132,228). Screenshots: shots/before/tab-focus-ring.png, keyboard-nav.png, findbar.png, sidebar-bookmarks.png, split.png, customize.png, bookmarks.png, urlbar-open.png (blue result badges); agents/colours/dark-doorhanger-c.png (blue checkbox) and dark-groupeditor.png (blue field ring next to the purple swatch ring). I tested a prototype with the fix below: the editor field ring became rgb(120,111,166), Done rgb(120,111,166), and the split outline and URL-bar badges turned accent (agents/colours/fix-split.png, fix-urlbar.png).

title: Nova's violet-to-orange toolbox gradient shows behind vertical tabs and around the floating page (Windows, built-in Light/Dark themes)
problem: When Firefox is not using the native theme (Windows, or any platform with the built-in Light or Dark theme), Nova paints `--toolbox-background-gradient` on <body>. Cascade only covers it on #navigator-toolbox. With horizontal tabs, #browser gets an opaque toolbar background, so the gradient is hidden. With vertical tabs nothing covers <body>, so the whole vertical tab strip / sidebar launcher and the floating-page gutters show a purple-to-brown gradient instead of --uc-base-colour. The expand-on-hover launcher paints the gradient explicitly as well. The Linux system theme is not affected (the gradient resolves to image(transparent) there), which is why shots/before/vertical.png looks right.
evidence: tokens-shared.css:1051 `--toolbox-background-gradient: linear-gradient(96deg, color-mix(var(--toolbox-background-gradient-leading) 50%, transparent) 39.84%, …)` with :1056 `--toolbox-background-gradient-leading: light-dark(var(--color-violet-10), var(--color-violet-desaturated-70))`; browser-shared.css:132-134 `@media -moz-pref("browser.nova.enabled") { --toolbox-background-image: var(--toolbox-background-gradient); }`; browser-shared.css:365-368 `:root:not([theme-image-in-toolbox]) body { background-image: var(--toolbox-background-image); }`; content-area.css:192-196 `@media (not -moz-pref("sidebar.verticalTabs")) { #browser { background-color: var(--toolbar-background-color); } }` (nothing covers body with vertical tabs); sidebar.css:555 `background-image: var(--toolbox-background-gradient), image(var(--toolbox-background-color));` (expand-on-hover launcher). Probe with the built-in Dark theme (-moz-native-theme false): body background-image `linear-gradient(96deg, oklab(0.350395 0.0333667 -0.0714453 / 0.5) 39.84%, oklab(0.363806 0.0999189 0.068457 / 0.5) 101.72%)`. Screenshot agents/colours/vertical-builtin-dark.png: tab strip pixel (125,400) = rgb(46,41,65), right gutter (1397,400) = rgb(69,32,27), instead of base rgb(30,32,33). With the fix (agents/colours/fix-vertical-builtin-dark.png) everything is base.
fix:
In the :root mapping (cascade-colours.css and integration copies):
```css
  /* Nova paints a violet to orange gradient behind the toolbars; it shows
     around the page and behind vertical tabs */
  --toolbox-background-gradient: none !important;
```
This leaves lightweight-theme images alone: they replace --toolbox-background-image directly (browser-shared.css:136-150).

title: Nova tints toolbar icons, panel icons and secondary text violet; Cascade does not map --toolbarbutton-icon-fill, --text-color or --urlbarview-text-color-secondary
problem: Without the native theme (Windows, built-in Light/Dark themes), Nova sets toolbar icon fill, panel icon fill, --text-color and the URL-bar result description colour to violet-desaturated tones. Cascade's toolbar text is --uc-inverted-colour, but the sidebar, reload, account and extensions icons stay lavender. In light mode they are #75669f on #fafafc, which is visibly purple next to the dark URL-bar icons. With warm palettes (gruvbox, rose-pine, catppuccin) the icons never match the palette. In Nova private windows the private theme's `icons: #ffffff` leaks through the same unmapped variable.
evidence: tokens-shared.css:1039 `--toolbarbutton-icon-fill: light-dark(var(--color-violet-desaturated-50), var(--color-violet-desaturated-10));`, :1023 `--text-color: light-dark(var(--color-violet-desaturated-90), var(--color-violet-desaturated-0));`; browser-colors.css:37 `--panel-icon-fill: var(--toolbarbutton-icon-fill);`; urlbarview.tokens.css:93 `--urlbarview-text-color-secondary: light-dark(#3e315f, #e7e1f8);`; LightweightThemeConsumer.sys.mjs:168 maps theme `icon_color` to `--toolbarbutton-icon-fill`. Probe with the built-in Dark theme: #reload-button icon fill rgb(231,225,248) while toolbar text is rgb(250,250,252). With the built-in Light theme the icons are #75669f (agents/colours/light-icons.png). In a temporary private window: `--toolbarbutton-icon-fill: rgb(255,255,255)`. With the fix the icons are neutral (agents/colours/fix-light-icons.png).

title: Page-styled <select> dropdowns become unreadable: Cascade forces its text colour over the page's background
problem: For a web page <select> with custom colours, Firefox draws the dropdown with the page's background (as a background-image on the popup's arrowscrollbox) and the page's text colour (as an inline --panel-text-color). Cascade's user-origin `!important` `--panel-text-color` and `color` on every `menupopup` override the inline page text colour but not the page background. Options are drawn in --uc-inverted-colour on the page's background: white on cream/white in the dark palette, dark on dark in the light palette. This affects platforms where `dom.forms.select.customstyling` is on. The Linux build ships it off (greprefs.js:340). It is preprocessed per platform, and Windows honours page select colours.
evidence: SelectParent.sys.mjs:196-199 `if (property == "color") { property = "--panel-text-color"; } menupopup.style.setProperty(property, value);`, :205-218 the background becomes `--content-select-background-image` and `menupopup.style.setProperty("--panel-text-color", selectStyle.color)`; global-shared.css:419-425 `#ContentSelectDropdown > menupopup[customoptionstyling="true"]::part(arrowscrollbox) { background-image: var(--content-select-background-image, none); background-color: -moz-Combobox; }`. Probe with dom.forms.select.customstyling=true and a select styled `background:#fff8dc;color:#222`: inline `--panel-text-color: rgb(34, 34, 34)` but computed `--panel-text-color: #fafafc` and option colour rgb(250,250,252) over rgb(255,248,220). Screenshot agents/colours/select-dark3-c.png (illegible options). With the fix, options are rgb(34,34,34) (agents/colours/montage1.png, top).

title: menupopup host background paints a square opaque box over the rounded, shadowed popup content
problem: Firefox paints popups on ::part(content), with border-radius, box-shadow and a 4px shadow margin. The host gets a matching negative margin and stays transparent. Cascade sets `background-color: var(--uc-base-colour) !important` on the menupopup host. That fills the whole host box, shadow margin included, with an opaque square. On Windows and on Linux with a compositor, context menus and dropdowns lose the 8px rounded corners Cascade itself requests (--popup-border-radius / --panel-border-radius) and lose their shadow. With Windows 11 Mica popups it paints over the native backdrop. The rule is redundant anyway: --panel-background-color is already forced for menupopup at cascade-panels.css:16. The harness cannot show this: without a compositor Firefox forces radius and margin to 0 (popup.css:46-50), which is why every menu in the shots is square.
evidence: popup.css:33-39 `:is(menupopup, panel) { … margin: calc(-1 * var(--panel-box-shadow-margin)); …`, :65-75 `&::part(content) { … background: var(--panel-background-color); border-radius: var(--panel-border-radius); … box-shadow: var(--panel-box-shadow); margin: var(--panel-box-shadow-margin); }`; tokens-shared.css:444 `--panel-box-shadow-margin: 4px;`; popup.css:46-50 radius/margin forced to 0 only `@media (-moz-platform: linux) and (not (-moz-gtk-csd-transparency-available))`; menu.css:70-76 Mica `appearance: auto; -moz-default-appearance: menupopup`. Probe: menupopup host background is rgb(30,32,33) with Cascade and rgba(0,0,0,0) once the line is removed. The panel content is still base, via --panel-background-color.

problem: In Nova, Firefox splits container colours into --identity-stroke-color (shade 40, for the tab line) and --identity-fill-color (a light-dark pair, shade 60 on light and 20 on dark). title: Lightweight themes give a hybrid: the theme's header image behind tabs/URL bar, Cascade palette on top, base-coloured page gutter
problem: With an AMO/built-in lightweight theme (e.g. Alpenglow), Cascade forces --lwt-accent-color, --lwt-text-color and every toolbar/field/tab/panel colour to the palette. The result: the theme's header image shows behind the tab strip and URL-bar row while the URL bar, active tab and menus are Cascade colours. The gutter around the floating page is plain --uc-base-colour, so the image stops abruptly. Text colour is forced to the palette regardless of the image. problem: In FF160 with Nova, every temporary private window (default prefs) swaps in the built-in 'firefox-privatewindow@mozilla.org' theme. The root gets [lwtheme] and inline theme colours. Cascade overrides most of them. The ones it doesn't are: `--sidebar-border-color` (purple 50%, drawn around #sidebar-box only under [lwtheme]), `--toolbarbutton-icon-fill` (#ffffff, wrong with palettes whose text isn't white) and `--tab-icon-fill-loading` (#d4c1ff). Probe: #statuspanel-label background rgb(54,54,58), colorScheme 'dark' (content). Screenshots shots/before/status.png, split.png (footer). Fixed render: agents/colours/montage2.png (bottom).

title: Selected row in login / form-history autocomplete popups is system blue inside a Cascade-coloured panel
problem: Cascade gives `panel[type="autocomplete-richlistbox"]` (the saved-login and form-history dropdown under page fields) its base colour. The highlighted suggestion still uses the system SelectedItem/SelectedItemText, a bright blue row in an otherwise palette-coloured popup. Cascade's own hover rule only covers menuitem/menu.

problem: Firefox reads --lwt-toolbar-field-highlight(-text) only inside `:root[lwtheme]` rules. Cascade's inverted selection therefore shows only in Nova private windows and with themes. Normal windows select URL-bar and findbar text in the system Highlight colour (blue on GNOME/Windows). The same action looks different depending on the window.

title: Light palette 'muted' colour is darker than the text colour, so de-emphasised text is not de-emphasised
problem: The light palette has `--uc-inverted-colour: #1e2021` and `--uc-muted-colour: #191b1c`, so the muted colour is darker than normal text (1.06:1 between them). The mapping uses muted for inactive-window toolbox text, URL-bar box text, the URL-bar 'action' text ('— Search with Google'), and --text-color-deemphasized in panels (shortcut labels, secondary lines). In light mode none of these recede, so menu shortcuts are as heavy as the labels.

Screenshot shots/before/appmenu-light.png (the 'Ctrl+T' shortcuts look as dark as the labels). Candidate #55585e: 6.84:1 on base, 5.11:1 on highlight, 2.29:1 against the text colour.

title: Panel button and banner overrides lose meaning: dark-on-accent primary text is 3.60:1 and add-on warning banners lose their warning colour
problem: (1) Primary button text is hard-wired to --uc-base-colour. With the default dark accent (#786fa6), 'Allow', 'Translate' and 'Done' read 3.60:1, where white would give 4.36:1. Light-accent palettes (catppuccin, rose-pine dark) need the opposite choice, so no fixed palette slot works everywhere. The default dark accent is also below 3:1 against the highlight colour (2.88:1), which matters once it becomes the focus-ring colour (WCAG 1.4.11). (2) Firefox gives `.addon-banner-item` and the update-manual/unsupported banner a warning background. Cascade forces --uc-highlight-colour onto all banners, so the warning state is only signalled by the small icon.
evidence: cascade-panels.css:81-83 `--button-text-color-primary: var(--uc-base-colour) !important;` (×3). FF160 supports contrast-color(): harness `CSS.supports('color', 'contrast-color(red)')` → true. Contrast: #1e2021 on #786fa6 = 3.60, #fafafc on #786fa6 = 4.36; #786fa6 vs #2e3133 = 2.88; candidate #a29bfe = 6.74 on base, 5.40 on highlight. panelUI-shared.css:644-648 (Nova) `#appMenu-update-banner:is([notificationid="update-manual"], [notificationid="update-unsupported"]), .addon-banner-item { --panel-banner-item-color: var(--button-text-color); --panel-banner-item-background-color: var(--background-color-warning); }`, overridden by cascade-panels.css:92.

title: The Firefox-variable mapping is copied into every colour integration, so each mapping fix has to be made 9 times
problem: Every integration is a full copy of cascade-colours.css. From the `:where(:root)` defaults to the identity classes it is byte-identical (diff against line 49 onward is empty for all 8 files). Every fix above (accent tokens, gradient, icon fill, infobars, container classes, URL colour) must be applied 9 times, and a user who installed a theme months ago keeps the old mapping forever. cascade-panels.css already avoids this ('Everything here is built from the palette … so colour integrations do not need their own copy').
evidence: `diff <(sed -n '49,200p' chrome/includes/cascade-colours.css) <(awk '/Defaults for options/{p=1} p' integrations/<x>.css)` prints nothing for ayu, catppuccin ×3, gruvbox, nord and rose-pine ×2. The only differences are the two palette `@media (prefers-color-scheme)` blocks.
fix: Move lines 49-170 into a new include, e.g. chrome/includes/cascade-mapping.css, imported in userChrome.css right after cascade-colours.css. Reduce cascade-colours.css and each integration to the two palette blocks. Keep the `:where(:root)` defaults in the new include, following the existing convention. Mention in the README that integrations now only replace the palette.

title: Default configs hide the live camera/microphone/screen/location sharing indicator in the URL bar
problem: Both configs hide #identity-permission-box all the time, under the comment "Only hides permission items". In Firefox 160 that box also holds the red indicators that show a site is using the camera, microphone, screen, location, XR or a serial device right now. It also holds the blocked-permission icons (popup, autoplay, notifications), which are the way to undo a block. So with Cascade's default setup, a site can stream your camera or microphone with no indicator in the URL bar. Only the small tab overlay and the global indicator are left. This applies in every configuration, Nova on or off.
evidence: browser.xhtml:6498-6512: `<box id="identity-permission-box" ...><image id="permissions-granted-icon"/><box ...><image class="sharing-icon" id="webrtc-sharing-icon"/><image class="sharing-icon geo-icon" id="geo-sharing-icon"/>...<box id="blocked-permissions-container">`. identity-block.css:240-247: `#identity-permission-box { display: none; }` and `#identity-permission-box[open="true"], #identity-permission-box[hasPermissions], #identity-permission-box[hasSharingIcon] { display: flex; }`, so Firefox already hides the box unless there is something to show. identity-block.css:251-282 gives the sharing icons `fill: var(--icon-color-critical)` while sharing is active. browser-sitePermissionPanel.js:308-341 sets `hasSharingIcon` while camera, microphone, screen or geo sharing is on. Cascade's `#identity-permission-box { display: none !important; }` is user-origin !important, which beats the author `display: flex` on the same element. The box can therefore never appear.

refute.reasoning: In FF160 #identity-permission-box holds #permissions-granted-icon, the four .sharing-icon images and #blocked-permissions-container. Firefox's own CSS shows the box only while it has something to show. Cascade's user-origin `display: none !important` beats Firefox's author `display: flex`, so the box can never appear. The trust panel (on by default) only hides #identity-icon-box and #tracking-protection-icon-container, and it does not show sharing state itself. None of these rules is Nova-gated, so the problem exists in every configuration. A probe in real FF160 shows it happening.
refute.fix_notes: Verified in FF160: the fix shows only the sharing icons and keeps the static granted and blocked icons hidden, the same minimalism as before. Updating the #identity-box comment is right.

fixreview.reasoning: The problem is real in every setup. Firefox already hides #identity-permission-box until it has something to show (identity-block.css:240-247), and it sets [hasSharingIcon] while the camera, microphone, screen, location, XR or a serial device is in use, or during a camera/microphone grace period (browser-sitePermissionPanel.js:308-358). Cascade's user-origin `#identity-permission-box { display: none !important; }` (cascade-config.css:122-124, cascade-config-mouse.css:116-118) beats the author `display: flex`, so the indicator can never appear. None of these rules sit behind a Nova @media query, so Nova on and off behave the same, and so do vertical tabs, popups and every density. The proposed fix works. In Firefox 160 the box shows only the red sharing icon and still hides the granted and blocked icons. That keeps the original intent of hiding permission items and only adds the safety indicator back. A possible refinement: scope the selectors to #identity-box. Firefox 160 also builds an #identity-permission-box with a #blocked-permissions-container child inside sidebar tool documents (sidebar-permissions-ui.mjs:52-79). That box uses a `.showing` class and never gets [hasSharingIcon]. If userChrome.css reaches that chrome document, the unscoped `:not([hasSharingIcon])` keeps hiding the sidebar's own microphone indicator, as Cascade already does today. Scoping lets the sidebar indicator behave as Firefox designed it, and the URL bar result is the same.
fixreview.fix_notes: Works as proposed with Nova on and off, in every density, with horizontal and vertical tabs and in popups, since none of the identity-block rules are gated. User !important beats the author display:flex, and the attribute selector matches because Firefox's own CSS uses `[hasSharingIcon]` with the same casing. Apply it in both configs and update the `#identity-box` comment as proposed. Optional: scope to #identity-box so the sidebar tool's permission indicator is left alone (see better_fix). The fix keeps hiding the blocked-popup and blocked-permission icons, which matches the 'Only hides permission items' intent. Firefox also shows an infobar for blocked popups.

title: Following the documented 'always show the tab close button' setting makes the button disappear on hover
problem: The config says "Enable this to always show the Tab Close button: show: flex" for --show-tab-close-button, and a separate knob for hover. A user who sets only --show-tab-close-button: flex keeps --show-tab-close-button-hover: none, the default in cascade-config.css. The hover rule is more specific, so the close button shows on every tab and then disappears from the hovered tab, which is exactly when the user wants to click it. The knobs give no way to get 'always' except by setting both, and that is not documented.
evidence: cascade-tabs.css:28-33: `.tabbrowser-tab:not([pinned]) .tab-close-button { display: var(--show-tab-close-button) !important; }` and `.tabbrowser-tab:not([pinned]):hover .tab-close-button { display: var(--show-tab-close-button-hover) !important; }`. Both are user !important, and the :hover rule is more specific, so it wins. Harness check (Firefox 160, default config with only `--show-tab-close-button: flex`): with no hover, getComputedStyle(close).display was `flex` on both tabs. While hovering gBrowser.tabs[3] it returned `[true, "none", "flex"]`: the hovered tab's button was `none`, the other tab's `flex`. Screenshots: agents/config/G-nohover.png and G-hover.png.

refute.reasoning: Both close-button rules are user !important. The :hover rule is more specific, (0,4,0) against (0,3,0), so on hover it always wins. In the default config the hover knob is `none`, so a user who sets only the documented 'always show' knob loses the button on exactly the tab under the pointer. The mouse config is not affected because its hover knob is `flex`. Reproduced in FF160.
refute.fix_notes: The proposed fix works and the fallback chain keeps old configs working, though old configs keep the old behaviour. It bundles a --uc- rename. The minimal fix without a rename is `--show-tab-close-button-hover: var(--show-tab-close-button);` in cascade-config.css, with the three combinations documented.

fixreview.reasoning: Both rules are user !important, and `.tabbrowser-tab:not([pinned]):hover .tab-close-button` (cascade-tabs.css:31-33) is more specific than the 'always' rule (:28-30). A user who follows the comment and sets only `--show-tab-close-button: flex` keeps the keyboard config's `--show-tab-close-button-hover: none`, so the hovered tab loses its button. I reproduced this and tested the proposed fix in Firefox 160. With the rename and fallback chain, a keyboard config that sets only `--uc-show-tab-close-button: flex` gives `flex` on every tab, including the hovered one. An old config that still uses the old names (HEAD~1 mouse config: `--show-tab-close-button: none; --show-tab-close-button-hover: flex`) still works through the fallback: none on idle tabs, flex on the hovered tab. The old `-moz-inline-block` value is invalid both before and after the change and behaves the same. Because the hover knob is a var() of the other knob, resolved at computed-value time, it also follows a later override at the end of userChrome.css.
fixreview.fix_notes: Correct and backward compatible as written. Keep `--uc-show-tab-close-button-hover: flex` in the mouse config and declare both new names in both configs. Two caveats for the release notes. (1) An old config that sets only the old 'always' knob to flex still hits the bug, because it explicitly declares `--show-tab-close-button-hover: none`. Users need to migrate to the new names or also set the hover knob. (2) This was already true before the change: in expanded vertical tabs Firefox still applies `visibility: collapse` to the close button of tabs that are neither hovered nor selected (tabs.css:3074-3076), so 'always' is not quite always there. In collapsed vertical tabs Firefox's absolutely positioned `display: block` button only changes to flex, with no visible difference.

title: Colour integrations are 8 full copies of cascade-colours.css; split the palette from the mapping (verified backwards compatible)
problem: Every colour scheme carries its own copy of the 122-line mapping that applies the palette to Firefox's tokens: the :where defaults, the toolbar/tab/urlbar/sidebar tokens, .urlbarView-url and the .identity-color-* classes. Any mapping fix has to be pasted 9 times, and users who copied an integration never get it. This has already caused a missed update. Firefox 160 renamed container colours (turquoise to cyan, toolbar to gray) and added violet and gray. Cascade maps neither, so in every scheme violet and gray containers show Firefox's stock colours instead of the palette. Fixing that today means editing 9 files.
evidence: `diff` of lines 48-170 of each integration against cascade-colours.css: all 8 files are byte-identical in the mapping section (only lines 9-23 and 31-45, the palette, differ). Firefox 160 usercontext.css:94-112 defines `.identity-color-violet { --identity-tab-color: #764edd; ... --identity-stroke-color: var(--color-violet-40) }` and `.identity-color-gray { --identity-tab-color: currentColor; ... }`. ContextualIdentityService.sys.mjs:25-87 lists the colours (gray, yellow, orange, red, pink, purple, violet, blue, cyan, green), :93-96 `CONTAINER_COLOR_ALIASES = { turquoise: "cyan", toolbar: "gray" }`, and migrate5to6 (:1121-1130) rewrites stored identities to the canonical names. Cascade defines only blue, cyan, green, yellow, orange, red, pink and purple (cascade-colours.css:123-170). Harness, Nord with 4 containers: current full copy (N0) gives violet `--identity-stroke-color: #9871ff` and gray `#949297`, Firefox's colours. The split prototype (N1) gives `#b48ead` and `#d8dee9`, from the palette. The repo already follows this principle for panels: cascade-panels.css:4-5 says "Everything here is built from the palette in cascade-colours.css, so colour integrations do not need their own copy of this file".
fix:
1) Move cascade-colours.css:49-170 into a new chrome/includes/cascade-colours-mapping.css. Users never replace this file. Add the new colours there with fallbacks, so palettes that predate them still work:
.identity-color-violet { --identity-tab-color: var(--uc-identity-colour-violet, var(--uc-identity-colour-purple)) !important; /* same for -icon-, -fill-, -stroke-color */ }
.identity-color-gray { --identity-tab-color: var(--uc-identity-colour-gray, var(--uc-muted-colour)) !important; ... }
(Optionally read cyan as `var(--uc-identity-colour-cyan, var(--uc-identity-colour-turquoise))`.)
2) cascade-colours.css and each integration become palette only: the two `@media (prefers-color-scheme)` blocks, about 47 lines. Add a header: "Palette only. Copy over chrome/includes/cascade-colours.css; the mapping lives in cascade-colours-mapping.css."
3) userChrome.css: add `@import "includes/cascade-colours-mapping.css";` right after `@import "includes/cascade-colours.css";`.
Backwards compatibility, verified in Firefox 160:
(a) New userChrome.css with an OLD full-copy integration as cascade-colours.css (prototype N2): the old copy's mapping comes first and the new file re-declares the same properties later, with the same origin, importance and specificity, so the new mapping wins. Computed tokens were identical to the palette-only setup (N1), and a pixel compare gave 0 differing pixels. Old copies keep working and also get the new violet/gray mapping.
(b) Users who kept an older, customised userChrome.css (windows fix swapped in, TCR appended) together with a new palette-only file would get no mapping. Either say so in the release notes, or also put `@import "cascade-colours-mapping.css";` as the first line of cascade-layout.css: every userChrome.css since 2025-01 imports it right after the colours, and importing the file twice is harmless.
(c) Users who edited the mapping inside their cascade-colours.css: the mapping now comes later and wins. Migration note: move such overrides to the end of userChrome.css, after the imports.
4) Bonus: a palette-only file declares only --uc-* inside prefers-color-scheme, so it can be pasted as-is into the Tab Center Reborn stylesheet (see the TCR finding).
5) Add a CI check that integration files declare only --uc-identity-colour-* and --uc-{base,highlight,inverted,muted,accent}-colour.

refute.reasoning: All 8 integrations really are byte-identical to cascade-colours.css from line 48 on. Only the palette differs. FF160 has violet and gray container classes that Cascade never maps, so those containers keep Firefox's stock colours in every scheme. Splitting the palette from the mapping follows the precedent the repo already set in cascade-panels.css:4-5. The import order makes old full copies harmless, because the later mapping re-declares the same properties with the same origin, importance and specificity. One part of the motivation is overstated: duplication did not cause the violet/gray miss. In f67aa11 the maintainer updated all 9 copies in lockstep (turquoise to cyan, about 92 lines each) and missed violet/gray in all of them, as a single file would have.
