The concrete harm of the copies is different: users who copied an integration before f67aa11 still have the pre-159 mapping (--lwt-frame, --toolbar-bgcolor, --urlbar-box-bgcolor…), which FF159+ no longer reads, and they will never get mapping fixes.
refute.fix_notes: The design is sound and backward compatible as described. Putting `@import "cascade-colours-mapping.css";` first in cascade-layout.css is valid (@import before any rule) and resolves inside includes/. Migration point (c) is a real behaviour change for anyone who edited the mapping, so it needs a release note. The violet/gray mapping with fallbacks is worth shipping even if the split is postponed.

fixreview.reasoning: Lines 48-170 of all 8 integrations are byte-identical to cascade-colours.css, so only the two palette blocks differ. Firefox 160 has violet and gray container colours (usercontext.css:94-112) that Cascade never maps, so those containers show Firefox's own colours in every scheme. The split works in Firefox 160. I verified the riskiest compatibility path, option (b): an OLD userChrome.css with no mapping import, a palette-only (Nord) cascade-colours.css, and `@import "cascade-colours-mapping.css";` as the first line of cascade-layout.css. The mapping loaded, the Nord tokens applied, violet resolved through the purple fallback and gray through the muted fallback. The relative @import resolves against includes/, and @import is valid after a leading comment. A double import, from both userChrome.css and cascade-layout.css, only repeats identical declarations. The earlier N2 run already showed that an old full-copy integration combined with the new mapping file still works and picks up violet and gray. The proposal is sound. It only needs the abbreviated violet/gray rules written out in full, and the default palette should get real violet and gray values so violet containers are not identical to purple ones.
fixreview.fix_notes: Ready to apply as proposed. Notes: (1) Write the violet/gray rules out in full (see better_fix) and give the default palette its own violet and gray values. Integrations can add theirs later, and the fallback covers files that do not. (2) Use the cascade-layout.css @import shim. Without it, users who kept a customised old userChrome.css lose ALL toolbar colours as soon as they copy a new palette file, which is far worse than missing panel theming. The shim was verified to work. (3) Item 5 (CI) is not cheap: the repo has no CI today (.github holds only issue/PR templates), so it would mean adding a workflow. (4) Migration note (c) is needed: edits users made to the mapping inside cascade-colours.css are now overridden by the later mapping file.

title: The mouse config hides the window controls (minimise / maximise / close)
problem: cascade-config-mouse.css is the setup for mouse users (back/forward and close-on-hover kept), but it copies the keyboard config's `.titlebar-buttonbox-container { display: none !important; }`. With Firefox drawing its own title bar (default on Windows and macOS, and Linux with CSD), a mouse user then has no buttons to close, minimise or maximise the window. That includes F11 fullscreen, where these buttons are the only mouse way out, and macOS, where the traffic lights disappear.
evidence: browser.xhtml:6245, 6351, 6817: three `<hbox class="titlebar-buttonbox-container" skipintoolbarset="true">` (menubar, TabsToolbar, nav-bar). browser-shared.css:404-415: `.titlebar-buttonbox-container { order: 1000; ... (-moz-platform: macos) order: -1 }`. :470-483: Firefox itself hides them when the menubar is always shown, and keeps them only in the first visible toolbar (`#navigator-toolbox:not([tabs-hidden]) > #nav-bar > :is(.titlebar-buttonbox-container, .titlebar-spacer) { display: none; }`), so they need no help from Cascade to avoid duplicates. Under Xvfb the harness has no custom title bar (`customtitlebar` is null), so this was not checked visually.

refute.reasoning: The core issue is real. Firefox shows .titlebar-buttonbox-container whenever it draws its own title bar or is in fullscreen, so the mouse config leaves mouse users on Windows, macOS and GNOME CSD without minimise, maximise and close buttons, also in F11 fullscreen. Some claims are overstated. The buttons are not 'the only mouse way out' of F11: the toolbar context menu has 'Exit Full Screen' and the app menu has a fullscreen toggle. The drag space and taskbar also still work. The proposed fix also has an unmentioned flaw. On macOS, and on GTK with buttons on the left, the box gets `order: -1` inside #TabsToolbar. In Cascade's default oneline layout #TabsToolbar sits to the right of #nav-bar, so the traffic lights would land mid-window between the URL bar and the tabs, not only with --uc-urlbar-position: 3. This could not be checked visually because the harness has no custom title bar.
refute.fix_notes: Commenting the rule out in the mouse config is reasonable. The comment must also warn that on macOS (and GNOME with left-hand buttons) the controls appear between the URL Bar and the tabs in the default layout, and on Windows/Linux only with --uc-urlbar-position: 3.

fixreview.reasoning: The mouse config copies the keyboard config's `.titlebar-buttonbox-container { display: none !important; }` (cascade-config-mouse.css:37-40). When Firefox draws its own title bar, and also in fullscreen, Firefox shows these controls. browser-shared.css:424-426 hides them only for `:root:not([customtitlebar], [inFullscreen])`. So mouse users lose minimise/maximise/close, and in F11 fullscreen they lose the restore button. Firefox already prevents duplicates: it hides them under a permanent menubar and keeps them only in the first visible toolbar (browser-shared.css:470-484). Under Xvfb, `browser.tabs.inTitlebar=1` did not produce [customtitlebar], so I set the attribute by hand to see the layout. With the rule commented out in the mouse config, the controls render cleanly in the oneline layout. With `--uc-urlbar-position: 1` they sit at the far right of the row; with 3 they sit between the tabs and the URL bar. The proposed comment is incomplete, though. The controls take order -1, the left end of #TabsToolbar, on macOS (browser-shared.css:407-417) and on Linux with left-placed GTK buttons (browser.css:201-205). In those setups the DEFAULT position 1 puts them between the URL bar and the tabs, and position 3 puts them at the outer edge.
fixreview.fix_notes: Commenting the rule out in the mouse config is right, and the keyboard config can stay as it is. Only the comment needs correcting: the controls sit at the outer end of the tab bar, which is the right end on Windows and Linux but the left end on macOS and on Linux with left-placed buttons. So the 'between tabs and URL Bar' case is position 3 on Windows/Linux but position 1, the default, on macOS. Also say that Firefox shows them in fullscreen even without a custom title bar. Nothing else in Cascade depends on them being hidden: .titlebar-spacer stays hidden through cascade-layout.css:64-66, and in vertical tabs ([tabs-hidden]) Firefox moves the visible set to #nav-bar by itself.
fixreview.better_fix:
/* Window controls (minimise, maximise, close), shown when Firefox draws
   its own title bar and in fullscreen. They sit at the outer end of the
   Tab Bar: right on Windows / Linux, left on macOS (and Linux with the
   buttons on the left). So with --uc-urlbar-position: 3 (Windows / Linux)
   or 1 (macOS) they end up between the tabs and the URL Bar.
   Uncomment to hide them */
/* .titlebar-buttonbox-container { display: none !important; } */

title: Half the knobs have no :where(:root) default, so an older or trimmed config breaks; the all-tabs button already shows wrongly with an old mouse config
problem: The 'defaults in each include' convention covers only the knobs added in November 2026. The includes read 15 knobs that have no default. These are --uc-border-radius, --uc-status-panel-spacing, --uc-toolbar-position, --uc-darken-toolbar, --uc-urlbar-min-width/-max-width/-position, --uc-show-all-tabs-button, --show-tab-close-button(-hover), --uc-active/inactive-tab-width, --container-tabs-indicator-margin and --uc-identity-glow. A var() of an undefined property makes the declaration invalid at computed-value time, so it computes to unset. A missing --uc-urlbar-min-width gives `width: auto` on #nav-bar and #TabsToolbar and the oneline row collapses. A missing --uc-border-radius makes every Firefox radius token Cascade sets invalid. This is not hypothetical. The mouse config shipped until commit 7407005 (HEAD) never declared --uc-show-all-tabs-button, so every user still on that config gets `display: unset`, which blockifies to `display: block` on #alltabs-button.
evidence: Harness with the current includes and the config from the oldest commit in history (88b8b7d, mouse): `#alltabs-button` computed display = `block`, --uc-show-all-tabs-button = "". `--show-tab-close-button-hover: -moz-inline-block`, the old documented value and no longer valid, also computed to `block` on hover. A knob check script (agents/config/check-knobs.py) lists the 15 knobs read with no default. Run against HEAD~1, it also reports the config drift that 7407005 fixed ("knob --uc-show-all-tabs-button is declared in only one config"). Duplicate defaults also exist: --uc-inactive-opacity is defaulted in both cascade-nav-bar.css:5 and cascade-tabs.css:9.

refute.reasoning: The CSS mechanism is correct: a var() of an undefined property makes the declaration compute as unset, and the 15 knobs listed have no :where(:root) default. However, 14 of them are declared in both configs at the oldest commit available (88b8b7d, 2025-01; the clone is shallow) and at HEAD~1. Older configs from that history are therefore fine, and only a hand-trimmed config (or one from before the shallow history) breaks. The only demonstrated case is --uc-show-all-tabs-button, which the mouse config lacked until 7407005. With HEAD includes and the HEAD~1 mouse config, #alltabs-button does compute to `display: block`. The visible effect is only about 1px, because the stale margin-top: 5px happened to compensate. 'Shows wrongly' is true but minor. The duplicated --uc-inactive-opacity default follows the convention that each include defaults what it reads, and it is harmless.
refute.fix_notes: Adding zero-specificity defaults is cheap, harmless hardening. `display: var(--uc-show-all-tabs-button, flex)` is the right fallback, and it is needed before the config-06 migration note is safe (see config-06). Putting the defaults for renamed knobs in var() fallbacks is consistent.

fixreview.reasoning: The CSS mechanics are right. A var() of an undefined custom property is invalid at computed-value time, so for example a missing --uc-border-radius makes Cascade's `--toolbarbutton-border-radius: var(--uc-border-radius) !important` invalid and the corners square. But the impact is overstated. Git history shows that all 15 knobs have been declared in BOTH configs since the oldest commit (88b8b7d, 2025-01), with one exception: --uc-show-all-tabs-button in the mouse config. Only hand-trimmed configs hit the other 14. The one real case is mild today. The old mouse config gives #alltabs-button `display: block`, but its own `margin-top: 5px` happens to make up for that, and the icon sits at y=13 against 14 for the other buttons. The proposed fix has a regression. `display: var(--uc-show-all-tabs-button, flex)` combined with that old 5px margin moves the icon to y=17, 3px off, which is worse than today's 1px. Adding `margin-top: 0 !important` to the include fixes it: icon at y=14, button 44px tall like the others. The :where(:root) defaults are correct and harmless (zero specificity, so the config always wins), with one small mistake: --uc-urlbar-position is not read by cascade-responsive-windows-fix.css, so it needs no default there. 'Run check-knobs.py in CI' is not ready: the repo has no CI, and the script fails on HEAD because it flags the intentionally mouse-only --uc-page-action-margin.
fixreview.fix_notes: Add the defaults as proposed, but (1) pair the all-tabs fallback with a margin reset in cascade-tabs.css, or old mouse configs regress from 1px off to 3px off with a hover box shifted 5px. A migration note alone will not reach users who copied the config long ago. (2) Do not add --uc-urlbar-position to the windows-fix include, which never reads it. (3) Keep --uc-border-radius in one include (cascade-layout.css, imported before every other reader) or in each reader: both work, so pick one rule and follow it. (4) CI: give check-knobs.py an allowlist for config-specific knobs such as --uc-page-action-margin before wiring it into a new workflow.

title: Mouse config: the stale #alltabs-button margin-top: 5px puts the all-tabs icon 3px too low
problem: The mouse config still has `#alltabs-button { margin-top: 5px !important; }` from older Firefox versions. In Firefox 160 the button is laid out like every other toolbar button, so the margin only pushes it down. Its icon sits 3px below the other toolbar icons, and the button's hover box is cut short at the top.
evidence: Harness (mouse config, dark): `#alltabs-button` rect [1364, 5, 36, 39] inside #TabsToolbar [491, 0, 909, 44]. Icon at y=17 while #PanelUI-menu-button's icon is at y=14. With the rule removed (agents/config/F): rect [1364, 0, 36, 44], icon y=14, aligned. Zoomed crop: agents/config/B-alltabs-zoom.png. Firefox 160 tabs.css:3170 styles `#alltabs-button` only with `list-style-image` and badge rules, and gives it no vertical offset that would need correcting.
fix: Delete cascade-config-mouse.css:144-146. Migration note for users on an old mouse config: delete the same rule from your copy.

refute.reasoning: In FF160 #alltabs-button gets only list-style-image and badge rules, and with `display: flex` it centres like every other toolbar button. The 5px top margin shortens its box and pushes the icon 3px below the other toolbar icons. History matters here. Before 7407005 the button computed to `display: block` (knob undefined), and the margin roughly compensated (icon y=13 against 14). 7407005 declared the knob as `flex` 'with the same result' and turned the margin into a 3px drop, so this is a regression from HEAD.
refute.fix_notes: Deleting the rule is correct for the HEAD mouse config. The migration note is wrong on its own. Harness V6 (old mouse config with the margin deleted, knob still undefined) gives display `block` and icon y=8, 6px too high. Old-config users must delete the margin and also add `--uc-show-all-tabs-button: flex;`, or the include must first get the config-05 fallback `var(--uc-show-all-tabs-button, flex)`.

fixreview.reasoning: With HEAD's mouse config the all-tabs icon sits 3px below every other toolbar icon, and its 32px hover highlight (the badge stack) is shifted down by the same amount. Firefox 160 styles #alltabs-button only with list-style-image and badge rules (tabs.css:3170-3180) and gives it no margin. The root cause is slightly different from the finding's 'stale from older Firefox' explanation. The margin used to make up for `display: block`, which old mouse configs got because they never declared --uc-show-all-tabs-button (icon at y=13, almost aligned). Commit 7407005 (HEAD) declared `--uc-show-all-tabs-button: flex` and kept the margin, and only then did the button become 3px off. So this is a regression from the latest commit. Deleting cascade-config-mouse.css:144-146 aligns the icon exactly.
fixreview.fix_notes: Delete cascade-config-mouse.css:144-146. For users on an old mouse config, a migration note is not enough once config-05's `flex` fallback lands, because their copied margin would then put the icon 3px off. Add `margin-top: 0 !important` to the #alltabs-button rule in cascade-tabs.css (see config-05). Verified in agents/verify-config2/C2b: icon y=14, button 44px tall.

title: The all-tabs knob is documented as 'Hide' but holds 'flex', and it hides the button everywhere (vertical-tabs nav-bar, customize mode)
problem: The comment reads "Hide the all Tabs button from the Tab Bar", but the knob is a display value, and the mouse config sets it to `flex`, which shows the button. The rule also matches #alltabs-button wherever it is, not only in the tab bar. With vertical tabs Firefox puts the button in the nav-bar by default, and Cascade hides it there too. In customize mode it is invisible, so users cannot see it in the toolbar or drag it out.
evidence: cascade-tabs.css:13-15: `#alltabs-button { display: var(--uc-show-all-tabs-button) !important; }`, with no ancestor in the selector. CustomizableUI.sys.mjs:385-389, nav-bar `verticalTabsDefaultPlacements: ["alltabs-button", ...]`, and :411-418, tab strip defaultPlacements `[..., "alltabs-button", ...]` with `verticalTabsDefaultPlacements: []`. CustomizeMode.sys.mjs:531 `this.#document.documentElement.toggleAttribute("customizing", true)`. The customize screenshot (shots/before/customize.png) shows the tab strip with no all-tabs button.

refute.reasoning: Two of the three claims hold. The comment is a wording nit, not a bug. The rule is unscoped (cascade-tabs.css:13-15), so it hides the button in the vertical-tabs nav-bar and in customize mode. The customize-mode part is real and I reproduced it, but config-09 covers the same thing. Hiding the button in the vertical-tabs nav-bar is factually correct, but it fits what the knob is for: a minimalist user who set it to none wants the button gone. The vertical tab list already shows every tab, and '% ' in the URL bar searches them. So that part is a design choice, not a defect. The comment does list 'show: flex / hide: none', so the 'Hide' title confuses but does not mislead. Rewording it to 'Show ...' is a small documentation improvement.
refute.fix_notes: The customize-mode part of the fix works (verified in run B). Scoping to #TabsToolbar also changes the default for vertical-tabs users: with the knob at none they would suddenly get a button in the nav-bar, against Cascade's minimal default. Rewording the comment is fine.

title: --uc-tab-border-radius never reaches Firefox's --tab-border-radius, so square tabs keep rounded split-view boxes, group labels and close buttons
problem: The config documents "square and full height (classic Cascade): set both to 0px" for --uc-tab-border-radius and --uc-tab-margin. Cascade applies the knob only to .tab-background. Firefox's --tab-border-radius stays tied to the global --uc-border-radius, so everything Firefox derives from it stays rounded at 8px around square tabs: the split-view wrapper, the tab close button, the tab group label highlight, the scroll buttons.
evidence: cascade-layout.css:11 `--tab-border-radius: var(--uc-border-radius) !important;`. Firefox 160 tab.tokens.css:22 `--tab-border-radius: var(--toolbarbutton-border-radius);` (defined only on :root). tabs.css uses it at :958 (`--button-border-radius` of the close button), :1032, :1538 and :1704 (split-view wrapper), :2274 (group label), :2619 and :2687. Harness with `--uc-tab-border-radius: 0px; --uc-tab-margin: 0px` and a split view: tab-split-view-wrapper border-radius `8px`, .tab-background `0px`, --tab-border-radius `8px`. Crop: agents/config/S-split-zoom.png shows a rounded box around square tabs.

refute.reasoning: Cascade sets `--tab-border-radius: var(--uc-border-radius) !important` on :root (cascade-layout.css:11). Firefox defines the token only on :root/:host in a layer (tab.tokens.css:22), so the user !important value wins everywhere and never follows --uc-tab-border-radius. With the documented 'square and full height' settings (both knobs 0px), the split-view wrapper keeps an 8px radius. It has a visible background when [hasactivetab] (tabs.css:1546-1550), so square tabs sit inside a rounded box. The close button (calc(r - 3px) = 5px, tabs.css:1032), the scroll buttons (:2619) and the audio button (:958) also stay rounded. Two details in the finding are wrong. tabs.css:958 is .tab-audio-button, not the close button. With Nova on, the tab group label radius comes from `calc(var(--tab-group-label-size) / 2)` (tabs.css:2289), not from --tab-border-radius, so labels stay pills with or without the fix; only Nova-off uses :2274. The core bug stands.
refute.fix_notes: Verified in harness run B. The default setup is unchanged, because the :where default of --uc-tab-border-radius in cascade-tabs.css falls back to --uc-border-radius. The negative calc() for the close button clamps to 0.

title: The config hide rules also apply in customize mode, so hidden buttons are invisible there
problem: #back-button and #forward-button (default config), #alltabs-button and the new-tab buttons are hidden with plain `display: none !important`, including in customize mode. A user customising the toolbar cannot see that those buttons are still placed, cannot drag them out, and gets gaps that are hard to explain.
evidence: CustomizeMode.sys.mjs:531 sets `customizing` on documentElement while customising, and Firefox itself uses it, for example tabs.css:3164 `#TabsToolbar[customizing] #tabs-newtab-button { display: none; }`. shots/before/customize.png: the nav-bar shows sidebar, reload, urlbar, downloads, account; back/forward are missing although they are still in the placements.

refute.reasoning: Plain `display: none !important` hide rules also apply in customize mode. The back/forward buttons (default config) and the all-tabs button stay in their placements but render at 0 width inside their toolbarpaletteitem wrappers. Users cannot see them, drag them or remove them, and the nav-bar shows unexplained gaps. Gating the rules on `:root:not([customizing])` brings them back only while customising. This is a genuine usability improvement that costs nothing in normal use. Only these items matter: Firefox already hides #tabs-newtab-button while customising (tabs.css:3164), and #vertical-tabs-newtab-button is not a CustomizableUI widget.
refute.fix_notes: Verified working. Adding a note in the config header is worthwhile, so users are not surprised that the items disappear again after Done.

title: Stale --uc-page-action-margin knob and rule in the mouse config; the documented tweak misaligns URL bar icons
problem: The mouse config declares --uc-page-action-margin ("This might need customisation depending on your setup!") and applies it as `margin-top` on `.urlbar-page-action > image`. At 0px it does nothing. Any other value, including 7px, the shipped default until recently, pushes the star, reader-mode, translations and other page-action icons down inside their hover boxes. The knob exists only in the mouse config, which the knob check flags as drift.
evidence: Firefox 160 urlbar.css:929-944 centres page actions with `align-items: center; justify-content: center` inside a `--urlbar-basic-component-size` box, so no manual offset is needed. Harness with the old mouse config (7px): #star-button-box [345, 10, 24, 24], icon at y=18, i.e. flush with the box bottom. With 0px the icon is at y=14, centred.
fix: Remove both the knob (lines 30-34) and the rule (lines 126-129) from cascade-config-mouse.css. Migration note: "If your config still contains `.urlbar-page-action > image { margin-top: ... }`, delete it; Firefox 160 centres these icons itself."

refute.reasoning: Firefox 160 already centres page-action icons in a fixed-size flex box, so the margin-top knob has no correct value other than 0. At the shipped 0px the rule does nothing. At 7px, the mouse config default before f67aa11, which users who keep their old config file still carry, the star and other icons drop 3.5px and sit on the bottom edge of their hover box. The knob also exists only in the mouse config; cascade-config.css has no counterpart and no :where default declares it.
refute.fix_notes: Removing the knob and the rule is right. The migration note matters, because the bad rule lives in users' own copied config files.

title: #pageActionButton hide rule does nothing in wide windows and removes the overflow menu in narrow ones
problem: Firefox already hides the page-actions (meatball) button. It shows it only in windows 680px wide or less, as the overflow target that replaces the page-action buttons after it. Cascade's unconditional hide is therefore a no-op normally, and in narrow windows (split screens) it removes both the meatball and the star it replaces.
evidence: urlbar.css:749-753 `/* The page actions menu is hidden by default, it is only shown in small windows ... */ #pageActionButton { display: none; }`. :758-767 `@media (max-width: 680px) { #pageActionSeparator, #pageActionButton[multiple-children] ~ .urlbar-page-action { display: none; } #pageActionButton[multiple-children] { display: revert; } }`. browser.xhtml:6680-6691: #star-button-box follows #pageActionButton, so it is the item hidden in favour of the meatball.
fix: Delete the `#pageActionButton` rule from both configs. If someone really wants no star in narrow windows, offer it as a commented-out line next to the existing `#page-action-buttons > :not(#urlbar-zoom-button)` option.

refute.reasoning: The rule is a no-op in wide windows, as claimed. The narrow-window harm needs a condition the finding leaves out. Firefox shows the meatball and hides the following page actions only when #pageActionButton has [multiple-children]. That attribute is set only when PageActions.actions.length > 1, and the only built-in action is 'bookmark'. So nothing happens without an extension that adds a page_action, and the star is never hidden. With such an extension, at 680px or narrower, Firefox hides the star and the extension's page-action buttons (inserted before the star, after the meatball) in favour of the meatball. Cascade then also hides the meatball, so every one of those actions disappears from the URL bar. The bug is real but narrower than described.
refute.fix_notes: Deleting the rule from both configs restores Firefox's overflow behaviour, and nothing changes in wide windows. The optional commented-out line is fine.

title: Undocumented #PanelUI-menu-button 1px hack: a 1x44px hit target with an invisible focus ring and a floating badge
problem: The default config shrinks the app menu button to a 1px icon with no padding and no comment. The result is a 1px wide, 44px tall button. It is still reachable with toolbar keyboard navigation, but its focus ring is invisible. When Firefox badges the menu (update available, restart, add-on permissions) the blue dot floats on its own next to the extensions button. Nothing tells users how to open the menu, and the mouse config does not use the hack at all.
evidence: Harness, default config: #PanelUI-menu-button rect [490, 0, 1, 44], icon [490, 22, 1, 1]. After `setAttribute('badge-status','update-available')` the badge renders at [482, 13.5, 12, 12] (agents/config/A-badge-zoom.png: a lone blue dot after the extensions icon; mouse config B-badge-zoom.png: the dot on the hamburger). browser.xhtml:6798-6804: #PanelUI-menu-button is `badged="true"` and `consumeanchor="PanelUI-button"`, which is why it cannot simply be `display: none`: the app menu and its doorhangers anchor to it.

refute.reasoning: Most of the measurements hold, but two points are overstated. The hack at cascade-config.css:40-48 is undocumented, and the mouse config does not use it. It leaves a 1x44 button with a 1x1 icon. Toolbar keyboard navigation still reaches it: the walker skips only width-0 nodes (browser-toolbarKeyNav.js:89-92). There, Firefox's focus ring, a 2px outline inset by 2px on the 1x1 badge-stack, renders as a ~3px blue dot. That dot is not literally invisible, but it does not read as a focus ring and looks just like the update badge. For a keyboard-centred theme, a proper indicator and a comment are real improvements. The lone floating update badge is arguably a fine minimal 'needs attention' cue rather than a defect.
refute.fix_notes: The documentation comment is good. The focus-visible rules work (verified), with two drawbacks. The URL bar shifts while the button has keyboard focus. And the ring is cramped, because cascade-config.css:46-48 still sets the badge-stack padding to 0.

title: Inconsistent knob names (--show-tab-close-button, --container-tabs-indicator-margin, 'toolbar' meaning the bookmarks toolbar); rename with fallbacks
problem: Three knobs break the --uc-* convention, so they could collide with Firefox tokens; Firefox already owns the --tab-close-button-* and --tab-context-line-* namespaces. The container line is called 'identity' in one knob (--uc-identity-glow) and 'container-tabs-indicator' in the next. --uc-toolbar-position and --uc-darken-toolbar are about the bookmarks toolbar, called the 'Personal Toolbar' in the comments, but read as if they controlled the nav-bar. The position knobs also expose raw `order` values (0/4 and 1/3) whose meaning depends on the order values hard-coded in cascade-layout.css:68-80.
evidence: Firefox 160 tabs.css:1223-1231 already defines `--tab-context-line-block-offset` and `--tab-context-line-inline-offset`, and tab.tokens.css:24-27 `--tab-close-button-*`. cascade-layout.css:68-80 `#TabsToolbar { order: 2 }`, `#nav-bar { order: 3 }`, `#notifications-toolbar { order: 5 }`, `#PersonalToolbar { order: var(--uc-toolbar-position) }`. The knob check reports "knob --show-tab-close-button lacks the --uc- prefix" and the same for the other two.
fix:
Rename in both configs and read the old names as fallbacks, with no :where default for the new names, so old configs keep working:
--uc-show-tab-close-button / --uc-show-tab-close-button-hover (see the close-button finding)
--uc-container-line-margin: `margin: 2px var(--uc-container-line-margin, var(--container-tabs-indicator-margin, 10px)) 0 !important;`
--uc-container-line-glow: `var(--uc-container-line-glow, var(--uc-identity-glow, 0 1px 10px 1px))`
--uc-bookmarks-toolbar-position: `order: var(--uc-bookmarks-toolbar-position, var(--uc-toolbar-position, 4));`
--uc-bookmarks-toolbar-darken: `rgba(0, 0, 0, var(--uc-bookmarks-toolbar-darken, var(--uc-darken-toolbar, 0)))`
In the config, explain the numbers: "0 = above the tabs/URL bar row, 4 = below it (between the toolbars and notification bars)". Migration note: the old names keep working, and new configs use the new ones.

title: The documented --uc-urlbar-position: 3 does nothing with cascade-responsive-windows-fix.css
problem: The config documents "1 – tabs on the right, 3 – tabs on the left". The windows fix, the alternative layout for Windows users, never reads --uc-urlbar-position: it hard-codes the URL bar on the left with physical margins. Windows users who choose 3 still get the URL bar on the left.
evidence: windows-fix:10-11 `margin: calc(...) calc(100vw - var(--uc-urlbar-min-width)) 0 0 !important;` and :14 `#TabsToolbar { margin-inline-start: var(--uc-urlbar-min-width) !important; }`, with no reference to --uc-urlbar-position. Harness, windows fix with position 3: #nav-bar [0, 4, 490, 40], #TabsToolbar [490, 0, 910, 44], URL bar still on the left. The fix below gives #nav-bar [910, 4, 490, 40] and #TabsToolbar [0, 0, 910, 44]; on focus #nav-bar is [770, 4, 630, 40], growing to the left.

title: Tab Center Reborn stylesheet: dark-only hard-coded palette, dead 'turquoise' selector, no violet/gray
problem: tabcenter-reborn.css runs inside the extension page, so it cannot reach the chrome palette. It hard-codes the default dark palette in a bare :root. In light mode, and with any colour integration, the TCR sidebar stays Cascade-default dark next to a light or themed browser. Its container selectors still use `[data-identity-color="turquoise"]`. Firefox 160 migrates stored containers to 'cyan' and the WebExtension API returns the canonical name, so cyan containers lose their indicator, and violet and gray have none. cascade-tcr.css is indented with 4 spaces while the rest of the repo uses Prettier's 2. It still lists `#sidebar-main`, which does not exist in Firefox 160 (its own comment says it was renamed). It uses physical `margin-left: 50px`.
evidence: tabcenter-reborn.css:1-20 is a bare `:root { --uc-base-colour: #1e2021; ... }` with no prefers-color-scheme. ContextualIdentityService.sys.mjs:93-96 `turquoise: "cyan", toolbar: "gray"`, :1121-1130 migrate5to6 `identity.color = this.resolveContainerColor(identity.color)`. ext-contextualIdentities.js:37-52 returns `color: identity.color`, the canonical name. browser.xhtml has `id="sidebar-container"` but no `sidebar-main`.
fix: Wrap the palette in tabcenter-reborn.css in `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) { :root {...} }` and `@media (prefers-color-scheme: light) { :root {...} }`, and add the comment "paste the palette of your colour scheme here". Once integrations are palette-only, their whole content can be pasted in as-is. Add `[data-identity-color="cyan"], [data-identity-color="turquoise"] { --identity-color: var(--uc-identity-colour-turquoise); }`, `[data-identity-color="violet"] { --identity-color: var(--uc-identity-colour-violet, var(--uc-identity-colour-purple)); }` and `[data-identity-color="gray"] { --identity-color: var(--uc-identity-colour-gray, var(--uc-muted-colour)); }`. In cascade-tcr.css: reformat with Prettier, drop `#sidebar-main`, and use `margin-inline-start`.

title: Wrong or misleading comments in the configs, and no guidance in userChrome.css for the swaps users are expected to make
problem:
Several knob comments are wrong or stale:
- URL bar width: "If enabled the max-width is applied on focus otherwise the URL Bar will always be it's min-width". Nothing can be 'enabled'; it should say to set max equal to min to disable growing. It is also the nav-bar width, not the URL bar's, and only applies in windows of 1000px or more, which is mentioned nowhere.
- "Personal Toolbar" is the bookmarks toolbar.
- "Allow tabs to have dynamic widths" actually sets max-widths.
- "Hide the all Tabs button" has value flex in the mouse config.
- "--uc-identity-glow ... Setting it to 0 disables the Glow": `box-shadow: 0 <color>` is invalid and only 'works' because it computes to unset.
- The mouse config hides the Nova container pill (#userContext-icons) with no matching commented option in the default config.
userChrome.css, the file users must edit to switch to the mouse config, the Windows fix or the TCR/Side View integrations, has no comment explaining any of this. It points mouse users to an external project (Waterfall) even though the repo ships its own mouse config.
evidence: Quoted lines are from cascade-config.css:83-86, :54, :148-150, :187, :200-203, and cascade-config-mouse.css:131-134. cascade-responsive.css:8 `@media (min-width: 1000px)` is the oneline breakpoint; it cannot be a knob because custom properties are not allowed in media queries. Firefox 160 urlbar.css/usercontext.css:198-215 style #userContext-icons as the Nova container pill (icon + name, tinted with --identity-fill-tint).

title: Two configs that are 95% identical drift apart; add a CI knob check, .editorconfig and Prettier config
problem: Every knob has to be added to two files by hand. The latest commit (7407005) exists only because the mouse config had silently lost --uc-show-all-tabs-button, and the configs still differ in knob set (--uc-page-action-margin is mouse-only). There is no CI. The 'style: format with prettier' commit has no checked-in Prettier config, cascade-tcr.css uses 4-space indents, and contributing.md tells contributors to use a `.editorconfig` that does not exist.
evidence: `diff cascade-config.css cascade-config-mouse.css` shows 10 hunks, of which 7 are intended (back/forward, close-on-hover, all tabs, PanelUI hack, userContext, alltabs margin, page action). agents/config/check-knobs.py on HEAD reports the knob-set difference; on HEAD~1 it reports the --uc-show-all-tabs-button drift that 7407005 fixed. `ls -a` at the repo root shows no .editorconfig, .prettierrc or .github/workflows.
fix:
Add .github/workflows/check.yml:
on: [push, pull_request]
jobs:
  check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - run: npx --yes prettier@3 --check "chrome/**/*.css" "integrations/**/*.css"
      - run: python3 .github/scripts/check-knobs.py
The check script (prototype at agents/config/check-knobs.py) asserts that both configs declare the same knobs, that every knob read by an include has a :where default, that all knobs use the --uc- prefix, and, after the palette split, that integrations declare only palette variables. Add .editorconfig (`root = true`, `[*] indent_style = space; indent_size = 2; end_of_line = lf; insert_final_newline = true; charset = utf-8`) and a .prettierrc ({}), so the contributing.md instruction becomes true. Put mouse-only rules in one clearly marked section at the end of cascade-config-mouse.css, so the diff between the two files is easy to review.

title: contributing.md points to a missing .editorconfig, a nonexistent dev branch and the old repo, and has no testing checklist
problem: contributing.md says to send PRs to `dev` (the repo only has `main`) and to use the `.editorconfig` file (missing). It links the licence to andreasgrafen/cascade while the README uses cascadefox. It says nothing about the project's actual conventions: conventional commits; new knobs go in both configs plus a :where default; mapping changes go to all integrations (or, after the split, to the mapping file only). It also gives no test matrix for a userChrome theme.
evidence: `git branch -a` lists only main (plus the CI branch). There is no .editorconfig at the root. contributing.md:27 links `https://github.com/andreasgrafen/cascade/blob/main/LICENSE`, while README.md:22-41 links to cascadefox. The git log uses `fix(tabs): ...` / `feat(nav-bar): ...` throughout.
fix: Replace the guidelines with: PRs go to `main`. Commit messages use conventional commits, short and lowercase (`fix(tabs): …`). A new knob is added to both configs, gets a :where(:root) default in the include that reads it, and uses the --uc- prefix. Test on the current Firefox release with Nova on and off (browser.nova.enabled), compact/normal/touch density, vertical tabs (sidebar.verticalTabs), light and dark, and both configs. Attach before/after screenshots. Run `npx prettier --write`. Fix the licence link to a relative `LICENSE`, and add the .editorconfig the text refers to.

title: README still says the project is stale and unmaintained, and states no supported Firefox version
problem: The first thing visitors see is the old maintainer's "This repo got quite stale ... I've recently switched to another browser" banner, while the theme was just updated for Firefox 159/160 and is actively maintained. Nothing says which Firefox versions are supported, or that Nova is supported. All customisation docs live on an external site, so the documented knobs can drift from the config files. That site (cascadefox.github.io) could not be fetched from this session to check, because its host is not allowed by the session's network settings. The `<div style="display: flex">` badge row is stripped by GitHub, and the Discord badge's alt text is "Repo Size".
evidence: README.md:1-5 (maintainer banner), README.md:32-36 (`alt="Repo Size"` on the Discord shields.io badge), README.md:50 (external docs only). The git log shows active fixes on 2026-11-15/16.
fix: Replace the banner with a status line such as: "Supports Firefox 160 (Nova and Proton). Report breakage with your Firefox version and config". Fix the badge alt text. Add a short 'Configuration' section listing each --uc-* knob, its default and its values, in the same wording as the config comments. Also add a 'Colour schemes' section: "copy integrations/<name>/<file>.css over chrome/includes/cascade-colours.css".

title: Issue and PR templates do not ask for the information a userChrome bug needs
problem: The bug template asks only for a description, expected behaviour and optional screenshots. Almost every Cascade bug depends on the Firefox version, OS, Nova on or off, density, vertical tabs, which config, which responsive file, which colour integration and other userChrome mods, so triage needs a round trip each time. The support template is empty. The PR template has no checklist (both configs updated, :where default added, tested with Nova on and off, screenshots).
evidence: The template contents shown above. Examples of state-dependent behaviour found in this audit: the windows-fix-only urlbar-position bug, the mouse-config-only all-tabs offset, the close-button bug that only appears with one knob combination.
fix: Convert bug_report.md to an issue form (.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.yml) with required fields: Firefox version (about:support), OS, browser.nova.enabled, density, vertical tabs on/off, config (default or mouse), responsive file (default or Windows fix), colour scheme, other userChrome.css changes, screenshot. Add .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/config.yml with `blank_issues_enabled: false` and a contact link to Discussions for support. Add a PR checklist: [ ] both configs, [ ] :where default for new knobs, [ ] tested with Nova on and off and in vertical tabs, [ ] screenshots, [ ] conventional commit title.

title: Duplicated rules and hard-coded values that belong in one place or in a knob
evidence: Quoted lines in the listed files, e.g. cascade-nav-bar.css:40 `transition: opacity 150ms ease;`, cascade-tabs.css:113 `transition: opacity 150ms ease;`, cascade-tabs.css:53 `height: 1px !important;`, cascade-layout.css:83 `padding: 6px !important;`.
fix: Merge cascade-floating-panel.css into cascade-layout.css, but leave the file as a one-line comment stub, because older userChrome.css files still @import it. Remove the duplicate #nav-bar rules from layout.css (nav-bar.css owns them), and the inline fallback in nav-bar.css. Add knobs with :where defaults: `--uc-dim-transition-duration: 150ms` (used in both files, inside `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)`), `--uc-container-line: 1px` (height of .tab-context-line, 0px disables it) and `--uc-bookmarks-toolbar-padding: 6px`. Declare them in both configs.

title: URL bar jumps 20px to the right and only gets 100 of the 140px each time it grows on focus
problem: In the oneline layout (≥1000px, any density, Nova on or off), Firefox's two default flexible spaces stay on both sides of the URL bar. When the URL bar is focused (Ctrl+L, the main action in a keyboard-first theme), #nav-bar grows from 35vw to 45vw. The two springs take part of that new space, so the URL bar's left edge slides 20px to the right during the 200ms animation and the bar gains 100px instead of 140px. At rest the springs also take about 20px. The dropdown follows the shifted bar, so it no longer lines up with where the bar was a moment before.
evidence: Probe of the real FF160 window (1400x800, normal density). At rest: spring1 [77,0,10,44], urlbar-container [92,0,311,44], spring2 [408,0,10,44]. Focused: spring1 [77,0,30,44], urlbar-container [112,0,411,44], spring2 [528,0,30,44]. Compare shots/before/dark.png (URL bar x=92..403) with shots/before/urlbar-focus.png (x=112..523). The springs are part of the default nav-bar markup: browser.xhtml:6419-6424 `<toolbarspring cui-areatype="toolbar" class="chromeclass-toolbar-additional"/>` on either side of #urlbar-container. toolbarbuttons.css:675-681 `#nav-bar &:where(:not(#vertical-spacer)) { flex: 80 80; ... }` with max-width 112px (:673). urlbar.css:717-720 `#urlbar-container { flex: 400 0 auto; }`. Spare space is therefore split 400:80:80, and 140px × 80/560 = 20px per spring, which matches the probe exactly. cascade-responsive.css:24-28 only changes flex-shrink, min-width and width on #urlbar-container, so the springs keep growing. Verified fix (agents/product/after/urlbar-focus.txt): the URL bar stays at x=83 and goes from 329 to 469px wide (+140), and both springs are 1px.

title: Vertical tabs: tab backgrounds flush against the window edge, collapsed icons off-centre, inactive labels cut at 200px
problem: Two horizontal-only rules also apply to native vertical tabs (sidebar.verticalTabs). (1) `.tab-background { margin-inline: 0px !important }` removes Firefox's inline inset. Expanded, the selected/hover background runs from x=0 to the sidebar edge and touches the window border. Collapsed, the 32px background is pushed against the left edge while the favicon stays centred, so the icon sits off-centre in its own highlight. (2) The adaptive tab width rules cap inactive vertical tabs at --uc-inactive-tab-width (200px) and the selected one at 300px. In a 242px sidebar, inactive titles fade out about 40px early and their hover background is narrower than the selected one.
evidence: shots/before/vertical.png: the selected bg spans x=0..242 and titles are truncated ('Cascade — userChron', 'Wikipedia, the free en'). shots/before/vertical-collapsed.png: the selected bg is at x=0..32 while the icon is at 17..33. Probe (agents/product/out-vert.txt): inactive tabs `"tab": [0,40,200,41], "bg": [0,45,200,32], "maxw": "200px", "mi": "0px"`, selected `[0,81,242,41]`. Collapsed: `"bg": [0,45,32,32], "icon": [17,53,16,16]`. Firefox insets vertical tab backgrounds itself at tabs.css:2936-2937 (`#tabbrowser-tabs[orient="vertical"] ... .tab-background { margin-inline: var(--tab-margin-inline-inner); }`) and sizes collapsed ones at tabs.css:2953-2954 (`.tab-background { width: var(--tab-collapsed-background-width); }`). The Cascade rules are cascade-tabs.css:36-41 (max-width, no orient check) and :84 (`margin-inline: 0px !important`). Horizontal tab backgrounds have no inline margin in FF160 anyway (probe: horizontal `mi: 0px` without Cascade's rule). Verified fix: agents/product/after/vertical.png and vertical-collapsed.png (bg inset at 9..233, collapsed icon centred, full titles).

title: Selected result in the URL bar dropdown is nearly invisible (1.25:1), and hover looks the same as selection
problem: Arrow-key navigation through URL bar results is the main keyboard flow, but the selected row is shown only as a slightly darker shade of the dropdown: base #1e2021 on highlight #2e3133 in dark (1.25:1), and #fafafc on #dadadc in light (1.34:1). The default 'Search with …' row is also hard to spot. Hover uses the same colour, so with the mouse resting on the dropdown two rows look selected. The result URLs (accent #786fa6 on #2e3133) are only 2.88:1 at about 11px.
evidence: shots/before/urlbar-open.png and urlbar-open-light.png: the selected 'Search with Google' row is barely darker. Stock (shots/stock/urlbar-open.png) uses a strong highlight. Firefox paints the row from tokens: view-nova.css:171-180 `&[row-selectable]:not([selected]):hover { background-color: var(--urlbarview-background-color-hover) } &[selected] { background-color: var(--urlbarview-background-color-selected) }`. Cascade sets both tokens to the same value (cascade-colours.css:105-106 `--urlbarview-background-color-hover/-selected: var(--uc-urlbar-selection-colour)`) and paints both states again on the inner box (cascade-nav-bar.css:30-36 `.urlbarView-row:hover > .urlbarView-row-inner, .urlbarView-row[selected] > .urlbarView-row-inner { background: var(--uc-urlbar-selection-colour …) }`). Contrast measured from the palette values: 1.25 (dark) and 1.34 (light); URL text 2.88. box-shadow/outline cannot be used for an indicator here because cascade-nav-bar.css:20-24 removes them from `#urlbar *`, and the view is light DOM inside #urlbar (UrlbarInputBase.mjs:228 `<div class="urlbarView"`). Verified fix: agents/product/after/urlbar-open.png and urlbar-open-light.png (the selected row is clearly accent-tinted and hover stays neutral).

title: Tabs are not as tall as the URL bar in touch density or with Nova off (the latest 'every density' fix only holds for normal/compact Nova)
problem: --uc-tab-margin defaults to --tab-margin-block, so the tab background is --tab-min-height tall. That only equals --urlbar-height for normal and compact with Nova on. In touch density, tab backgrounds are 41px next to a 34px URL bar and 34px toolbar buttons. With Nova off they are 36px next to 32px (normal) and 29px next to 26px (compact). In the oneline layout the mismatch sits right next to the URL bar, so it is very visible.
evidence: Probe (agents/product/out-touch.txt): `urlbar [94,10,307,34]`, `reloadIcon [45,10,34,34]`, `selTabBg [669,6,172,41]`. Crops agents/product/crops/touch-top.png and novaoff-top.png (from shots/before/touch.png and nova-off.png) show the taller tab pill. Sources: tabs.css:9 `--tab-min-height: 32px`, :16 compact 28px, :23 touch `--tab-min-height: 41px`, :32 Nova off `--tab-min-height: 36px`, :38 Nova-off compact 29px. urlbar/variables.css:14 `--urlbar-height: max(32px, 1.4em)`, :30 compact 28px, :33 Nova-off compact 26px, :38 touch 34px. tab.tokens.css:77 `--tab-margin-block: 4px` (Proton) / :145 6px (Nova). tabs.css:1077 `.tab-background { min-height: var(--tab-min-height) }`. tabs.css:50 `--tabstrip-min-height: calc(var(--tab-min-height) + 2 * var(--tab-margin-block))`. Cascade: cascade-tabs.css:7 and :83, cascade-config.css:165 (`--uc-tab-margin: var(--tab-margin-block);`), cascade-config-mouse.css:170. Verified fix: touch tab bg [669,10,172,34] = urlbar [87,10,321,34]; Nova off tab bg [669,6,172,32] = urlbar [85,6,327,32]; normal/compact unchanged (6..38 / 4..32); toolbar heights unchanged (44/36/53); split view still 44px tall (agents/product/after/*.txt).

title: Keyboard focus ring on toolbar buttons is dimmed to 65% along with the icon
problem: Firefox draws the toolbar button focus ring on the icon / badge stack. Those are exactly the elements Cascade fades to --uc-inactive-opacity unless the button is hovered, open, checked or disabled. With Tab/Shift+Tab or F6 navigation, the focused button therefore stays dimmed and its ring is drawn at 65% opacity, so keyboard focus is weaker than mouse hover. That runs against Cascade's keyboard-first goal. Tabs reached with keyboard navigation in the tab strip keep their dimmed label in the same way.
evidence: Real keyboard navigation run (agents/product/steps-kbd.json: focus URL bar, Shift+Tab twice): activeElement `sidebar-button`, `:focus-visible` true. The ring pixel is srgb(46,98,160), while the undimmed tab focus ring in shots/before/tab-focus-ring.png is srgb(53,132,228). 0.65×(53,132,228)+0.35×(30,32,33) = (45,97,160), so the ring is at exactly 65% opacity (crop agents/product/crops/kbd-focus.png). Firefox: toolbarbuttons.css:227-235 `&:focus-visible { outline: none; > .toolbarbutton-icon, > .toolbarbutton-text, > .toolbarbutton-badge-stack { outline: var(--focus-outline); ... } }`. Cascade: cascade-nav-bar.css:42-46 `#nav-bar .toolbarbutton-1:not(:hover, [open], [checked], [disabled]) > :is(.toolbarbutton-icon, .toolbarbutton-badge-stack) { opacity: var(--uc-inactive-opacity) !important; }`. Tab keyboard focus: tabs.css:1199 `#tabbrowser-tabs[tablist-has-focus] .tabbrowser-tab.tablist-keyboard-focus > .tab-stack > .tab-background`, versus cascade-tabs.css:115.

title: Firefox's own accent (GTK blue on Linux, Nova violet elsewhere) still shows in focus rings, the loading throbber, attention dots, split view, links and URL selection
problem: Cascade maps --uc-accent-colour only onto the tab line and, inside menupopup/panel, onto --color-accent-primary and --focus-outline-color. Everything that inherits from :root keeps Firefox's accent: the tab keyboard focus ring, focus rings in the sidebar search and findbar, the split view active-pane outline, the tab loading throbber and the attention/title-changed dot (Nova), the bookmarks toolbar 'Manage bookmarks…' link, and the customize-mode 'Done' button. Selected text in the URL bar uses system Highlight blue because Firefox applies --lwt-toolbar-field-highlight only under [lwtheme], which leaves cascade-colours.css:93-94 with no effect on the default/system theme. With catppuccin/rose-pine etc. the result is a two-accent UI.
evidence: Probe with the current Cascade: `--color-accent-primary: AccentColor`, `--focus-outline-color: AccentColor`, `--tab-icon-fill-loading: AccentColor`, `--tab-attention-dot-color: AccentColor`, `--link-color: LinkText` on :root. Screenshots: shots/before/tab-focus-ring.png (blue ring), split.png (blue pane outline), sidebar-bookmarks.png (blue search ring), bookmarks.png (blue link), urlbar-focus.png (blue selection). Sources: tokens-platform.css:33-34 `--color-accent-attention: AccentColor; --color-accent-primary: AccentColor;`. tokens-shared.css:369 `--focus-outline-color: var(--color-accent-primary);` and :428 `--link-color: var(--color-accent-primary);`. tab.tokens.css:13 `--tab-attention-dot-color: var(--color-accent-attention);` and :144 (Nova) `--tab-icon-fill-loading: var(--color-accent-primary);`. urlbar.css:535-539 `:root[lwtheme] { .urlbar-input::selection { background-color: var(--lwt-toolbar-field-highlight, Highlight); ...` All of these are declared on :root in @layer blocks (author origin), so user !important on :root wins. Verified fix: the tokens resolve to #786fa6, the tab focus ring and split outline turn purple, and so do the throbber and attention dot (agents/product/after/tab-focus-ring.png, split.png, attention.png, urlbar-focus.png).

title: Hovered tab looks the same as the selected tab
problem: --tab-background-color-hover and the selected tab background are both --uc-highlight-colour, so a tab under a resting mouse pointer looks selected. Only the 2px accent line tells them apart, and in light mode with the 0.65 dimming it is easy to miss. This hurts most when switching tabs with the keyboard while the pointer happens to be over the tab strip.
evidence: Probe while hovering tab 3 (agents/product/out-hover.txt): `hoverBg: rgb(46, 49, 51)` and `selBg: rgb(46, 49, 51)`. shots/before/hover.png and tab-context-light.png (the right-clicked hovered 'Hacker News' tab matches the selected one). Firefox: tabs.css:1082-1085 `.tabbrowser-tab:hover > .tab-stack > &:not([selected], [multiselected]) { background-color: var(--tab-background-color-hover); }`. Cascade: cascade-colours.css:80 `--tab-background-color-hover: var(--uc-highlight-colour) !important;` and cascade-tabs.css:95-96 (selected = highlight). Verified: agents/product/after/hover.png.
fix:
cascade-colours.css:80:
```css
  --tab-background-color-hover: color-mix(in srgb, var(--uc-highlight-colour) 50%, var(--uc-base-colour)) !important;
```
Toolbar-button hover can stay on --uc-highlight-colour, since buttons have no selected state.

title: Default light palette: the 'muted' colour is darker than body text, so nothing is de-emphasised
problem: In the default light palette --uc-muted-colour is #191b1c, darker than --uc-inverted-colour #1e2021. Everything meant to be secondary shows at full strength: keyboard shortcut hints in the app menu and context menus (--text-color-deemphasized), action text and labels in the URL bar dropdown, URL bar box labels, and the inactive-window text colour. In a keyboard-centred theme the shortcut column then competes with the menu labels. All colour integrations use real greys for muted in light mode, so only the default palette is affected.
evidence: cascade-colours.css:43-44 `--uc-inverted-colour: #1e2021; --uc-muted-colour: #191b1c;`. Contrast on #fafafc: muted 16.58:1 versus text 15.69:1. Uses: cascade-colours.css:66, :100, :109 and cascade-panels.css:30 (`--text-color-deemphasized: var(--uc-muted-colour)`). Crop agents/product/crops/appmenu-light.png (from shots/before/appmenu-light.png): 'Ctrl+T' is as dark as 'New Tab', whereas in shots/before/appmenu.png (dark) the shortcuts are grey. Integrations: catppuccin light muted #9ca0b0, ayu #4d5566, gruvbox #928374 (integrations/*/…css:44). Verified: agents/product/after/light.png.
fix:
cascade-colours.css:44:
```css
    --uc-muted-colour: #5c5c60;
```
(about 6.4:1 on #fafafc and 4.9:1 on the #dadadc URL bar dropdown, so still AA for small text but visibly secondary).

title: Keyboard config: the 1px app menu button turns update/add-on/sync alerts into a stray dot with a 1px click target
problem: The keyboard config shrinks #PanelUI-menu-button to a 1px icon with no padding (keeping it as the anchor for doorhangers). When Firefox needs attention (update available or restart to update, add-on alert, sync sign-in needed), it badges this button. The badge then renders as a floating blue dot next to the extensions icon with no menu icon and a 1px-wide target. Users never see what the dot means and can hardly click it, so updates and add-on permission prompts go unnoticed. The app menu banner that would explain it sits in the panel this button opens.
evidence: cascade-config.css:40-48 (`#PanelUI-menu-button { padding: 0px !important; } … .toolbarbutton-icon { width: 1px !important; }`). Firefox: panelUI-shared.css:65-117 `#PanelUI-menu-button { &[badge-status] > .toolbarbutton-badge-stack > .toolbarbutton-badge { display: flex; ... }` with update-* / addon-alert / fxa-needs-authentication variants, and toolbarbutton-icons.css:171-180 switching to menu-badged.svg. Run with `badge-status="update-available"` set (agents/product/steps-badge.json): current config button rect [482, 9px wide] with an orphan dot (agents/product/crops/badge-kb-before.png). With the fix, [451, 40px] showing a full badged hamburger (crops/badge-kb-after.png).

title: Both configs hide the camera/microphone/screen/location 'in use' indicators in the URL bar
problem: `#identity-permission-box { display: none }` is meant to drop the granted/blocked permission icons. In FF160 that box also holds the live sharing indicators (#webrtc-sharing-icon for camera/microphone/screen, plus geo, xr and serial). With Cascade, a site using your camera or microphone gives no sign in the URL bar, and Firefox's popup/autoplay-blocked icons disappear too. This is a privacy affordance that both stock Firefox and other minimal themes keep.
evidence: browser.xhtml:6498-6510: `<box id="identity-permission-box" …>` contains `<image class="sharing-icon" id="webrtc-sharing-icon"/>`, `geo-sharing-icon`, `xr-sharing-icon`, `serial-sharing-icon` and `#blocked-permissions-container`. browser-sitePermissionPanel.js:355-358 `this._identityPermissionBox.toggleAttribute("hasSharingIcon", hasSharingIcon);` (set while any device is shared). Cascade: cascade-config.css:122-124 and cascade-config-mouse.css:116-118 `#identity-permission-box { display: none !important; }`.

title: New-tab button: hidden even in the mouse config, appears only when horizontal tabs overflow, never in vertical tabs
problem: cascade-tabs.css hides #tabs-newtab-button and #vertical-tabs-newtab-button for everyone, including users of cascade-config-mouse.css. The comment says 'there is also one for overflow', which is only half true. In horizontal mode Firefox shows #new-tab-button only while the strip overflows, so a '+' pops up once you pass about 15 tabs and vanishes again below that. In vertical mode the overflow button is the one Cascade hides, so there is never a new-tab button.
evidence: tabs.css:3159-3166: `#tabbrowser-tabs[hasadjacentnewtabbutton]:not([overflow]) ~ #new-tab-button, … #tabbrowser-tabs[orient="vertical"]:not([overflow]) > #vertical-tabs-newtab-button, #tabbrowser-arrowscrollbox[overflowing] > … > #tabs-newtab-button … { display: none; }`. cascade-tabs.css:129-132 `#vertical-tabs-newtab-button, #tabs-newtab-button { display: none !important; }`. shots/before/dark.png has no '+', shots/before/many-tabs.png shows '+' at x≈1354, and shots/before/vertical.png has no 'New Tab' while stock (shots/stock/vertical.png) shows '+ New Tab'. Probe: all three new-tab buttons computed `display: none` with 5 tabs.

title: Dimming hides the attention/title-changed indicators on background and pinned tabs
problem: Firefox marks a background tab that wants attention (alerts, a pinned mail or chat tab whose title changed) with a dot and a bold label drawn on .tab-content. Cascade fades every non-selected .tab-content to 0.65, so these cues, which only appear on non-selected tabs, are always dimmed and blend in with the quiet tabs.
evidence: tabs.css:1255-1261 `.tabbrowser-tab:is([image], [pinned]) > .tab-stack > .tab-content[attention]:not([selected]), .tabbrowser-tab > .tab-stack > .tab-content[pinned][titlechanged]:not([selected]) … { background-image: radial-gradient(circle, var(--tab-attention-dot-color) …` and tabs.css:1289 `.tab-label[attention]:not([selected]) { font-weight: bold }`. tab.mjs:124-125 shows .tab-content inherits `titlechanged,attention`. Cascade: cascade-tabs.css:115-117. Before/after: agents/product/crops/att-before.png (dimmed blue dot, dimmed bold label) versus att-after.png (full-strength accent dot and label).

title: Menu bar (Alt / F10) squeezes into the oneline row with its items stuck to the top
problem: When the menu bar is shown temporarily (Alt) or permanently, it becomes another item in the flex-wrap row. It pushes the nav-bar 349px to the right and shrinks the tab bar, so the whole row reflows each time Alt is pressed. Its File…Help items are also top-aligned (text centred at y≈12) while every other item in the row is centred at y=22.
evidence: shots/before/menubar.png. Probe (agents/product/out-menubar.txt): `menubar [0,0,349,44]`, `fileMenu [0,1,35,23]`, `navbar [349,0,490,44]`, `tabsToolbar [839,0,561,44]`, `urlbar [440,6,311,32]`. Firefox: browser.css:20-23 `#menubar-items { flex-direction: column; justify-content: normal; /* align the menubar to the top also in customize mode */ }`. browser-shared.css:550-553 gives the autohide menubar `min-height: var(--tabstrip-min-height)`. Cascade only handles the inactive state (cascade-layout.css:36-42). Verified fix: agents/product/crops/menubar-after.png (menu bar on its own row with centred items, oneline row unchanged below it).

title: Light mode: the floating page has no visible edge (white page on a #fafafc frame)
problem: The floating page (gap plus rounded corners) is a signature look, but in light mode most pages are white and the frame is #fafafc (1.04:1), so the gap and the rounded corners disappear. The same goes for the vertical tab sidebar against the page. Panels already get a 1px --uc-panel-border-colour edge, but the page does not.
evidence: shots/before/light.png and vertical-light.png: no visible page boundary. Contrast #ffffff vs #fafafc = 1.04. cascade-layout.css:110-113 only sets border-radius and overflow on `#tabbrowser-tabpanels .browserContainer`. cascade-panels.css:7-14 defines `--uc-panel-border-colour` on :root. Verified: agents/product/after/light.png (hairline frame, invisible in dark mode where the gap already shows).

title: Mouse config: the hover close button shrinks the tab title and moves its fade point
problem: With --show-tab-close-button-hover: flex, the close button switches from display:none to flex on hover. That takes 13px from the label, so the title's cut-off point jumps as the pointer moves across tabs (layout shift on every hover).
evidence: Probe with cascade-config-mouse.css (agents/product/steps-mouse.json): label container [1014, 137px] at rest and [1014, 124px] while hovered, close [1138, 20px]. Firefox: tabs.css:13 `--tab-content-button-size: 20px` and tabs.css:1020 `margin-inline-end: calc(var(--tab-padding-inline) / -2)`, which gives 20 − 7 = 13px. Cascade: cascade-tabs.css:31-33. With the fix the label stays at 137px and the × sits over the label's faded end (agents/product/crops/mouse-hover.png vs mouse-hover-after.png).

title: The mouse-friendly config still removes the window controls
problem: cascade-config-mouse.css is offered as the mouse-friendly setup but still hides .titlebar-buttonbox-container. With tabs in the titlebar (the default on Windows, macOS and GNOME CSD) there is then no minimise/maximise/close by mouse. In the oneline layout the controls already sit sensibly at the end of the tab bar (order:1000), or at its start on macOS.
evidence: cascade-config-mouse.css:38-40 `.titlebar-buttonbox-container { display: none !important; }` (identical to cascade-config.css:32-34). Firefox places the box inside #TabsToolbar (browser.xhtml:6351) and orders it last: browser-shared.css:403-404 `.titlebar-buttonbox-container { order: 1000;`, or first on macOS (:406-410 `order: -1`). It is hidden automatically where it isn't needed (:423-425 `:root:not([customtitlebar], [inFullscreen]) & { display: none; }`).

title: Nova's 24px pill buttons and fields clash with Cascade's 8px radius everywhere else
problem: Cascade unifies tabs, URL bar, page, panels and menus on --uc-border-radius (8px), but Nova makes every button and the find field a full pill. Notification bar buttons ('Set as default'), customize-mode buttons, panel footer buttons and the find-in-page field all show 24px pills next to 8px boxes. Cascade only fixes this inside the URL bar.
evidence: Probe: `--button-border-radius: 24px` on :root (tokens-shared.css:826 Nova `--button-border-radius: var(--border-radius-xlarge);`, :785 `--border-radius-xlarge: 24px`). Consumers: moz-button.css:114 `border-radius: var(--button-border-radius);`, global-shared.css:169, panelUI-shared.css:250. findbar.css:88 `.findbar-textbox { … border-radius: var(--border-radius-xlarge);`. Screenshots: shots/before/notification.png ('Set as default' pill), customize.png (Toolbars/Done/Restore Defaults pills), findbar.png (pill field). Cascade only overrides it in #urlbar (cascade-layout.css:32-34).

title: Private windows look identical to normal ones
problem: Cascade forces the toolbox, toolbar, field and tab colours with !important, so a private window has exactly the same chrome as a normal one. The only cue left is Nova's small indicator icon at the end of the tab strip (or the label with Nova off). Users of minimal themes often run normal and private windows side by side and rely on a glanceable distinction.
evidence: content-area.css:15-24 (`&[privatebrowsingmode="temporary"] { --tabpanel-background-color: … }`) and browser-shared.css:841-895 (indicator button/label shown only for `:root[privatebrowsingmode="temporary"]`). Cascade: cascade-colours.css:61-115 maps every toolbar colour unconditionally. shots/before/private.png matches shots/before/dark.png apart from the icons (that run uses autostart, i.e. privatebrowsingmode="permanent", where Firefox shows no indicator at all).

title: Tooltips (which carry the keyboard shortcuts) are native black boxes outside the palette
problem: Toolbar tooltips such as 'Reload current page (Ctrl+R)' are where Firefox teaches shortcuts, which matters for a keyboard-centred theme. They still use the native or system tooltip look (black box with white text on Linux; Firefox's own grey on Windows), while every panel, menu and the tab preview follow the palette.
evidence: shots/before/hover-button.png (black square tooltip). xul.css:351-363 (UA sheet) `tooltip { appearance: auto; -moz-default-appearance: tooltip; … background-color: InfoBackground; color: InfoText; …`, with platform tweaks at :376-399. Since xul.css is UA origin, a user-origin rule wins.

title: Motion: the dimming fades ignore prefers-reduced-motion, and hover backgrounds snap while content fades
problem: The URL bar grow animation is correctly wrapped in prefers-reduced-motion, but the 150ms opacity transitions on tab content and toolbar icons are not. They also run alone: the tab or button background changes instantly while the label or icon fades in over 150ms, so hover feels slightly out of sync.
evidence: cascade-responsive.css:56-61 wraps the width transition in `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)`. cascade-tabs.css:112-114 `.tab-content { transition: opacity 150ms ease; }` and cascade-nav-bar.css:39-41 have no such guard. Probe: `.tab-background` computed transition `all` (i.e. none) versus `.tab-content` `opacity 0.15s`.

title: cascade-tcr.css hides the panel header of every sidebar, not just Tab Center Reborn's
problem: Lines 64-67 hide `#sidebar-panel-header` for all sidebars, and the rule applies even while TCR is closed. In Firefox 160 (sidebar.revamp is on by default) this element is the only header the built-in panels have: it holds the title, the panel switcher dropdown (the only way to switch panels in `hide-launcher` mode) and the close button. Anyone who has installed the TCR integration loses these on Bookmarks, History, Synced Tabs, the AI chatbot and other extensions' sidebars. Those panels can then only be closed with Ctrl+B or the toolbar button.
evidence:
Cascade: cascade-tcr.css:64-67 `/* hide panel title */ #sidebar-panel-header { display: none !important; }`. This rule sits outside the `#main-window:has(...)` block, so nothing scopes it.
Firefox 160: browser.xhtml:7048 `<html:sidebar-panel-header id="sidebar-panel-header"/>` (one element shared by every panel). browser-sidebar.js:599-602: "Revamp panels each provide their own header (the sidebar-panel-header Lit element), including the \"hide-launcher\" panel switcher dropdown, so the shared chrome-level header stays hidden." followed by `document.getElementById("sidebar-header").hidden = true;`. sidebar-panel-header.mjs:79-91 renders `<h4 class="sidebar-panel-title">`, `<sidebar-panel-switcher>` and a close `<moz-button ... @click=${this.closeSidebarPanel}>`. sidebar-panel-header.css:24-31: in `-moz-pref("sidebar.visibility", "hide-launcher")` the title gives way to the switcher. firefox.js:869 `pref("sidebar.revamp", true)`.
Harness test (real FF160 with a stand-in extension using id tabcenter-reborn@ariasuni, so the command is `tabcenter-reborn_ariasuni-sidebar-action`, see ext-sidebarAction.js:40-41 and ext-browser.js:98-102): open TCR, then `SidebarController.show('viewBookmarksSidebar')`. `#sidebar-panel-header` computes to `display: none`. Screenshot agents/extensions/shots/tcr-then-bookmarks.png has no "Bookmarks ×" header; harness/shots/before/sidebar-bookmarks.png (without the integration) does. With the scoped fix it computes to `display: block` and the header is back.

title: TCR with cascade-responsive-windows-fix.css pulls the whole toolbar off-screen
problem: Windows users who swap in cascade-responsive-windows-fix.css and enable the TCR integration lose the URL bar and all toolbar buttons at window widths of 1000px or more. The Windows fix pulls #nav-bar up into the tab row with a negative top margin. TCR hides #TabsToolbar but leaves that margin, so the nav bar moves above the window top and the toolbox ends up 0px tall. This also happens while the URL bar is focused.
evidence:
cascade-responsive-windows-fix.css:9-12 `#nav-bar { margin: calc((var(--urlbar-height) + 2 * var(--urlbar-padding-block)) * -1) calc(100vw - var(--uc-urlbar-min-width)) 0 0 !important; }`, plus the focused variant at :17-20 (specificity 3,1,0). cascade-tcr.css:4-11 only sets `#TabsToolbar { display: none !important; }` and `#nav-bar { width: 100vw !important; }`. Nothing resets the margin.
Harness (1400x800, Windows-fix chrome, TCR open): `#nav-bar` rect [0,-40,1400,40], margin-top -40px, margin-right 910px; `#navigator-toolbox` height 0px. Screenshot agents/extensions/shots/tcrwin-open.png shows no toolbar at all.
The reset has to beat the focused variant at (3,1,0). A `#main-window`-anchored selector does that: `#main-window:not([inDOMFullscreen]):has(> body > #browser > #sidebar-box[...]:not([hidden])) #nav-bar` is (4,3,1). A `:root`-anchored one would lose while the URL bar is focused. Verified with the fix: #nav-bar is [0,0,1400,40] with margin 0, both idle and after gURLBar.focus().

title: Side View: the forced legacy header has a dead close button and doubles up with the revamp header
problem: With Firefox 160 defaults (sidebar.revamp on), Firefox hides the old #sidebar-header and never connects its close button. cascade-sideview.css forces that header back with `display: flex !important`. The result is a full-width "×" strip that does nothing when clicked, stacked above the revamped panel header, which has its own working close button. The integration's `border: none` also has no effect because it lacks !important.
evidence:
cascade-sideview.css:11-20 `#sidebar-box[sidebarcommand*="side-view"] #sidebar-header { display: flex !important; ... border: none; }`. A user `!important` declaration beats Firefox's author `!important` rule at global-shared.css:118-120 `:where([hidden]) { display: none !important; }`, so the hidden header reappears.
browser-sidebar.js:602 `document.getElementById("sidebar-header").hidden = true;` (revamp branch). The listener at :628-633 `this._switcherCloseButton = document.getElementById("sidebar-close"); ... addEventListener("command", () => { this.hide(); })` is only added in the `else` (non-revamp) branch. sidebar.css:57-61 `#sidebar-header { ... border-bottom: 1px solid var(--sidebar-border-color); }` is an author declaration, so the non-important `border: none` loses to it.
Harness with a stand-in extension using id side-view@mozilla.org (command `side-view_mozilla_org-sidebar-action`; the `*="side-view"` selector still matches): #sidebar-header has hidden=true but computes to display:flex. #sidebar-close is 333x20 and sits above the 72px #sidebar-panel-header (agents/extensions/shots/sv-open.png). After clicking it, `SidebarController.isOpen` is still true. With sidebar.revamp=false the same click closes the sidebar.

title: Firefox's inline 7px gutter takes 14% of the 50px TCR strip
problem: When a panel is open with no launcher next to it (horizontal tabs, the default), Firefox 160 sets an inline `padding-inline-start: var(--space-small)` on #sidebar-box. cascade-tcr.css only resets padding-bottom. The TCR page therefore gets 43px of the 50px strip, and a 7px band in the toolbar colour runs down the window edge next to it.
evidence:
SidebarState.sys.mjs:590-593 `#updatePanelPadding() { this.#sidebarBoxEl.style.paddingInlineStart = this.panelOpen && !this.launcherVisible ? "var(--space-small)" : "unset"; }`. `InspectorUtils.getMatchingCSSRules(#sidebar-box)` lists an inline style with `padding-inline-start: var(--space-small); order: 3;`. cascade-tcr.css:37 only has `padding-bottom: 0px !important`.
Harness: #sidebar-box padding-left is 6.667px; the box is at x=0, w=50 but `#sidebar` is at x=7, w=43.33 (agents/extensions/shots/tcr-open.png, dark band on the left). The same happens with sidebar.revamp=false and with browser.nova.enabled=false. The inline style is not !important, so a user `!important` rule wins. With the fix, `#sidebar` is [0,40,50,760].

title: TCR ignores "Move sidebar to right" and lays out wrongly in RTL
problem: The overlay has top and bottom insets but no inline inset, so it sits at its static position. The room for it is reserved with a physical `margin-left: 50px`. With sidebar.position_start=false, TCR still appears on the left. In RTL, the static position is inline-start (the right), but the margin is still reserved on the left, so the strip covers 50px of the page and leaves an empty 50px gutter on the other side.
evidence:
cascade-tcr.css:16-18 `#tabbrowser-tabbox { margin-left: 50px !important; }` and :28-30 `position: absolute !important; top: 0; bottom: 0;` (no left, right or inset-inline). Firefox moves the sidebar to the right by changing `style.order` on #browser's children and toggling `sidebar-positionend` on :root, #sidebar-box, #tabbrowser-tabbox and #sidebar-container (browser-sidebar.js:1016-1047). `order` has no effect on an absolutely positioned box.
Harness with sidebar.position_start=false: #sidebar-box is at [0,40,50,760] and the tabbox margin-left is 50px, so TCR stays on the left. With the fix: box at [1350,40,50,760], expanding to [1150,40,250,760] on hover, and tabbox margin-right 50px. The RTL behaviour follows from the same static-position rule; it was not run in the harness.

title: TCR palette in tabcenter-reborn.css is hard-coded dark; no light scheme, no text colour, ignores colour integrations
problem: tabcenter-reborn.css contains one `:root` block with Cascade's default dark values. When the browser follows a light system theme, Cascade's chrome turns light (#fafafc) but the TCR strip stays #1e2021. The file sets backgrounds only, never a text colour, so TCR's own light-theme text ends up dark on dark. Users of catppuccin, rose-pine, nord, gruvbox or ayu also get the default dark palette in TCR unless they edit it by hand. `--uc-inverted-colour`, `--uc-muted-colour` and `--uc-accent-colour` are defined but never used.
evidence:
tabcenter-reborn.css:1-20 has a single unconditional `:root { --uc-base-colour: #1e2021; --uc-highlight-colour: #2e3133; ... }`, a copy of cascade-colours.css:5-25. cascade-colours.css:27-47 has the light block, which has no counterpart here. Only `background` is set (:26-34), and no `color` appears anywhere in the file.
Harness with ui.systemUsesDarkTheme=0: the chrome is light and the TCR strip dark (agents/extensions/shots/crop-tcrlight-hover.png). The extension page is a moz-extension document whose `prefers-color-scheme` follows the browser theme. With the palette inside media queries, the strip turns light under the same settings (agents/extensions/shots/crop-tcrlightfix-hover.png).

title: With sidebar.revamp off, the legacy sidebar header is squeezed into the TCR strip and the page overflows
problem: Users who turned sidebar.revamp off get Firefox's legacy #sidebar-header ("Tab Center Reborn ▾ ×") at the top of the 50px strip. The integration also sets `display: block` and gives the browser stack `height: 100%`. The 44px header therefore pushes the TCR page down, and its bottom 44px is clipped.
evidence:
browser-sidebar.js:1077-1080: when revamp is off, `document.getElementById("sidebar-header").hidden = false;`. cascade-tcr.css only hides the revamp `#sidebar-panel-header` (:65). It also sets `display: block;` (:26) and `.sidebar-browser-stack { height: 100%; }` (:49-51).
Harness with sidebar.revamp=false: #sidebar-header is displayed at [7,40,43,44] and `#sidebar` at [7,84,43,760], so it runs to y=844 in an 800px window. Screenshot agents/extensions/shots/crop-tcrnorevamp-hover.png shows the squeezed title and switcher. Firefox already makes the stack fill the vbox: content-area.css:398-400 `.sidebar-browser-stack { flex: 1; }`. The block/height hack is therefore unnecessary. With the fix, the header computes to display:none and `#sidebar` is [0,40,50,760].

title: Fullscreen override works but is redundant and its comment is misleading
problem: The behaviour is correct, verified in both modes. In F11 the TCR strip stays visible and keeps its 50px of room. In DOM fullscreen (video) the margin is removed. However, `[inFullscreen][inDOMFullscreen]` behaves the same as `[inDOMFullscreen]`, and the comment "needed to increase specificity" is inaccurate. The override exists because Firefox hides the sidebar in DOM fullscreen with `visibility: collapse` rather than the `hidden` attribute, so the main rule's `:has(...:not([hidden]))` keeps matching. A separate override with a high-specificity selector is fragile; the condition belongs in the main rule.
evidence:
cascade-tcr.css:69-76 `#main-window[inFullscreen][inDOMFullscreen]:has(#sidebar-box[sidebarcommand*="tabcenter"]:not([hidden])) #browser #tabbrowser-tabbox { margin-left: 0px !important; }`.
browser-fullScreenAndPointerLock.js:406-411 and :442 toggle `inFullscreen` whenever the window is fullscreen. That covers F11 and DOM fullscreen, because DOM fullscreen also makes the window fullscreen. :664 sets `inDOMFullscreen` for DOM fullscreen only. fullscreen-and-pointerlock.css:5-13 `:root[inDOMFullscreen] #sidebar-box, ... { visibility: collapse; }` collapses the box only in DOM fullscreen, never in F11.
Specificity: the main rule is (4,2,0) and the override (4,4,0); with only `[inDOMFullscreen]` it would be (4,3,0), which still wins.
