Harness: with only `inFullscreen`, the tabbox margin-left is 50px and the box is visible. Adding `inDOMFullscreen` and `fullscreenNavToolboxHidden` gives margin 0 and a collapsed box.

title: TCR overlay: hard-coded widths, `transition: all`, no reduced-motion guard, no hover delay, width depends on the sidebar's saved width
problem: 50px and 250px are hard-coded, which breaks the convention that every knob is a `--uc-*` property. `transition: all 0.2s ease` runs regardless of prefers-reduced-motion, which Cascade guards everywhere else. The strip expands the moment the pointer crosses it (for example on the way to the window edge), while Firefox's own expand-on-hover waits 200ms. The expanded width is only a max-width clamp on Firefox's width (340px, or whatever width the user last dragged the splitter to), so a user who once made the sidebar narrower than 250px only gets that narrower width on hover.
evidence:
cascade-tcr.css:17 `margin-left: 50px`, :32 `transition: all 0.2s ease;`, :35-36 `min-width: 50px !important; max-width: 50px !important;`, :39-41 `&:hover { max-width: 250px !important; }`. cascade-responsive.css:56-61 wraps its transition in `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)`. firefox.js:871-872 `sidebar.animation.expand-on-hover.duration-ms` 200 and `...delay-duration-ms` 200. sidebar.css:17-19 `@media -moz-pref("sidebar.revamp") { ... width: 340px; }`; the splitter writes an inline width.
Harness with the fix: the computed transition is `max-width 0.2s` at rest and `max-width 0.2s 0.15s` while hovered, and the box goes from [0,40,50,760] to [0,40,250,760].

title: Dead and redundant selectors in cascade-tcr.css, and an unscoped :has() over the whole window
problem: Several rules no longer do anything in Firefox 160, and one comment is wrong. The window-level `:has()` searches all descendants of the window. Firefox re-evaluates it whenever a `hidden` or `sidebarcommand` attribute changes, and `hidden` changes constantly in the browser chrome. A child-combinator path is cheaper and states the intent.
evidence: `#sidebar-main` (:58): no element has this id in Firefox 160. browser.xhtml:7031-7035 is `<box ... id="sidebar-container"><html:sidebar-main flex="1">`, a custom element with no id, so the comment at :54-55 ("#sidebar-main was renamed to #sidebar-container") is wrong. `#browser { position: relative !important; }` (:13-14) duplicates content-area.css:179-181 `#browser { position: relative; }`. `display: block` (:26) and `.sidebar-browser-stack { height: 100% }` (:49-51) only work around each other; content-area.css:398-400 already gives the stack `flex: 1`. The harness confirmed that #browser's parent is body and body's parent is html, so `:has(> body > #browser > #sidebar-box...)` is valid.
fix:
Remove `#sidebar-main`, the `#browser` position rule, `display: block` and the stack height rule. Anchor the block as `#main-window:not([inDOMFullscreen]):has(> body > #browser > #sidebar-box[sidebarcommand*="tabcenter"]:not([hidden]))`, and hide the launcher and splitters with !important:
```css
#sidebar-container,
#sidebar-launcher-splitter,
#sidebar-splitter { display: none !important; }
```
The full rewrite was verified with default settings, Nova off, vertical tabs, the sidebar on the right, sidebar.revamp off and the Windows fix: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-cascade/48698eae-20a7-558b-9a00-57da38f74033/scratchpad/agents/extensions/fix/cascade-tcr.css

title: TCR integration is mouse-only; :focus-within cannot expand the strip
problem: Cascade calls itself keyboard centered, but the TCR strip expands, and tab titles appear, only on mouse hover. A keyboard user who focuses the sidebar sees a 50px column of favicons. Chrome CSS cannot fix this: the extension page is a separate document, so #sidebar-box never matches :focus-within. Inside the page, `body:hover` also depends on body filling the viewport.
evidence: Harness: after `SidebarController.browser.focus()`, `document.activeElement` is #sidebar, but `#sidebar:focus` and `#sidebar-box:focus-within` are both false and max-width stays 50px. The #sidebar browser loads chrome://browser/content/webext-panels.xhtml, which nests the remote `#webext-panels-browser` (webext-panels.js:20,34). tabcenter-reborn.css:36-49 hides `.tab-title-wrapper` (opacity 0, translateX(-10px)) unless `body:hover`, with no reduced-motion guard. In the test page, the extension received mousemove events but `body:hover` stayed false whenever the pointer was below the body's content height.

title: TCR page: hovered and active tabs look the same, no accent, close buttons hidden even for the mouse config
problem: Hovered and active tabs get the same background, so while the pointer is over the list (the only time titles are visible) the current tab cannot be picked out. The chrome tab bar marks the active tab with an accent line; the TCR page has nothing equivalent, and `--uc-accent-colour` is defined but unused. `.tab-close` is always hidden, even for users of cascade-config-mouse.css, which shows close buttons on hover in the tab bar. Firefox's 'toolbar' container colour has no mapping.
evidence: tabcenter-reborn.css:31-34 `.tab:hover, .tab.active { background: var(--uc-highlight-colour); }` and :84-88 `.tab-close { display: none; }`. cascade-tabs.css:98-106 draws the accent line on the selected horizontal tab. tabcenter-reborn.css:94-117 maps blue to purple only. The DOM names (`.tab.active`, `.tab-close`, `[data-identity-color]`) are taken from the existing file and from knowledge of TCR; TCR's source could not be fetched in this session.

title: Integrations lack install notes; Side View is superseded by native split view
problem: None of the integration files say how to install them. For example, cascade-tcr.css has to be @imported after the other includes, and tabcenter-reborn.css has to be pasted into TCR's own custom stylesheet setting, not into userChrome. Nor do they say which Firefox sidebar mode they were tested with. The README only links to the external site. Side View is a 2018 Test Pilot add-on that has not been updated in years, and Firefox 160 has native split view, which Cascade already styles. Tab Center Reborn overlaps Firefox's native vertical tabs in the same way.
evidence: Firefox 160 has tabbrowser/tabsplitview.mjs and `gBrowser.addTabSplitView` (used by the harness 'split' scenario). Cascade already handles split view in cascade-layout.css:101-108 and cascade-tabs.css:88-91. firefox.js:869 `sidebar.revamp` true and :875 `sidebar.verticalTabs` false: native vertical tabs are one setting away. README.md:50 only links to cascadefox.github.io/integrations.html.
fix: Start each integration file with a short header comment: where it goes (`chrome/includes/` plus `@import "includes/cascade-tcr.css";` as the last import in userChrome.css, or TCR settings > custom stylesheet for tabcenter-reborn.css), which knobs it reads, and that it was tested with Firefox 160 revamped and legacy sidebars. Mark integrations/side-view as deprecated in favour of native split view, and suggest native vertical tabs on the integrations page as the maintained alternative to TCR.
